News.title: Is it going to snow in the UK this week? Met Office issues a yellow weather warning
News.content:
SLEET DREAMS Is it going to snow in the UK this week? Met Office issues a yellow weather warning







Next

TEMPERATURES have taken a sharp dip across the UK as a cold snap takes hold at the start of the week.

With a band of wet and windy weather moving in, the Met Office has issued a yellow weather warning covering large parts of the country.



It follows an icy start to Monday morning across northern regions, opening the possibility of November snow disruption.

Here’s everything you need to know about the latest forecast and what to expect over the coming days.



Will it snow in the UK this week?

Yes, snow is expected in some parts of the UK this week.

But any significant snowfall is expected to be confined to higher ground rather than towns and cities at lower levels, instead of a widespread blanketing of snow.

A band of rain is forecast to push northwards across the country through Monday night and into Tuesday morning, turning to snow where it meets colder air.

Upland parts of Mid and North Wales are likely to see freezing rain or snow first on Monday evening.

Met Office meteorologist Aidan McGivern said significant snow is expected above 300 metres in northern England and above 150 to 200 metres in southern Scotland during the early hours of Tuesday.

In these areas, expect depths of 1cm to 5cm, while higher ground above 300 to 400 metres could see between 5cm and 15cm.



Strong wind gusts of 50mph to 60mph will also accompany the system across upland parts of northern England and southern Scotland.

This combination brings a risk of drifting snow, blizzards on high routes and ice build-up on infrastructure like power lines, which could trigger travel delays and isolated power cuts.

For lower levels, however, any brief snow should quickly turn back to rain, and any settled snow will melt quickly, according to the Met Office.

McGivern says: “For where most people live, it will mostly be wet weather rather than wintry weather.”

Where is the snow warning in place?

The Met Office has issued a yellow weather warning for snow across a large part of the UK, stretching from the West Midlands to southern Scotland, including higher routes across the Peak District, Pennines and Southern Uplands.



The warning covers 18 areas across England and Scotland. The affected areas are:

Blackburn with Darwen

Cheshire East

Cumbria

Derbyshire

Dumfries and Galloway

Durham

East Ayrshire

Greater Manchester

Lancashire

Midlothian

North Yorkshire

Northumberland

Scottish Borders

South Ayrshire

South Lanarkshire

South Yorkshire

Staffordshire

West Yorkshire

The 12-hour warning is in place from midnight until 11am on Tuesday, November 17.

What about the cold-health alert and the rest of the week?

The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has also issued a yellow cold-health alert for the North West, North East and Yorkshire and the Humber.

These alerts have been in place from 9pm on Sunday, November 15, and will remain until 9am on Thursday, November 19.

The UKHSA said these alerts mean weather conditions could result in an increased use of healthcare services and a greater risk to life for vulnerable people.



No further Met Office weather warnings are currently in force.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Midweek will bring a changeable mix of sunny intervals and scattered, occasionally heavy showers, with colder air pushing southwards again later in the working week to bring widespread overnight frosts.

By the weekend, conditions are forecast to turn less cold but more unsettled as rain moves in from the west, with any further hill snow likely limited to north-west Scotland.

News.title: Married teacher, 32, admits having sex with boy, 16, & sending him naked photos after ‘inviting him to locker room’
News.content:
Next

A MARRIED school football coach has confessed to having sex with her 16-year-old student.

Mary “Hanna” Mattingly, 32, sobbed in court as she pleaded guilty to sexual abuse charges after she was caught exchanging nude photos with her teenage pupil.





The married substitute teacher is expected to be locked up for five years after agreeing to a plea deal on Friday, WKYT reports.

Mattingly was arrested in after her Bardstown, Kentucky, school received an anonymous letter detailing her sickening crimes of “inappropriate contact”.

She was swiftly sacked from her role with the school immediately alerting authorities in 2025.

It is understood the disgraced coach engineered a relationship with her teenage student after she asked for his help cleaning the sports locker room.

The pair began then speaking on Snapchat, according to the student, before she began having sex with the student between March 1 and July 31, 2025, cops say.

Detective Eric Williamson said: “This investigation came from an anonymous tip, so if someone in the community knows something that’s going on, let us know.





“We can’t do anything about it if you don’t tell us. We’re here to support victims.

“We’re going to support you, listen to you, and walk beside you to do anything we can to bring you any form of justice in your case.”

Mattingly is set to be sentenced on January 21 where she is expected to receive a five-year prison sentence.

The scandal caused a stir in Bardstown, a small city of just 13,500 people roughly 40 miles south of Louisville.

It comes as a disgraced drama teacher has been jailed in Australia after she confessed to a sickening relationship with her teen student.

Ella Clements, 25, collapsed in shock when she was cuffed on school grounds after a string of alleged incidents against her 15-year-old male student came to light last year.

Clements, who worked at St Augustine’s Catholic School for Boys in Sydney, Australia, was recently locked up after taking a plea deal.

The bargain came after four of her charges were dropped in return for her pleading guilty to the more serious charge of maintaining an unlawful relationship with a child, the Mail reported.

She was hauled from court in handcuffs and now faces a maximum of life in prison.

In another shocking instance of abuse, a special education teacher reportedly booked hotels for a teen student before having sex with him.



Ann Margaret Bacon, 27, was sentenced to six month in jail at the end of last month.

The disgraced teacher reportedly first claimed that she didn’t start having sex with the pupil until a month after he left Tartan High School in Oakdale, Minneapolis.

But Bacon confessed and changed her story after cops showed her photos of her and her victim at a hotel together dated from while he was still attending her school, according to Pioneer Press.

Bacon pleaded guilty to third-degree criminal sexual conduct involving a prohibited occupational relationship.

News.title: Fears smuggler ‘motherships’ are towing migrants to tiny Canary Island as thousands sleep on dock after record surge
News.content:
Next

FEARS are growing that smuggler “motherships” may be towing thousands of migrants towards a popular Canary Island left on the edge of collapse by an unprecedented surge in arrivals.

Spanish authorities have declared a state of emergency after the tiny island of El Hierro was flooded by more than 12,000 migrants in just weeks – more than its entire permanent population.



Some 1,580 people were rescued at sea on Saturday alone – smashing the previous record for single-day arrivals in the Canaries and sparking fears of another Ceuta-style crisis.

In total, more than 3,900 men, women and children arrived over the weekend aboard 23 overcrowded wooden boats, pushing emergency services and local reception centres to breaking point.



Thousands of migrants have been forced to sleep rough on the docks amid growing local unrest, with local ambulances, hospitals and Red Cross teams operating beyond capacity.

Others are being urgently transferred to neighbouring islands, including Tenerife, where an old reception facility is being reopened in La Laguna to ease the mounting pressure.



Serious questions are also being raised over how so many tiny, fragile wooden boats – known as “cayucos” – are managing to survive the treacherous Atlantic crossing from west Africa.

Politicians and locals fear organised smuggling gangs are deploying large “motherships” to tow the smaller vessels across the open ocean – or carry migrants for hours before releasing them onto the ramshackle boats just miles from the Canaries.



The explosive theory has triggered urgent demands for the Spanish Navy to be called in to patrol the waters off El Hierro and intercept the alleged smuggling vessels.

Xavier Garcia Albiol, a senior politician with the opposition People’s Party (PP), is among those demanding immediate naval intervention.

While there is currently no evidence proving motherships are operating on the Atlantic route, a similar tactic was uncovered by Italian authorities near Lampedusa in the central Mediterranean back in June 2019.



Many of those rescued off El Hierro arrived suffering from severe hydration, hypothermia and skin abrasions after spending weeks at sea.

The majority of arrivals set off from countries in Africa including Mauritania, Senegal and Gambia.

Canary Islands president Fernando Clavijo has slammed Madrid’s response to the crisis, warning that the wave of arrivals is overwhelming the regional health service.

He has demanded increased patrols off the coasts of Senegal and Gambia as well as the deployment of EU border agency Frontex to stop boats setting off in the first place.

Clavijo also accused the Spanish government of failing to honour promises of financial aid and extra medical staff, warning: “The Spanish government is not honouring the agreement it reaches and this is generating widespread frustration among the population.”



He previously said: “We need more personnel, more resources for healthcare and emergency response, and swift transfers to ease the pressure on the island and its professionals.”

However, he rejected calls to use the army to intercept boats at sea, arguing soldiers would simply end up acting as “lifeguards” and bringing the migrants ashore anyway.

Territorial policy minister Angel Víctor Torres visited the fishing port of La Restinga on Sunday, where the surge in arrivals since mid-October has triggered protests from furious locals worried about safety and damage to the island’s tourist image.

Just 3,708 people reached the picturesque islands between January and June, according to interior ministry figures.

But more than 6,000 people arrived in October alone, followed by around 11,000 migrants in the first half of November.



In total, around 17,000 people have reached El Hierro so far this year – with around 27,000 making it to the Canary Islands as a whole.

The months after the summer are typically the busiest of the year, when hostile trade winds ease and the crossing becomes more navigable.

However, the crossing between the west African coast and the Canaries remains one of the world’s most dangerous migration routes.

El Hierro is the second smallest of the Canary Islands – an idyllic tourist favourite boasting volcanic landscapes, hiking trails and historic towns.

The island receives around 30,000 tourists per year, making it the least-visited of the main Canary Islands.



The migration emergency comes just two weeks before Spanish voters head to the polls for a snap general election.

Left-wing PM Pedro Sanchez – who offered amnesty to around one million illegal migrants earlier this year – could be replaced by a right-wing coalition, according to polls.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The surge also comes as the enclave of Ceuta continues to grapple with its migration crisis after more than 80,000 migrants stormed its borders in July.

Many migrants, including unaccompanied minors, remain sleeping in the streets despite local efforts to shelter, register and deport people back to Morocco.

News.title: James Cleverly accuses Sadiq Khan of surrending police powers and pledges to seize back control if elected London Mayor
News.content:
Next

JAMES Cleverly is promising to take back control of the London Mayor’s policing powers if he is elected to City Hall.

The Tory hopeful claims Sadiq Khan has “deliberately” given up key powers over the Metropolitan Police Service during his decade in power.



He accused Lord Khan of delegating important jobs to his deputy like approving the budget and holding Scotland Yard to account.

Sir James, former home secretary, said he will take responsibility for keeping Londoners safe.



He told The Sun: “I’d assumed Sadiq Khan had lost control of policing in London. It turns out he gave it away deliberately.

“Londoners expect their Mayor to take responsibility for keeping them safe. Instead, Sadiq has handed every mayoral policing power the law allows to a deputy.

“Keeping London safe will be my number one priority. If we can’t get that right, nothing else the Mayor does will matter.

“So I will not delegate my top priority. As Mayor, I will develop and set the Met’s priorities from the top, review and sign off its budget and hold it to account myself. Londoners will know exactly who to hold accountable: me.”

Sir James pointed to Home Office data that shows crime in London has risen by a fifth, while shoplifting and phone theft more than doubled under Lord Khan.

Meanwhile, 58 per cent of Londoners think crime has gotten worse, according to a YouGov poll.



And trust in the Met dropped from 86 per cent to 69 per cent on Khan’s watch, according to the Mayor’s Office for Policing and Crime public attitudes survey.

Ballots are currently open in the race to become the Tory candidate for mayor and close next Wednesday.

A source close to Sadiq Khan said: “This is complete nonsense. Despite huge Tory cuts to the police and our youth services, including during the period Cleverly served in government, we’re now seeing historic falls in violent crime under Sadiq and neighbourhood crime continues to fall across the capital.”

SICK ABUSE Girl, 2, ‘raped & beaten to death by monster stepdad, 23, days after grandfather spotted horror bruises on body’

A TWO-YEAR-OLD girl has died after allegedly being raped and beaten by her stepdad.

The girl’s granddad had warned the toddler’s mum when he noticed suspicious bruises all over her body about two weeks before her death.



Isis Gabrielly Lemos Nascimento was rushed to a hospital in Brazil when she turned purple and became limp but could not be saved.

Her stepdad Felipe de Souza Neckel da Silva, 23, was arrested after doctors discovered injuries that raised suspicions of sexual abuse.



The child’s mum, Maria Luiza Nascimento, 21, was arrested nine days later for failing to protect her daughter.

Both have been formally accused of murder and the rape of a vulnerable person.



The allegations against Maria stem from her alleged failure to intervene.

Police said the toddler suffered a cardiac arrest before she was brought to the emergency medical centre.

Felipe told police that Isis had sustained the injuries when she fell while he was bathing her.

He also claimed that bruises on her body were caused by an allergy.



Police lieutenant colonel Ricardo Edson said: “In his statement, the stepdad said he was bathing the child when she fell.

“However, that version does not match what was observed by the medical team.”

The toddler’s granddad, Klinger de Oliveira, 43, said he had warned his daughter about suspicious bruises on Isis’s body about 15 days before she died.

He said the family had become concerned when Maria began a relationship with Felipe about three months earlier.

“We warned her many times, but she always dismissed what I was saying and pushed me away,” he said.



“The signs started appearing about 15 days earlier. From then on, we became suspicious and kept warning her, but she always snapped at us.”

A neighbour first spotted Felipe holding the apparently unconscious child outside their home.

Felipe shouted out that the “little girl was dying”.

They used a neighbour’s car to rush her to hospital but she had “already arrived lifeless”, the neighbour said.

“She was completely limp and very purple. I put myself in the position of a father because I have a little girl too, and I even cried because of what had happened to her,” he said.

News.title: Security guard, 49, caught having sex with corpse of woman, 79, in morgue freezer after colleagues saw him ‘sweating’

DEPRAVED ACT Security guard, 49, caught having sex with corpse of woman, 79, in morgue freezer after colleagues saw him ‘sweating’

A DEPRAVED hospital security guard was caught having sex with the corpse of a 79-year-old woman after colleagues spotted him “sweating profusely”.

Randall Bird, 49, was caught red-handed with his flies “wide open” and his belt left on top of a gurney by two stunned colleagues after they walked into a morgue freezer.



The sick pervert has now been found guilty by a jury of four counts of crimes against the dead following the stomach-churning incident at a hospital in Phoenix, Arizona.

Bird – who was sacked following his arrest in November 2023 – was responsible for transporting the bodies of patients who passed away at Banner University Medical Center to the facility’s morgue.



But the twisted guard abused his position to carry out vile acts of necrophilia.

According to a statement prepared by Phoenix cops, Bird’s uniform appeared dishevelled and his duty belt was resting atop a stretcher where a bagged corpse had been placed.



The body bag contained the remains of a 5ft, 85lb pensioner, who had died from natural causes.

Horrified witnesses found the bag had been “completely unzipped open” with the dead woman lying face down.

Her hospital gown had also “been rolled up above her belly button area, exposing her naked body from the waist down,” according to court docs.

When his co-workers walked into the room, Bird frantically tried to cover up the elderly victim by pulling down her gown.



Detectives later confirmed the guard’s DNA was recovered from the corpse, while a post-mortem examination also detected unexplained rib fractures on the OAP’s body.

In a statement released at the time of the incident, hospital officials said: “We are saddened and appalled by the alleged actions of an individual at Banner-University Medical Center Phoenix that resulted in his arrest on November 28, 2023.

“Banner Health has and remains committed to high standards that require each of our team members to treat everyone, at every stage of life, with compassion, dignity and respect.”

An indictment filed last year accused the suspect of “having sexual intercourse with a dead human body” as well as sexual contact with the victim’s breasts.

Bird’s trial had previously been delayed after he underwent quadruple bypass surgery at a separate medical facility in Phoenix.



He has now been remanded in custody and booked into county jail ahead of his sentencing on December 18.

Each felony count carries a prison term of between 12 and 45 months.

The sick act comes after a British tourist’s body mysteriously vanished from a hospital morgue in Cyprus before being discovered under a completely different name.

News.title: Moment knife-wielding man plunges headfirst from window after being tasered by cops in two-hour standoff in tourist town
News.content:

THIS is the shocking moment a knife-wielding man plunges from a first floor window after being tasered by cops following a two-hour standoff.

Dramatic footage shows officers electrocute the 33-year-old before he plummets onto his head from the building in Granada, Spain.



The man quickly gets to his feet before continuing to confront police outside the residence.

His housemates had called the cops after he started behaving erratically and they were unable to calm him down.



They said he was potentially under the influence of alcohol or drugs, although this remains unconfirmed.

When officers showed up at around 7.50pm, they reportedly found the man armed with a large knife.

He is also said to have grabbed a screwdriver and threatened officers as they tried to talk him down.

Police initially tried to defuse the situation, but the man became increasingly aggressive, prompting officers to call in reinforcements.



A specialist Prevention and Reaction Unit (UPR) arrived as officers had spent around two hours attempting to bring the situation under control.

They eventually had to use a taser to subdue him.

But the confrontation took another extraordinary turn when he fell from a first-floor window onto the street below.

Despite the fall, he managed to get back up and continued threatening those around him.

Around ten officers were eventually needed to overpower and arrest the man in a nearby square.



He was taken to hospital under police guard before being transferred to a cell.

No details have been released about any injuries sustained during the fall.

News.title: Russell Brand prison message 'appalling' and being investigated, No 10 says
News.content:
A message by Russell Brand to his followers in which he claimed innocence for his sexual offences was "clearly appalling" and is being urgently investigated, Downing Street has said.

The comedian is currently serving a 10-and-half-year prison sentence after being convicted of rape and three counts of sexual assault.

His wife Laura read out a message from him on their Sunday Service show on YouTube, in which the convicted rapist claimed: "I am not guilty of the offences I have been jailed for."

No 10 said it expects action to be taken if Brand is found to have broken prison rules.

Victims' commissioner for London Andrea Simon said the claims will "certainly retraumatise his victims and other survivors of rape who have to hear it".

In the couple's podcast, released on Sunday, Laura Brand can be seen sitting on a sofa and is holding a Bible with a candle burning in front of her.

Relaying the message from her husband, Laura Brand said the comedian - who is currently being held at HMP Littlehey in Cambridgeshire - called prison staff "strong", "kind" and "dedicated", and asked people to support his "treasured wife and family".

She said she had been speaking to him and he "is OK and is praying".

Brand has positioned himself as a Christian influencer, and has a large following among believers, including in the US.

Asked about the message, the prime minister's official spokesman said: "Prisoners are strictly banned from making statements that cause distress to victims and speaking to the media is only permitted in exceptional circumstances.

"Prisoners cannot get around these rules by having someone else publish their comments."

Speaking earlier, Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband told Sky News: "His crimes are heinous and awful. I think it's revolting, by the way, that he shows no remorse today in his comments."

"No remorse, no sympathy for the victims. Just disgusting comments," he added.

Speaking on BBC Radio 4's Today programme, victim's commissioner for London Andrea Simon added: "The victims during the sentencing hearing highlighted how his denials and ongoing media fame over two decades had added to their pain and trauma," she said.

"The fact survivors are still having to hear this now is really problematic and very concerning that we can't do more to protect them from it."

While freedom of expression allows convicted sex offenders such as Brand to profess their innocence, Simon said terms of service of media platforms should regulate "the way in which they get their message out".

She added that prison rules should also be reviewed to "bar those convicted of sending messages to be broadcast" unless permission is granted by the prison governor.

If Brand is found to have broken prison rules, possible punishments enforceable by prison governors can result in restrictions on social visits or loss of privileges such as access to additional time in the gym or loss of TV.

Governors can also impose proportionate restrictions on communications where justified.

This could include blocking specific phone numbers, increased monitoring of calls or restricting contact with individuals where necessary to protect victims or maintain prison security.

Her workforce has more than halved to 21 staff. Osborne told the BBC it costs "around Â£60,000 to train an apprentice before we can actually start allowing them onto customers' heads".

Osborne does not feel she is getting help to offer jobs to youngsters.

The independent report by former Labour minister Alan Milburn has been in the works for a year and will be published on Tuesday in full.

He has already unveiled some of his proposals including:

Reducing benefits - under-25s should no longer be able to claim the health element of UK-wide Universal Credit or personal independence payment (Pip), which is the main disability benefit in England and Wales

A legal guarantee of a job, training or employment support with those who refuse to take up potentially losing their benefits.

Doubling the threshold at which businesses start paying NI for 21 to 24-year-olds from Â£5,000 to Â£10,000.

At the moment, businesses pay no employer NI contributions for workers younger than 21 or for apprentices under 25 â unless they earn above a threshold of Â£50,270.

However, for non-apprentices aged 21-24, employers pay 15% on annual earnings above Â£5,000.

This has been the situation since April 2025, after the then Chancellor Rachel Reeves increased the rate from 13.8% and lowered the threshold from Â£9,100.

Under Sir Keir Starmer, the government raised NI for firms but Milburn will say the Neets issue was not started by the increase.

Immediately axing NI for 21 to 24-year-olds would cost Â£5.1bn, according to research by the Resolution Foundation, a left-leaning think tank.

Milburn is set to say that an immediate across-the-board cut in employer NI is not the best use of several billions of pounds of public money.

But shadow work and pensions secretary, Helen Whately, said the government should "just stop doing the taxing".

News.title: Lindsay Clancy to face retrial next year for deaths of her three children
News.content:
Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts woman accused of murdering her three children, will face a second trial next year, a judge has said.

The judge set a trial date for 29 March 2027, though the district attorney did not explicitly say what charges Clancy would face.

Prosecutors said they wanted to proceed with a jury trial, and the defence said they took that to mean Clancy would again face first-degree murder charges, the same as she faced in the first trial.

The 36-year-old's first trial this year fell apart when a 12-person jury failed to reach a verdict over the deaths of five-year-old Cora, Dawson, three, and eight-month-old Callan at the the family home.

"I think you can read between the lines that when they say that the case is going to require a jury, that it's an indirect comment from the DA [district attorney] that they intend to proceed on first-degree murder indictments, so we will pick a trial date," defence lawyer Kevin Reddington said.

Clancy was charged in the first trial with three counts of first-degree-murder, which is the intentional and premeditated killing of another person.

The district attorney has not yet officially said he will proceed with first-degree-murder charges.

The prosecution could choose to bring lesser charges against Clancy, such as second-degree-murder, which applies to unlawful killings committed with malice or extreme recklessness, but without planning.

A week ago, Judge William Sullivan rejected a defence attempt to throw out the case on the grounds of double jeopardy.

Double jeopardy is a legal principle that protects someone from being prosecuted more than once for the same crime after an acquittal or conviction.

The judge's decision cleared the way for a second trial.

News.title: UK lost more than it gained from Brexit, Burnham to say ahead of EU summit
News.content:
The prime minister is expected to argue the UK has lost more than it has gained from leaving the European Union in a speech ahead of a UK-EU summit later this week.

Speaking at the Lord Mayor's Banquet on Monday, Andy Burnham will compare the UK's Brexit deal to the "emperor's new clothes" - saying "a needlessly hard Brexit" created barriers for businesses and the promise to "take back control" was not delivered.

He is due to sign new agreements on food, energy and youth mobility with the bloc at Friday's summit, after the substance of those deals was set by his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer.

The Conservatives have said Labour are "dragging us into the European Union via the back door".

Separately Burnham has said he wants to examine the "pros and cons" of different options for Britain's long-term relationship with the EU.

Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband told the BBC the prime minister would lay out these potential options after the UK-EU summit.

However, Burnham has ruled out major changes before the next general election.

Burnham is expected to say on Monday: "It's like the emperor's new clothes â where no-one is prepared to say the obvious truth. Well, I say it as I see it. And to be frank, the emperor has nothing on.

"The Brexit we were given has not worked. We have lost more than we have gained."

Ahead of Friday's UK-EU summit, Burnham will set out three tests for any agreement.

Firstly, that it must be consistent with Labour's 2024 general election manifesto pledge that there would be "no return to the single market, the customs union, or freedom of movement".

He will also say it must improve the original Brexit deal and bring it closer to what people thought they were voting for in 2016.

Finally, he will say any deal must pass the "Makerfield test" of providing tangible improvements to people's everyday lives - a reference to voters in Burnham's Greater Manchester constituency.

He will say the prospect of a new deal is a "win-win" and illustrates a "new approach".

"Not adversarial. No longer burning bridges. But being constructive and positive - showing that we can come together to confront shared challenges."

News.title: Yellow weather warnings issued for snow as temperatures plummet
News.content:

A yellow weather warning for snow comes into effect in the very early hours of Tuesday following a blast of Arctic air pushing across the UK causing temperatures to plummet.

Cold health alerts for parts of northern England also remain in force from the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) until 09:00 GMT on Thursday.

Some snow is forecast over the hills and mountains in the north over the coming days but the wintry chill will be fairly short-lived in the south, where temperatures will rebound to above average by midweek.
