Craig is a lifelong supporter of Liverpool, while both Pierce Brosnan and Sean Connery supported Celtic – even if the latter later changed his allegiance to fierce rivals Rangers.

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi is five points and seven goals WORSE than Thomas Frank was at Spurs – but stats show he’s much better
Sports.content:
Next

TEN LEAGUE games into his first proper season as Spurs boss and Roberto De Zerbi is seven goals and five points worse off than predecessor Thomas Frank at this point.

Yet the positivity surrounding the Italian among the Spurs fanbase is so different to doom and gloom under Frank that you would think it would be the other way round.



The eye test is giving Tottenham fans plenty of reason for optimism with De Zerbi’s more expansive, entertaining style of play, despite their slow start.

But now SunSport have delved into the numbers comparing the two spells between RDZ and Frank, who looks set to return to management with Crystal Palace.



And the stats back up just why that goodwill appears to be there from the fanbase, with De Zerbi surpassing Frank in nearly every metric (barring, admittedly, the all-important goals and points).

It is vital to remember that this is from the period under Frank where the going was as good as it got, as it quickly unravelled afterwards and he was sacked by February.

Whereas De Zerbi’s numbers come from a ten-game spell in which his side have failed to score in half of those fixtures.

There are caveats, of course. Big ones, too.

One is that De Zerbi already had seven games at the back end of last season to assess the squad and get across some of his ideas, albeit when the overwhelming priority was Premier League survival.

The next is that the current incumbent has no Europe to deal with, while Frank was managing a Champions League campaign as well as a Super Cup final.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

And lastly De Zerbi was backed to the tune of £300million-plus in the summer, with largely his first-choice signings.

While Frank missed out on priority targets Antoine Semenyo, Morgan Gibbs-White, Bryan Mbeumo and Eberechi Eze.

But even with those valid asterisks, Spurs fans who quickly lost faith with Thomas the Frank engine but are on board with De Zerbi may well feel vindicated by the underlying numbers.

POSSESSION

Having the ball, what does it mean any more? Certainly there are more and more examples of teams that dominate possession not having as successful results as they would like.

But at Spurs, there is an expectation from the fanbase to play dominating, entertaining football – they do not call it The Tottenham Way for nothing – and it is hard to do that without the ball.



De Zerbi is obsessed with possession and the numbers prove that.

From these first ten games, he is averaging 62.9 per cent possession per match – which is nine per cent more than Frank achieved in the comparative spell.

And as his team grows more accustomed with his style, they are dominating the ball more and more, with possession it the high 50s for his first three games but regularly in the 60s since then.

That includes the whopping 68.9 per cent of the ball they had at Stamford Bridge, of all place, for last month’s 2-0 win at Chelsea.



While Frank’s possession stats went on a downward trend during his tenure with more than 60 per cent in four of his first five games, but then averaging less than 50 across his next five, which included the dismal 1-1 draw at home to bottom-of-the-table Wolves.

It was just one aspect of why fans started to doubt Thomas early on into his failed tenure.

PASSING

It is one thing having the ball, it is another thing what you do with it.

De Zerbi’s average passing numbers are massively higher than Frank’s, with the Italian’s average of 576 passes per game a whopping 145 more than his predecessor.

Out of those passes, De Zerbi is averaging 144 successful final third passes a game – a crucial stat as it is the area in which you can really hurt the opposition – compared to 82 for Frank.



The disparity in numbers speaks to how so often under Frank, Spurs looked like they had no idea how they would break a team down in open play, compared to the, admittedly not frequent enough, spells De Zerbi’s side have overwhelmed the opposition this term.

Though it must be said that the 2-0 win over ten-man Crystal Palace last month skewed those numbers somewhat given Spurs managed a massive 373 successful final third passes that game.

Yet for all those passes, De Zerbi’s team is producing fewer long balls than Frank’s did per game.

It would be a tad harsh to label Frank’s Tottenham side a long-ball team but they certainly punted it more often than his successor’s team do.

Frank’s side managed 47 long balls on average per game, nine more than what De Zerbi’s side have averaged so far this term.



ATTACK

De Zerbi is marginally winning the expected goals per game – with an xG of 1.21 compared to 1.05 for Frank.

The modern-day stat may be divisive among some fans but it is generally an indicator of how well a team creates.

De Zerbi would certainly want to pump those numbers up and the fact that his side have had five games with an xG less than one (as well as five games without scoring!) shows how there is much work to do, particularly in the striker department.

But the fact that even with their goal woes they are still outperforming what Frank managed underlines just why Spurs fans speedily lost faith in the Dane.

None more so than with the pathetic showings at home to Bournemouth and Chelsea, both of which they lost 1-0, when their xG score was respectively 0-1 and 0.05.



Frank labelled the Bournemouth “horrendous” and said his xG score vs Chelsea (which was the worst of any Premier League side that season) “hurt massively”.

De Zerbi’s average of 15.5 shots per game across the ten matches is just under six more than Frank managed, while the Italian’s side also average 6.6 more touches per game more in the opposition box.

They are producing two more crosses per game and have just as many goals from set-pieces (three) as Frank, who many fans saw as too reliant on that route to scoring.

DEFENCE

This is where Frank’s numbers do edge out De Zerbi in terms of tackles and clearances.

But when you have less of the ball, it is a likely consequence that you will have to do more of those.



Frank averaged just over 20 tackles per game, while De Zerbi’s team is on 17.5.

For clearances, Frank’s 26.7 is more than De Zerbi’s 20.4.

Yet Frank’s team also averaged three more aerial duels lost than won per game.

While De Zerbi’s team are just about beating out their opposition on that metric – an average of 0.4 more aerial duel wins than losses, to be exact.

It suggests this De Zerbi side has a bit more fight about it, even if it is a long way from where he wants them to be, especially after the limp second half at Leeds on Saturday.



Frank’s side only conceded eight goals in their opening ten games but their expected goals against was 1.34.

De Zerbi’s have shipped ten but their xG against is 1.19, and that includes the abysmal 3.96 score Brentford inflicted on them on the opening day.

RUNNING

When things started going wrong for Frank at Spurs, he often talked about the need to “run harder”.

Spurs fans started to see through it as too simplistic and it only added to the perception that the ex-Brentford boss was out of his depth.

The irony here is that De Zerbi’s side are averaging marginally bigger distances than Frank’s was.



Collectively, De Zerbi’s team are averaging 113.3km covered per game, compared to 112.6km under Frank.

They have also outrun the opposition in each of the last six games before Saturday’s poor showing at Elland Road.

No doubt Tottenham’s momentum was checked with that 1-0 defeat in Yorkshire and shows De Zerbi still has plenty of work to do.

But if you zoom out, the numbers suggest things are improving – as does De Zerbi’s Premier League manager of the month award for October for three wins on the spin.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The same could not be said for Frank, who, by the time he lost at home to Chelsea for the last of his first ten games, was already starting to lose fan support.

Sports.title: How James Trafford and Jordan Pickford compare as Leeds and Everton goalies battle for England’s No1 jersey
Sports.content:
Next

JAMES TRAFFORD has been given his chance to become England’s No1, and the Leeds United goalkeeper is grabbing it with both hands.

The 24-year-old produced a stunning performance against Spain in Madrid on Sunday night, making a string of crucial saves to help England secure a famous 3-2 victory.



And his heroics have strengthened his case to replace Jordan Pickford as Thomas Tuchel’s first-choice goalkeeper.

Trafford‘s finest moment came deep into stoppage time when he produced a remarkable double save to deny Spain an equaliser.



With England desperately holding on to their narrow lead, the youngster showed incredible reactions to keep out two close-range efforts and preserve the victory.

He finished the night with six saves and was named Player of the Match as England ended Spain’s 43-game unbeaten run.



It was another huge statement from Trafford, who has been handed an opportunity by Tuchel and has done little to suggest he should give up the gloves.

And while the German boss has refused to publicly name his first-choice goalkeeper, his decision to start Trafford ahead of Pickford in such a huge game suggests the balance could be shifting.

Tuchel said afterwards: “There’s no number one. It’s a good double save. That’s what we wanted. He had a brilliant match.”

But it is not just Trafford’s performance in Madrid that should give Pickford reason to worry.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Their individual data show the Leeds goalkeeper has been outperforming his Everton rival in several key areas for England.

The figures, covering their respective appearances against Czechia, Spain and Croatia in September and October, make interesting reading.

Both goalkeepers played 180 minutes during that period, but Trafford faced nine shots on target compared to just five for Pickford.

The former Manchester City goalkeeper made eight saves, twice as many as Pickford’s four.

That gave Trafford an impressive save percentage of 88.9 per cent, compared to Pickford’s 80 per cent.



And the numbers become even more encouraging for the Leeds star when looking at the quality of chances he has faced.

Trafford prevented 0.8 goals according to Opta’s expected goals on target conceded metric, while Pickford prevented just 0.2.

It means Trafford has been stopping more goals than the quality of opposition shots would suggest he should.



His performances against Spain have been particularly impressive, with the youngster making six saves in September’s meeting between the two countries.

He followed that up with another six in Madrid on Sunday, including the dramatic late double stop that left his England team-mates rushing to congratulate him.

And his form for Leeds this season has been just as impressive.

Trafford has prevented 4.4 goals in the Premier League, conceding eight from shots worth 12.4 expected goals on target, putting him TOP of the division for that measure.

Pickford, meanwhile, has conceded ten goals from shots worth 11.05 expected goals on target, giving him a goals-prevented figure of 1.05.



That is another area where Trafford is outperforming his more experienced rival and strengthening his case for the England shirt.

However, Pickford still holds the upper hand when it comes to distribution at international level.

The Everton goalkeeper completed 63 of his 80 passes during the two games covered by Opta figures, giving him a passing accuracy of 78.8 per cent.

Trafford managed just 35 successful passes from 54 attempts, with an accuracy of 64.8 per cent.



Pickford also completed 20 long passes compared to Trafford’s seven, with the Everton man’s long-pass accuracy standing at 54.1 per cent against his rival’s 26.9 per cent.

And at 32, Pickford has the experience of 94 England caps and several major tournaments behind him.

But Trafford, eight years his junior, represents both the present and potentially the long-term future for England.

His performances have given Tuchel a genuine selection dilemma, particularly with the Leeds goalkeeper showing he can deliver against the very best opposition.



The England boss was also impressed by Trafford’s composure in possession against Spain, praising his ability to help the Three Lions play through the hosts’ pressing.

Tuchel said: “The obvious save, where he deserves full credit, is the double save at the very end. Absolutely brilliant.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And with England’s Nations League quarter-finals coming up in March, Trafford has given his manager every reason to keep faith with him.

Pickford has been a reliable servant for England for years but the numbers and Trafford’s heroics in Madrid suggest his position is no longer guaranteed.

Sports.title: Ratcliffe's Ineos Group settles £10m-plus claim with Ainslie's firm over yacht
Sports.content:
A company connected to Sir Jim Ratcliffe's Ineos Group said it has settled a High Court claim against a firm founded by Sir Ben Ainslie.

Ineos Racing sued Athena Racing earlier this year, alleging the latter breached a deal between the two companies by refusing to return the multimillion-pound yacht Ineos Britannia, which Ainslie captained at the 2024 America's Cup in a 7-2 defeat to Emirates Team New Zealand in Barcelona.

Lawyers for Ineos said in court documents filed earlier this year that the claim was valued at more than £10 million.

Athena Racing was defending the claim, arguing that Ineos was not entitled to have the yacht back.

Image: Ainslie is a four-time Olympic sailing champion

In a statement on Monday, Ineos said: "Ineos has reached a settlement with Athena Racing and considers the matter now closed."

No further details, including whether the yacht has been returned, have been provided.

Four-time Olympic champion Ainslie hit out at Ineos Britannia in April 2025 after they confirmed their challenge for the 38th America's Cup in Naples in 2027 would not involve him.

Ainslie's GB1 team is the challenger of record for the event in Italy next year.

No British team has ever won the America's Cup since it was first contested in 1850.

Sports.title: Sky Sports News presenter Fulton becomes Kent director of cricket
Sports.content:
Sky Sports News presenter David Fulton will become Kent's new director of cricket next month.

Fulton is a former Kent captain and will take up this new role on December 1.

He will return to the club in a full-time role after representing his home county in a playing career that spanned two decades, and will oversee both Kent men's and women's talent pathways, from age group to first-team level.

Fulton made his Kent first-class debut against Cambridge University in 1992, and went on to make over 300 appearances for the county in all formats, scoring over 14,000 runs.

He was named as the PCA's Cricketer of the Year in 2001, and was appointed as club captain in 2003, after previously leading Kent's County Championship side in the 2002 season.

Following retirement from playing, Fulton embarked on a successful career in the media with Sky Sports, while he also coached within the Kent Talent Pathway and men's first team as a batting consultant, as well as with England Lions.

"I'm extremely honoured to take on the role of director of cricket at my home county," Fulton said.

"Kent has always been a huge part of my life as a fan, a player and a captain, and I can't wait to take up this new challenge.

"I want Kent members and the wider fanbase to be proud of our club and the way we play our cricket. I'm excited to get to work with our men's and women's coaching staff heading into the 2027 season and beyond."

Sports.title: Camara to drive for Haas again at Las Vegas GP
Sports.content:
Haas have confirmed that Rafael Camara will continue as Oliver Bearman's team-mate for this weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix after making his Formula 1 debut last time out in Brazil.

The American-owned squad have been left with a vacant seat for the final five rounds of the season following a fallout between French driver Esteban Ocon and team boss Ayao Komatsu last month in Mexico.

Japanese driver Ryo Hirakawa, who had already featured in first practice in Mexico, drove in the Mexico City Grand Prix, before Camara, who had earlier in October been confirmed as Ocon's replacement at Haas for the 2027 season, was given the opportunity to make his debut at his home race in Sao Paulo.

The 21-year-old endured a challenging debut amid wet conditions at Interlagos, crashing out of qualifying before finishing the race last of the runners to take the chequered flag.

"We're looking forward to building on that for his second race weekend with us."

Sports.title: Mahomes has a new star and Cousins fights back tears - NFL Sunday Review
Sports.content:
"There's more of the story to be written." Kirk Cousins could barely fight back the tears as he processed a day he thought might never come, a second chance he thought might never arrive. But football can't keep Kirko Chainz down, and suddenly the Minnesota Vikings have hope.

It is the easiest story in the NFL to get behind. A 38-year-old Kirk Cousins, written off more times than he can count, deemed deep into the back nine of his career, coming back to a hero's welcome to spearhead a playoff charge while lighting a fire under an offense in desperate need of inspiration. His inspiration.

He is football's lovable goof, with the unpretentious, unflashy dad clothes and a 'down with the kids' willingness to sling on Justin Jefferson's chains should it lift his teammates. He is also now Minnesota's great hope of rewarding defensive mastery with an attack capable of competing in January football.

The Vikings were limping behind Kyler Murray, limping behind Carson Wentz but sitting a coveted 6-2, and on Tuesday rolled the dice by trading to bring back Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders.

It was three years ago that Cousins played the final game of his first chapter with the Vikings when he tore his Achilles tendon in Week Eight against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. On Sunday he was back where it ended - but could it yet be where it all started again?

Cousins, who had revived his starting career as mentor to No 1 pick Mendoza in Las Vegas, finished 21 of 31 for 207 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in his first game back as the Vikings stunned the Packers 30-10.

His start featured a perfectly placed sideline strike between two defenders to a reception-starved Justin Jefferson on third-and-second in the first quarter, and so too a high-level tight-window bullet to Myles Price for a 38-yard touchdown catch-and-run on third-and-23.

It would become Jefferson's best game of the season as he made eight catches from nine targets for 92 yards and two touchdowns, Cousins' reconnecting with one of the stars of the league having seen him suffer for the first half of the season.

Much of the debate and, at times, criticism around Cousins throughout his career has been the shortage of point guard ability as a needle-moving creator. The Patrick Mahomes' and Josh Allens and Joe Burrows and Lamar Jacksons of the world have unfortunately heightened that bar for all quarterbacks across the league. But what has never been in doubt with Cousins is the efficiency at which he feeds his best players, and at which he moves the ball and at which he can accentuate an offense's strengths without being spectacular. Spectacular isn't exactly needed when there is a Brian Flores defense foaming at the mouth in wait of their chance to go hunting on the sideline.

In one game the Vikings looked a more polished, more accomplished operation behind Cousins, and alongside that came another rampant defensive play that saw Minnesota sack Jordan Love eight times.

They were frightening, and the perfect complement once Cousins had helped the Vikings get on top early. The impact was evidenced through the time of possession, Cousins' offense holding the ball for 17.55 minutes in the first half and 35.16 a week on since the Vikings mustered just 17 minutes and 28 seconds of possession against the Bills. What a difference some respite for one of the league's most potent defenses makes.

There was a nice moment in the second half when former New Orleans Saints quarterback Drew Brees paid tribute to Cousins' communication at the line of scrimmage, where he shifted personnel and changed the play like an orchestra conductor. It was long-lost control and assurance under center.

Cousins later executed a trick play that saw him pump fake left and the swivel to pump fake to his right before tossing to Gavin Bartholomew over the middle of the field for a touchdown. For Kevin O'Connell to dial up a play like that just days after Cousins' arrival is testament to the footballing brain now leading Minnesota's offense.

"It was emotional coming to this stadium three years ago, tearing my Achilles here. It's been a tough three years, just grateful for the opportunity to play here, grateful for my teammates and what they did to make this outcome possible.

"It's been a tough three years. There's more of the story to be written," said Cousins post-game, his voice cracking several times."

Cousins won just one playoff game in six seasons during his first stint with the Vikings, before signing a four-year $180m contract with the Atlanta Falcons in 2024, only to be bench for Michael Penix Jr in his first season. He was then released in March earlier this year before landing in Las Vegas as something of a bridge towards their new era under Mendoza.

What looked like a declining career hurtling towards its end is instead flirting with one final twist.

What we learned

Patrick Mahomes' new friends are alright. The Kansas City Chiefs were without their best player this season in Kenneth Walker III on Sunday; it did not matter. The absence of last season's Super Bowl MVP paved the way for an increased role for fifth-round rookie running back Emmett Johnson, who capitalised emphatically with 22 carries for 101 yards and six catches for 70 yards and two scores through the air as Kansas City beat the Atlanta Falcons 35-13 in a five-touchdown day for Patrick Mahomes. Johnson showcased his menu of evasive manoeuvres in the open field with a clinic in tackle-missing jukes and the yards-after-catch threat primed to see him become one of Andy Reid's favourite weapons over the second half of the season.

There was also a debut for wide receiver Josh Downs, who had four catches for 53 yards and a touchdown in his first game since arriving via a trade from the Indianapolis Colts. It's been a long time since Mahomes and the Chiefs posed a consistent vertical threat but Downs could prove an answer to as much. Mahomes completed seven of 12 attempts on passes of 10-plus air yards for 206 yards and three touchdowns, while going three of six on attempts of 20-plus yards for 132 yards and two scores. The Chiefs offense is clicking.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player All of Patrick Mahomes five touchdowns in the Kansas City Chiefs' win over the Atlanta Falcons

Denzel Ward is playing at an All-Pro level. It is hard to be one of the best players on the league for so long on a team that has been bad for so long; Myles Garrett did it in Cleveland, and Denzel Ward is still doing it. He stepped up when the Browns needed him most on Sunday with a stunning diving pass break-up against Xavier Hutchinson to deny the Houston Texans with 30 seconds left in Cleveland's 27-24 victory. Ward allowed just four receptions for 16 yards from nine targets on Sunday while lining up against Nico Collins in man coverage on 10 of 11 routes, according to Next Gen Stats. Pat Surtain II may still hold the honour of top dog in the eyes of many, but Ward will feel he holds a strong argument as being the best corner in football.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Veteran NFL referee Gene Steratore admitted he'd never seen this play from Tory Horton, who jumped him to keep the ball from going out of the endzone for a touchback

There are encouraging signs for Fernando Mendoza. The Raiders ushered in a new chapter this weekend as No 1 overall Draft pick Mendoza led his side out against the Seattle Seahawks in his first regular season start following Cousins' trade to the Vikings. It started strongly with a touchdown run on his opening possession before Mike Macdonald dialled the pressure up a notch on defense in the second half as the Raiders offense suffered without star weapon Brock Bowers. He went 11 of 13 for 90 yards through the air in the first half, before managing just six of 16 for 53 yards following the interval. Mendoza finished the game 17 of 29 passing for 143 yards, zero touchdowns and zero turnovers while being sacked six times. Facing the league's best defense always beckoned as a baptism of fire, so the shortage of interceptions or apparent ball security issues was a plus point.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Seattle Seahawks against the Las Vegas Raiders from Week 10 of the NFL season

Overreaction or reality?

Brock Purdy is a top five quarterback in the NFL. For somebody so often pigeonholed as a 'system quarterback', he sure does do a lot of good outside of the system. Purdy continues to showcase an elite ability to extend plays and create outside of the pocket, perhaps best epitomised by the 74-yard McCaffrey touchdown catch-and-run that saw him side-step a near-certain sack, slide to his left, cut back inside and fire a dart to his open running back. Poise in the face of chaos and a ground threat that makes him dangerous off-script. Purdy finished the game 22 of 28 for 389 yards and three touchdowns with a 154.5 passer rating. He is in the MVP hunt and playing at a level among the premier play-callers in football. By now, though, he knows his true judgement comes around playoff time.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Detroit Lions wide receiver Isaac TeSlaa makes an unbelievable catch against the New England Patriots in Munich

Winners and losers

Winners:

Christian McCaffrey: If you thought injury setbacks had zapped the juice in the 49ers running back, think again. McCaffrey went off for 223 scrimmage yards and three touchdowns to tear apart of hobbling Cowboys defense, which surrendered a franchise-worst 584 yards at home. McCaffrey's 161 receiving yards were the most by a running back in a game since Jamaal Charles' 195 in 2013, while he is the first 49ers player with 200 scrimmage yards and three scores in a regular season game since Jerry Rice in 1995.

Parker Washington: Jacksonville Jaguars head coach Liam Coen called him the best player on the field, and a man possessed. The Tennessee Titans could not live with Parker Washington as the Jags receiver took another major step closer towards a bumper new contract with a career-best seven catches for 152 yards and a touchdown in his side's 40-23 win. One play saw him put Alontae Taylor in a blender with another clinic in route-running, another play saw him levitate to haul in Trevor Lawrence's pass at the sideline, and another saw him race free for a 50-yard catch-and-run. His outstanding season continues.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Detroit Lions' Aidan Hutchinson injured himself while celebrating a sack of New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye in Germany

Losers:

Mike Vrabel: On more than one occasion on Sunday, the camera captured Mike Vrabel closing his eyes in excruciating thought at the sight of another setback for his Patriots, be it an injury or a pre-snap penalty. The game was over before it ever really began for last year's beaten Super Bowl finalists, Drake Maye departing after the opening drive through injury and a sputtering offense later losing AJ Brown in the latest disruption to what is threatening to become a nightmare maiden season in New England. They are 5-5 with the Buffalo Bills, Minnesota Vikings and Kansas City Chiefs coming up over the next month; their season is teetering on the edge.

Aidan Hutchinson: Perhaps it is unfair to kick a man when he is down, but it is hard to overlook a game-ending, potentially season-ending injury caused by a celebration. Lions edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson is feared to have suffered a serious knee injury after landing awkwardly during a post-sack celebration on the opening drive of New England's defeat to the Lions in Munich. It was the same play that saw Maye suffer his own game-halting injury, with neither returning to the field. His absence would leave Detroit without their star edge rusher heading into the second half of their playoff charge

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Amon-Ra St. Brown scores a stunning 56-yard TD in Munich for the Detroit Lions

Player of the Weekend - Jahmyr Gibbs, RB, Detroit Lions

Jahmyr Gibbs is a familiar resident in this slot, but he is impossible to ignore as the clear frontrunner for Offensive Player of the Year through 10 weeks. The Lions running back was at his scintillating best in Munich as he put up 252 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns to torch the Patriots defense, his 62 career touchdowns breaking Terrell Davis' record for most by a player through his first four seasons in NFL history. He is not only the perfect cocktail of speed and shiftiness, but one of the smartest crease detectors in football. He runs hard, he runs fast, he runs with high-powered intelligence as the focal point of Drew Petzing's Lions offense. Another clinic, this time on European soil, to extend his lead as the NFL leader in scrimmage yards.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Miami Dolphins cornerback Chris Johnson intercepts Daniel Jones to score a touchdown

Game of the Weekend

The 49ers and the Cowboys go way back as one of the NFL's most storied rivalries between two of football's most prestigious franchises. They renewed their dislike to the sight of record numbers as they combined for a series-high 86 points, with San Francisco beating Dallas 46-40 to improve to 8-1 on the season. While the 49ers flexed their offensive power, in doing so there were more glaring concerns over the Cowboys and a defense ranked third worst in yards allowed. Dak Prescott threw five touchdown passes, three to George Pickens, as the Cowboys put up 439 yards of offense, only to come out second best. Purdy produced two scoring strikes to McCaffrey and one to Deebo Samuel.

"The second half was unacceptable; tackling was atrocious, you can't give up three explosive plays of over 65 yards for touchdowns and expect to win. Totally unacceptable defense in the second half," said Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer.

Sports.title: Hutchinson celebration results in season-ending injury
Sports.content:
Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson has been ruled out for the season after suffering a knee injury while celebrating a sack against the New England Patriots.

Hutchinson leaped in the air but went straight to the ground after landing. He immediately grabbed his right knee, staying down before eventually walking to the blue tent for evaluation.

He then walked gingerly to the locker room and didn't return to the game.

NFL Network Insider Ian Rapoport reported Monday that initial tests revealed Hutchinson sustained a torn ACL that will see him miss the rest of the season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Amon-Ra St. Brown scores his second touchdown of the game to extend the Detroit Lions' lead over the New England Patriots

Hutchinson had sacked Maye on third down at the Detroit 15-yard line to end New England's opening drive, which saw Andy Borregales then kick a 33-yard field goal.

Maye also exited the game after the same play and is feared to have suffered a season-ending fractured ankle, with further tests expected upon his return to the United States.

The Lions went on to win the game 35-10 at Munich's Allianz Arena as the Patriots offense capitulated behind backup quarterback Tommy DeVito.

But it came at a major cost, with Detroit now set to resume their bid to reach a first Super Bowl minus their star pass rusher for the rest of the way.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Amon-Ra St. Brown scores a stunning 56-yard TD in Munich for the Detroit Lions

Hutchinson has six sacks so far this year along with 50 pressures, following on from a 2025 season in which he led the team with a career-high 14.5 sacks.

Defensive end Derrick Moore impressed in Hutchinson's absence Sunday with two of the team's four sacks, with Alim McNeill also adding six pressures and increasing his sack tally to 6.5 on the year.

Hutchinson missed 12 games during the 2024 campaign after breaking his tibia and fibula.

Next up for the Lions, who are 7-2, is a meeting with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers before they host the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving.

Sports.title: Patriots QB Maye feared to be out for season with ankle injury
Sports.content:
New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye could miss the remainder of the 2026 NFL season after suffering a suspected ankle fracture in Sunday's loss to the Detroit Lions.

Maye was injured on the opening drive of the game in Munich when he was sacked by Lions pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson, who would himself then also suffer a game and potentially season-ending knee injury by landing awkwardly during his post-sack celebration.

Maye limped to the locker room and was replaced by Tommy DeVito for the remainder of the game as the Patriots lost 35-10 to drop to 5-5 on the year.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Monday that the Patriots fear Maye's injury could keep him out for the rest of the campaign, with ESPN's Adam Schefter adding that it is feared to be a fractured ankle.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Amon-Ra St. Brown scores his second touchdown of the game to extend the Detroit Lions' lead over the New England Patriots

Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said on Sunday that the team would run more tests upon returning to the United States, with Maye staying in Germany overnight to determine whether he required surgery.

The Patriots offense collapsed in Maye's absence as back-up quarterback Tommy DeVito finished 12 of 24 for 81 yards, one touchdown and an interception.

It comes ahead of a difficult run that will see the Patriots follow a meeting with the winless Los Angeles Chargers by facing the Buffalo Bills, Minnesota Vikings and Kansas City Chiefs in a bid to keep their season alive.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Amon-Ra St. Brown scores a stunning 56-yard TD in Munich for the Detroit Lions

Maye has struggled to hit the MVP-contending heights of last season so far this year, and has gone 181 of 276 passing for 2,330 yards and 18 touchdowns to 11 interceptions.

The Patriots were dealt another blow in the fourth quarter when star wide receiver AJ Brown exited with a hamstring injury having only just returned from a two-game absence with a knee issue.

"He wasn't able to finish. We'll see what the severity of that is once we get back and kind of go from there," Vrabel added.

Sports.title: Frank agrees deal in principle to become new Crystal Palace head coach
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace have agreed terms in principle with Thomas Frank to become their next head coach, Sky Sports News understands.

Formalities are now being concluded so Frank can get to work as soon as possible and he is at the Crystal Palace training ground putting the final touches on his appointment.

An announcement is expected on Monday or Tuesday if everything progresses smoothly. Sky Sports News understands the Dane will sign a deal until the summer of 2029.

Frank will replace Pierre Sage, who was dismissed on November 12 following a seventh league defeat of the season to Liverpool.

Frank was the number one choice to take over from Sage and was among a list of names that Palace considered in the summer.

Other candidates that Palace were interested in included Frank Lampard, Sean Dyche, Vitor Pereira, Kim Hellberg, Vitor Matos, Tony Popovic, Jens Berthel Askou and Ole Werner.

Frank's first task is to get Palace out of the relegation zone. They are currently bottom of the Premier League with seven points, two from safety. They face the team in 17th place - Coventry - when the league resumes on Saturday November 21.

Frank's previous experience at Brentford and Spurs

Frank had great success at Brentford during his seven-year spell between 2018 and 2025, getting the Bees into the Premier League and then establishing them as a top-flight club, reaching a ninth-place finish in 2023.

Such was his success with the Bees, Frank was interviewed for the Manchester United and Chelsea jobs in the summer of 2024.

He then moved to Tottenham last season to replace Ange Postecoglou as head coach, but was sacked after less than eight months in charge with the club in 16th place, five points above the relegation zone.

Image: Frank's time at Tottenham was littered with setbacks

Spurs only sealed survival from relegation on the final day of last season, after Igor Tudor and Roberto De Zerbi replaced Frank as head coach.

Frank failed to win over the Tottenham faithful, with his short tenure littered with setbacks, including drinking from a coffee cup which carried the badge of rivals Arsenal.

He is believed to be rejuvenated and refreshed after taking some time away from the game - he has recently returned from Australia.

Who will be part of Frank's coaching staff?

Crystal Palace are working on putting together Frank's coaching team.

They are approaching Chelsea to get Bernardo Cueva. He was a set-piece coach under Frank at Brentford before moving to Chelsea. He would work as a coach at Palace.

The Eagles also want to add Justin Cochrane to the staff. He also worked with Frank at Brentford and is currently part of Thomas Tuchel's England coaching team.

Frank also wants Chris Haslam to join Palace with him. Haslam was a fitness and performance coach for 14 years at Brentford and he was performance and assistant coach under Frank at Tottenham.

Sports.title: French football head Philippe Diallo to fight Infantino for Fifa presidency
Sports.content:
The French Football Federation president, Philippe Diallo, has been confirmed as Uefa’s surprise late choice to run for the Fifa presidency. The search for a Uefa-backed candidate to challenge Gianni Infantino was taken to the wire, with Wednesday the deadline for those planning to contest the Fifa election in March.

“At a meeting held today and chaired by Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin, the national associations represented on the Uefa executive committee and the Fifa council invited Philippe Diallo, president of the French Football Federation (FFF), to stand as a candidate in the Fifa presidential election in March 2027 and unanimously pledged their full support,” a statement said.

Diallo emerged as the favourite after plans to enlist a decorated former player or manager did not reach fruition. Uefa said the 63-year-old had accepted the invitation and that his candidacy was due to be ratified by the FFF on Tuesday.

Diallo strongly criticised Infantino in September, saying he had “seriously damaged the image and unity of football”. He continued: “His initiatives during and after the World Cup have seriously damaged the image and the unity of football. As a result, we believe that trust has been broken.”

It is unclear whether the move to back Diallo will spell the end of the campaign begun by Kozo Tashima, the honorary president of the Japanese Football Association, to challenge Infantino. Tashima, a Fifa council member, has influential backers within Uefa but its hierarchy appears to feel Diallo has a greater chance of wooing voters in other areas of the world.

Quick Guide How do I 

Diallo is expected to win the backing of the vast majority of Uefa’s member associations and there are hopes he could pick up votes from Francophone members of the Confederation of African Football, which has been steadfast in its support for Infantino.

There are concerns that having multiple challengers to Infantino will strengthen his position and play into the hands of a campaign that will present the incumbent as the unity candidate after months of in-fighting.

Concacaf, the North and Central American and Caribbean confederation, has been reluctant to endorse an alternative candidate, despite opposing Infantino, with some federations arguing that a boycott of the election would send the strongest message regarding the need for governance reform.

Diallo getting Uefa’s backing represents a marked departure from its original approach, in which it sought to coalesce behind a more high-profile figure who had made their name on the pitch or in the dugout. There had been late hope that Arsène Wenger, Fifa’s chief of global development, would throw put himself forward, but it would have required a major change of heart from him. Former players such as Mikaël Silvestre and, belatedly, Didier Drogba are understood to have expressed interest that never came to anything.
