Sports.title: Champions League to lose iconic feature as major change made after 26 years
Sports.content:
The famed Champions League star ball is to be remodeled with Nike agreeing a deal to replace Adidas at the start of next season.

German brand Adidas has been the competition’s exclusive match ball supplier since taking over from rivals Nike in 2001.

2 The iconic star design on the Adidas match balls could well be on its way out now that Nike have agreed a four-year rights deal with UEFA Credit: Getty

It was shortly after that, that Adidas introduced the iconic starred design in tandem with the Champions League logo.

However, after 26 years, there is going to be a change made in all UEFA competitions, with Nike taking back the rights.

UEFA make major change to iconic ball

Nike have agreed a four-year deal to become the UEFA match ball provider from the start of the 2027/28 campaign.

Talk of a switch began in April of this year, as a statement was released, revealing that negotiations were ongoing after the the ball deal was put out to tender.

The statement read: “UC3, the joint venture between UEFA and European Football Clubs (EFC) that controls and manages the strategic marketing, sales and delivery of commercial rights for UEFA club competitions, has agreed to enter an exclusive negotiation period with Nike to become the official match ball provider for all UEFA men’s club competitions from 2027 to 2031.

“This decision follows a highly competitive tender process launched in March 2026 by UC3 and its agency, Relevent Football Partners. No further comment will be made in the meantime.”

And following that, Nike have now agreed a deal to take over.

Puma were also reported to have been interested, but the American brand has claimed the exclusive rights to the match ball.

It will be the first time ever that all three UEFA competitions, the Champions League, Europa League and Conference League, have had the same officially ball provider.

Adidas are going to remain at the helm for the rest of the ongoing Champions League campaign.

2 The iconic star design on the Champions League ball is likely to change now that Adidas have lost the supplier rights Credit: Getty

Nike to take over from Adidas

Vice President of Nike, Camilo Andrade is delighted to have got a deal over the line to replace Adidas as the match ball provider.

He said in a statement: “We are excited and honoured to return to the UEFA Champions League, one of football’s biggest stages, after more than two decades, and to bring Nike match balls across UEFA’s men’s club competitions, including all three major competitions for the first time.

"Football is the world’s game, and the ball is at the centre of it, the one thing every player, in every competition, has in common.

"This is a long-term commitment for Nike.

"We will listen to the athlete's voice, push ​the edges of innovation, ​honour the prestige ⁠and tradition of these competitions, and make sure the ball represents the instinct, creativity and joy football brings to billions of fans."

With Nike beginning their deal from the 2027/28 season, the last time the iconic star design of the Adidas match ball will be seen on the pitch on the Champions League will be this year's final.

The showpiece match will take place on June 5, 2027 at the Estadio Metropolitano in Madrid, Spain.

Sports.title: Jurgen Klopp joins movement to oust Gianni Infantino as UEFA’s new FIFA candidate emerges
Sports.content:
Jurgen Klopp believes controversial FIFA president Gianni Infantino has done a worse job than his predecessor Sepp Blatter.

The ex-Liverpool current Germany manager wants to see change made when the FIFA presidential election takes place.

4 Klopp wants to see someone else take over from Infantino as FIFA president, saying the current chief is worse than the controversial Blatter Credit: Getty

Klopp has called for someone who cares about the future of football to step up and take over from Infantino in March.

Infantino will run for another term as FIFA chief, despite a summer full of a huge controversy regarding the World Cup.

His relationship with US President Donald Trump and uncovered plans to sell off the tournament led to huge backlash.

Since then, there have been many calls for him to quit, but he is going to be pursuing an extension to his time as president.

And that's something that Klopp doesn't want to see happen, speaking out about the need for change.

Klopp says Infantino worse than Blatter

"I've been following football for many years," he began. "There are people who are much more knowledgeable about this than I am.

"But I think most people now agree a change would make a lot of sense.

"I didn't think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter, but someone has managed to do just that."

"Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job," Klopp added.

Blatter was FIFA president from 1998 through to 2015 and is known as one of the most controversial figures ever seen in sport.

4 Infantino is going to run for another term as FIFA president despite a summer full of huge controversy and backlash Credit: Getty

4 But Klopp wants him ousted, saying that he has been a worse president than Blatter

He resigned 11 years ago after a huge corruption scandal led to the arrest of multiple FIFA officials at the time.

The Swiss chief was also accused of bribery and vote-buying during his tenure, while he also made many offensive comments.

But Klopp thinks Infantino may have done an even worse job as president, calling for someone who cares to take over.

"There are people who truly care about the future of football - people who aren't driven by financial interests," he said.

"If someone like that were to step up - if someone like that were to become president - I think that would be a significant improvement.

"There are surely people who care deeply about the future of football and have no financial interests in it."

4 French Football Federation preside Diallo is expected to run for FIFA presidency, with the election taking place next year Credit: Getty

New candidate emerges for FIFA presidency

Japan's Football Association president Kozo Tashima is going to run for FIFA presidency against Infantino next year.

Tashima could well be his biggest challenger, but UEFA are also going to have a new candidate in the running.

It won't be legendary Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger, who, despite being tipped to run, has ruled himself out.

Instead, talkSPORT understands that French Football Federation president, Philippe Diallo, is a contender to run for the presidency.

UEFA are hopeful that his candidacy to stand against Infantino is announced within the next 24 hours.

Diallo, who has been the head of the French Football Federation since January 2023, said that Infantino had 'seriously damaged the image and the unity of football' when speaking in September.

The presidential election will take place at the 77th FIFA Congress on March 18, 2017 in Rabat, Morocco.

Sports.title: Man United talks with Mauricio Pochettino alternative soured over £25million contract
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino wasn't the only man contacted by Manchester United to replace Michael Carrick as manager.

The Red Devils also got in touch with former France boss Didier Deschamps - but talks didn't end very well...



2 Man United held brief talks with Deschamps, who left his job as France manager following the World Cup this summer Credit: Getty

talkSPORT understands that negotiations with the World Cup winning coach were only brief and failed to progress.

Pochettino was, in the end, the man brought in to the Old Trafford dugout from the USA, rather than Deschamps.

The ex-Tottenham and Chelsea manager is expected to arrive in Manchester on Thursday and take charge of his first game as boss against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday afternoon.



Meanwhile, Deschamps may prefer a move to Saudi Arabia.

Why did United not pursue Deschamps?

Deschamps was approached by Man United and talks took place, but the Red Devils are said to have been left suspicious.

According to The Athletic, conversations between the two parties ended up with United feeling as if they were being used.



They believed that the legendary French manager and ex-player was looking to gain leverage for a move to Saudi Arabia.

It had been reported in France in September that Deschamps had been offered a three-year contract by Al Ahli.



That contract is said to have been worth around £8.3million per season, so a whopping total payout of £24.9m.

And United were suspicious that talks with the 58-year-old were only ongoing to encourage a big-money Saudi offer.

2 The World Cup-winning manager left United feeling like he was using them as leverage to get a big-money contract in Saudi Arabia Credit: AFP

Who else was in the running for the job?

Deschamps was one of a few contenders to replace Carrick at Man United, albeit a short-lived one.



There were a couple of other big names that were linked with the job, including Antonio Conte.

Conte was linked even before Carrick was sacked, having to put out a statement to deny that he was in talks.

United are said to have shown some interest, however, they opted to not push for the former Chelsea and Spurs boss, going for another ex-manager of the two Premier League giants instead.

Eddie Howe was also in the running, but talkSPORT understands that he wasn't given an interview despite co-owner Jim Ratcliffe making a case for him to come in.



Meanwhile, former Germany manager Julian Nagelsmann was sounded out for the job in October.

A move wasn't pursued though, and eventually Pochettino was the man that United's chiefs settled on.

Sports.title: Simon Jordan fumes at TV reporter’s ‘disingenuous’ interviews with Declan Rice and Thomas Tuchel
Sports.content:
Simon Jordan accused Gabriel Clarke of being 'divisive and disingenuous' over his Declan Rice and Thomas Tuchel interviews.

ITV reporter Clarke has landed himself in hot water for the second time in four months over his post-match England one-on-ones.

6 England reporter Gabriel Clarke was the man to raise the idea of Argentina flashbacks Credit: ITV

The 62-year-old spoke to Declan Rice in the immediate aftermath of The Three Lions' dramatic 3-2 win over world champions Spain.

Thomas Tuchel's men dominated the first hour at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano and deservedly found themselves three goals up.

However, Elliot Anderson's red card in the 63rd minute flipped the momentum and sparked wave after wave of Spanish pressure.

The home side cut the deficit down to one, but England ultimately held on to record their first-ever victory on foreign soil over the team ranked No.1 in the world.

The manner of the Three Lions defending a lead against elite opposition led Clarke to reference the heartbreaking World Cup semi-final exit to Argentina, in which they conceded twice late on.

What did Gabriel Clarke say to Declan Rice?

Asked directly by the journalist, 'Were there flashbacks?' to that match, Rice replied: “Yeah, of course, but it’s football.

“Argentina on that day wasn’t meant to be. For a second, when they [Spain] got their second, you might have thought it was going to go the other way.

“But that resilience, that defending, doing anything for this badge, it’s a massive win.”

6 Tuchel was later presented with a different account of what Rice had said Credit: Getty

Clarke later told England boss Tuchel: “Like, Declan said, there were flashbacks to the Argentina game when you were hanging on...”

Tuchel, who has had to contend with intense scrutiny over his in-game management against Argentina, chuckled at the remark.

Yet talkSPORT's Simon Jordan was among the fans who voiced their annoyance at Clarke attributing the flashbacks quote to Rice, considering he had been the one to raise that idea.

The former Crystal Palace owner took to social media on Sunday evening to write on X: "Gabriel Clarke just did it again."

The latter had previously been held to account by Jordan for the manner of his interview with Jude Bellingham following England's World Cup quarter-final win over Norway in July.

Speaking immediately after Bellingham had played a gruelling extra-time in the Miami heat, Clarke selectively told the Real Madrid star that Tuchel was 'not happy' with how his side had performed, while omitting other parts that the German was happy with.

6 Jordan previously suggested that Bellingham may have reacted differently had he known the full context of Tuchel's response Credit: Getty

Gabriel Clarke 'was intellectually dishonest'

Jordan further expanded on his social media post during a back-and-forth with Jim White and Troy Deeney, live on talkSPORT.

Asked whether he believed Clarke's interview was 'another glaring example of international media spin', the 59-year-old replied: "No, it's a glaring example of that particular journalist.

"He was defended to the hilt by his fellow journalists, yourself, Piers Morgan - anyone who would want to jump up and defend the art of journalism.

"The art of journalism is being balanced, fair, and objective and creating outcomes and trying to extract information, not being divisive and disingenuous and intellectually dishonest.

"He was intellectually dishonest in America, and he was intellectually dishonest, divisive and disingenuous and outright lying to Thomas Tuchel to get a reaction.

6 Jordan admitted he has a 'real problem' with what he perceives as intellectual dishonesty Credit: talkSPORT

He continued on Monday's White and Jordan: "You saw Tuchel's reaction, and I have a real problem with it.

"I've had a problem with it in all walks of life because I think it's really, really poor and it creates division; it creates ill feeling; it degrades relationships, and it brings a divide between the media, and then the media wonder why there's a closed shop, why they get formulaic answers, why nobody wants to say anything.

"We sit here trying to strive for the best version of a conversation to try and hold things to account, to stand up an argument to make it based upon something of solidity, not to create a story, narrate a story and then devise an outcome. It's garbage."

Putting words in Tuchel's mouth?

His talkSPORT colleague, White, who strongly defended Clarke in the summer, said: "It was a game against Norway, if you remember, and Tuchel said that the result was great - Yeah, sure, because England had won - but he wasn't happy with the way that England had played.

"He said that England had been sloppy and that they were lucky, and Clarke put those comments then to Jude Bellingham, who reacted quite rightly to that, in any way Jude saw fit.

"But last night I do believe, and I heard Jeff Stelling on this this morning as well, and I concur with him, it is literally trying to put words in Tuchel's mouth last night off the back of the Declan Rice chat."

6 10-man England beat world champions Spain in a stunning Nations League clash Credit: Getty

Jordan went on to reference a separate interview pre-match, in which Tuchel was angered by his remarks about the racism protocols being 'twisted' when put to his opposite counterpart, Luis de la Fuente.

He added: "If someone shows you what they are, believe them.

"He showed you what he was in the summer, and no one would have it because everyone gangs together and gets their little cronyism, and now he's actually been emboldened by that and did what he did.

"Now it's no big massive thing. It isn't world-changing. It's not some awful illness, but it's a symptom of the press, in the same way that what Thomas Tuchel had done to him by the Spanish journalist is a symptom of the press, which is basically, 'We're not going to report news, we're going to make news.'"

Jordan then further questioned Clarke's motivations behind his relaying of Tuchel's remarks to Bellingham at the World Cup.

He added: "You had the argument which said, 'Tuchel did say that'; yes, we all know he did say that, but he also said a lot of other things.

"And at the time, what was presented to a player who just ran his legs off, that was emotionally overwrought by the outcome of the game, was that the manager wasn't very happy with you.

"So of course you're going to get a negative reaction. The argument was, 'What was the motivation behind it?'

"The journalist is trying to get a rise - [You] wouldn't have it. So now we've seen what the journalist does now."

6 Kane slammed attempts to 'create division' in the England camp in the wake of the Clarke interview with Bellingham Credit: Getty

White appeared to pour cold water on the suggestion that a pattern had emerged, considering the amount of post-match interviews over his career that Gabriel Clark has done.

Watford legend Deeney replied: "Yeah, loads, and I'm not making it about Gabriel Clarke.

"I'm talking about a bigger piece, but you know why you two [White & Jordan] are so successful?

"Because you give an opinion, you have a balanced view, and then you let somebody else decide whether you're right or wrong.

"What journalists are doing now is saying, 'this is the point', repackaging it, not standing there with any integrity and going, 'this is it', because it might generate some clips.

"That's why I think Simon's getting frustrated."

Sports.title: Nations League quarter-final draw: Date, time and teams involved as England await fate
Sports.content:
England will learn their Nations League quarter-final opponents later this week.

Thomas Tuchel’s Three Lions produced a stunning display to beat world champions Spain on Sunday night and top Group A3.

3 Tuchel's England have been brilliant in recent months Credit: Getty

England were brilliant for 60 minutes in Madrid and raced into a 3-0 lead.

But after Elliot Anderson was sent off, Spain got back into it with two goals in ten minutes before James Trafford’s heroics late on secured the win for the visitors.

Following defeat to La Roja in their opening match, England have been perfect since, winning five games in a row and scoring at will.

They are now among the favourites to win the Nations League next summer but first, they must discover who they’ll face in the next round.

Date and time for Nations League draw

The quarter-final draw will be held on Friday, November 20.

It will get underway at 11am UK time and is being held in Nyon, Switzerland.

The draws for all knockout stage and play-off matches across the leagues will be conducted concurrently.

Teams who played each other during the group phase cannot meet in the next round, meaning England will not be drawn against Spain.

The first legs will be played on March 25–27 with the return matches held on March 28–30.

3 England claimed a memorable win over Spain in Madrid Credit: Getty

The Nations League Finals will then be held in June but the host nation for those matches has not yet been confirmed.

talkSPORT will have full coverage from the proceedings in Switzerland.

Listen talkSPORT through the website or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.

Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app, whilst talkSPORT is also available to watch on Samsung TV Plus.

Subscribe to the talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, 

For the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event, visit talkSPORT BET.

Teams involved in Nations League draw

France (Group A1 winner)

Belgium (Group A1 runner-up)

Netherland (Group A2 TBC)

Greece or Germany (Group A2 TBC)

England (Group A3 winner)

Spain (Group A3 runner-up)

Portugal (Group A4 TBC)

Denmark or Norway (Group A4 TBC)

Group A2 will be decided on Monday.

Germany, who face the Netherlands in their final group game, must get a better result than Greece, who host Serbia.

Group A4 will then be settled on Tuesday with Portugal looking to secure top spot away to Wales.

There is then a shootout between Denmark and Norway in Copenhagen for the last quarter-final place.

3 Portugal are the defending champions in the Nations League Credit: Getty

Nations League draw: What has been said?

After topping Group A3 above world champions Spain, England will be among the heavy favourites to claim their first Nations League title.

The Three Lions came third in the inaugural edition of the UEFA tournament but have not featured at the finals since.

Tuchel was asked if England would win the Nations League next summer following their victory in Madrid but simply said: "Now to win the quarter-finals."

He added: "Brilliant performance. Well deserved win. Overall we were the better team. Fantastic performance from start to finish.

"Complete performance. We brought everything to the table. We were brave. Spirit wise, energy wise and also football quality was highest level.

"We deserved it. We focused on our performance and attitude. I can't praise the team high enough for what they put out there.

“We are always ready to push our limits. We had our best result in 60 years [at the World Cup] and we weren't happy with it.

“It's impressive what we did in the last two camps."

England will not play again until their Nations League quarter-final clash with international football put on hold until early spring.

Sports.title: Man United hire private jet to get Mauricio Pochettino straight to Manchester after final USA game in Cincinnati - and new boss is expected to start work as soon as he steps off the plane!
Sports.content:
Man United hire private jet to get Mauricio Pochettino straight to Manchester after final USA game in Cincinnati - and new boss is expected to start work as soon as he steps off the plane!

Manchester United have laid on a private jet for Mauricio Pochettino to fly straight to England on Wednesday morning after he finishes work as US national team coach.

Pochettino’s last game in charge is against Haiti in Cincinnati, which kicks off at midnight on Tuesday UK time. The 54-year-old will speak to the media and say farewell to his players before jumping on a direct flight to Manchester which has been organised by United.

It will enable Pochettino to sleep before he lands in the UK on Wednesday morning ready to go straight to Carrington and start work.

It has emerged that three members of his trusted coaching team – assistant Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez and his son and fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino – have already been allowed to travel to Manchester after the US won the first leg 6-0 in Miami at the weekend.

First-team coach Miguel D’Agostino and fitness coach Silvia Tuya are expected to follow.

Man United have laid on a private jet for Mauricio Pochettino to fly straight to England after he finishes work as US national team coach

Pochettino will take charge of his final match as USA boss in Cincinnati before boarding the direct flight to Manchester

Pochettino's long-time assistant Jesus Perez is one of three trusted staff members who have already been given permission to travel to Manchester

It means that Pochettino’s back-room staff have been able to make a headstart in their preparations for his first game in charge against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday. It is a huge fixture in the calendar for United but even more so because he takes over a team languishing in the relegation zone.

Pochettino will be able to work with the players as they begin reporting back from international duty, and is expected to speak to club media before conducting his pre-match press conference on Friday lunchtime.

Speaking ahead of the second leg against Haiti, Pochettino said: ‘The assistants are ahead. After the game they flew to Manchester and they are there in advance.

‘That was the plan when we agreed terms with Manchester United and with the national team. They are there in advance. They are preparing because Wednesday when we will arrive it’s going to be non-stop, and then start with playing games.’

Sports.title: Astonishing moment darts rivals almost come to blows in 'cheating' row - as furious player tells referee he can 'f***ing p*** off' and match is abandoned
Sports.content:
Astonishing moment darts rivals almost come to blows in 'cheating' row - as furious player tells referee he can 'f***ing p*** off' and match is abandoned

A darts match was abandoned after an astonishing fight broke out between two players on Sunday.

Tempers flared during the WDF Irish Classic clash between Ronan McDonagh and Kieran Lennon, after the latter was accused of deliberately dropping his darts to distract his opponent.

McDonagh, who was leading 3-2 before the remarkable bust-up, became visibly irate as Lennon dropped his darts on three separate occasions.

Fuming, he stepped on one of Lennon's arrows before taking to the oche and landed a score of 100 to take control of the leg.

Lennon took issue with a small group of supporters near the front who loudly cheered McDonagh's ton, telling them to 'shut the f*** up' as he went to throw.

His expletive remark prompted the referee to intervene and he was told to calm down.

A darts match was called off after a furious row between Ronan McDonagh and Kieran Lennon

From today in the WDF Irish Classic, this is incredible



56 seconds of pure cinema 🤣🤣🤣 pic.twitter.com/KaDNjVzbYa — Josh (@joshpearson180) November 15, 2026

The referee also questioned Lennon over his repeated dropping of darts, suspecting potential foul play.

'You don't seem to drop your darts when you're throwing. You've dropped them three times,' the official said.

Lennon furiously responded: 'Are you telling me I'm playing f***ing games, are you?'

After the referee replied, 'Yes I am', Lennon angrily turned his back and let out another sweary remark, exclaiming: 'Well, you can f***ing p*** off!'

He then looked at McDonagh to say: 'Are you happy with that?'

The feisty pair immediately squared up to each other in a furious bust-up as Lennon shoulder-barged McDonagh.

Referees swiftly intervened to break the pair apart, before TV cameras cut away. Footage of the incident quickly went viral on social media, with many fans calling for Lennon to be suspended.

'Kieran Lennon is a disgrace and should be banned from playing competitive darts (and also should be given a good slap),' one fan posted on social media platform X.

Many fans called for Lennon to be banned from playing competitive darts after the incident

'Vile cheat,' another angry fan wrote.

A third added: 'Kieran Lennon needs to be suspended. This is a joke, even if you're not a darts fan, watch this.'

The round of 128 clash was subsequently abandoned and McDonagh, who was winning at that point in the match, was awarded the victory.

Sports.title: Crying Rory McIlroy's pain for his sick father: How golf superstar is driven on by his dad's double-lung transplant - after years of putting personal troubles aside to win
Sports.content:
As Rory McIlroy's voice began to crack, it was hard not to feel that sinking feeling in your stomach.

Here was one of Britain's most popular sportsmen breaking down in a way we had rarely, if ever, seen before.

McIlroy was opening up about his father's serious health problems, revealing that Gerry had undergone a double-lung transplant in September as a 'last resort' after 18 months of ill health.

The Northern Irishman, speaking shortly after lifting a joint-record eighth Race to Dubai title on Sunday, disclosed that he had spent nine days with his father, 67, in intensive care ahead of a recent key tournament in India, and had been unsure whether he would be able to compete.

It was an outpouring of sadness, love and, above all, relief that Gerry was 'recovering well'. McIlroy also recounted a recent visit to his father in Cleveland, Ohio, where he is recuperating.

'I went up to see him before I left for Abu Dhabi a couple of weeks ago, and he said to me, "Rors, go and win me The Race to Dubai",' he said.

Rory McIlroy broke down in tears after opening up on his father Gerry's recent ill health

Gerry (right), pictured with McIlroy and his mum Rosie, has been a huge driver of his career

'So that was, you know, that was in my head for the last two weeks, and I really wanted to do it for him and I know he's in hospital in his hospital bed, and he would have been watching this morning. It was nice to be able to get it done for him.'

McIlroy's decision to speak so openly was all the more poignant given that news of Gerry's ill-health had been kept under wraps.

During the 18-month period that McIlroy referred to, Gerry had continued to make regular appearances at tournaments, most notably when his son retained the Masters title earlier this year.

He has, of course, been a constant presence and driving force in McIlroy's career.

For one, Gerry worked multiple jobs and sacrificed family holidays to help finance his son's golfing ambitions as he grew up in Holywood, Northern Ireland.

He once cut down clubs for him when he was too small to use full-sized ones, acted as his caddie, installed a putting green in their garden – which Daily Mail Sport visited in 2025 – and even built a fence to shield his teenage son from the prying eyes of onlookers as he practised.

Their relationship has always had a competitive edge, too. Ahead of this year's Masters at Augusta, McIlroy took a few weeks off to familiarise himself with the course, with Gerry joining him for one of those rounds.

It makes Sunday's achievements all the more remarkable. While producing some of the finest golf of his career, McIlroy has been privately grappling with the prospect of his father's deteriorating health.

McIlroy is renowned for his determination and mental resilience, but the past 18 months have seen his achievements reach new ground.

Over that period, he has extended his number of consecutive Race to Dubai titles to five, finally completed the career Grand Slam after an 11-year wait by winning the Masters, retained that title this year, and played a pivotal role in Europe's Ryder Cup victory last September.

The personal circumstances behind those achievements offer a glimpse into the pressures McIlroy has been carrying away from the golf course.

McIlroy and his dad celebrate after he retained the Green Jacket at Augusta earlier this year

During McIlroy's childhood, Gerry worked multiple jobs to help finance his son's golf career

They maintain a competitive relationship on the golf course and regularly play rounds together

It is difficult to imagine anything more distressing than worrying about the health of a parent, yet McIlroy has repeatedly displayed an incredible ability to compartmentalise significant personal challenges during his career.

There is an interesting historical parallel and anecdotal evidence, but no suggestion that one necessarily explains the other.

Following his high-profile split from former tennis superstar Caroline Wozniacki in 2014, McIlroy went through a memorable purple patch.

Just weeks after their engagement was called off, he won The Open in July, before he lifted the PGA Championship a month later. It was his first major double and last major success until his Masters breakthrough last year.

McIlroy subsequently surged to world No 1, and later acknowledged his breakup for prompting him to completely involve himself in his golf.

Speaking after the third round of that year's PGA Championship, McIlroy said: 'I've put a little bit more time into my golf and refocused in a way. It's the only thing I have, I've got my family and my friends, but I just immersed myself in my game.

'I've practised hard and I've done all the right things and I'm reaping the rewards. Golf is the number one priority to me and while I'm on this run of form I want to try and keep it going as long as possible.'

An emotional Rory McIlroy speaks about his father after winning an eighth Race to Dubai title. #DPWTC | #RolexSeries pic.twitter.com/JIMjEgy5uF — DP World Tour (@DPWorldTour) November 15, 2026

McIlroy has also maintained his form through other periods of considerable pressure.

This included when he notably became the de facto PGA Tour spokesman during the initial rise of LIV Golf. His role as a player director on the Tour's Policy Board did ultimately take a significant mental and physical toll though, and he eventually resigned.

Perhaps there is a sense that, since finally completing the career Grand Slam, some of the pressure has lifted. Whatever happens next, McIlroy has already secured his place among golf's all-time greats.

For now, though, the hope among golf fans will be a rather simpler one; that Gerry continues to recover and is soon back where he has always been, cheering on his son, just as he has done since those early days in Holywood.

Sports.title: Klopp breaks ranks to savage Infantino: Liverpool legend becomes first boss to turn on FIFA president - who is WORSE than Sepp Blatter - as pressure mounts after World Cup farce
Sports.content:
Jurgen Klopp has called on FIFA's embattled president Gianni Infantino to resign, becoming the first national team manager to do so.

Infantino's reputation took a nosedive after his sycophantic behaviour towards Donald Trump before and during the World Cup - most memorably by awarding him a 'FIFA Peace Prize'.

And it only got worse when his clandestine plot to sell off stakes in the World Cup, a devious scheme which would have banked him millions, was revealed by The Times.

Now Germany manager Klopp has hit out: 'There is now a unanimous consensus that a change would make sense.

'I thought that, after Sepp Blatter, the situation couldn't get any worse - but here we are.

'Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job.

Jurgen Klopp has publicly savaged FIFA president Gianni Infantino, becoming the first national team manager to do so

The Germany manager said Infantino - who tried to sell off stakes in the World Cup to his own benefit - is 'worse' than his predecessor Sepp Blatter

'Without a doubt, there are people who truly care about football and have no financial interests,' the former Liverpool manager said.

Infantino has clung on to his job thus far, surviving a crisis summit in Morocco in August, despite intense and widespread opposition.

A total of 90 nations including all of UEFA's teams rebelled, with threats to boycott FIFA competitions, and Infantino's £3.1billion plan fell apart.

But he still maintained a large swell of support among Africa, Asia, and South America - especially after offering each nation £30million if they supported his plan. His opponents pointed out that he could simply have given money from FIFA's cash reserves of roughly £4.5b.

In the pages of this historic newspaper, football legend Luis Figo wrote that 'Infantino must go' and accused him of 'debasing the office of FIFA President'.

FIFA does not have a history of picking good leaders - Blatter resigned in 2015 amid allegations of corruption, though he was cleared alongside Michel Platini last year.

Infantino now looks well-placed to be re-elected for a fourth term in next March's presidential elections.

The deadline for candidacies to be submitted is November 18.

Philippe Diallo, the French Football Federation president, has agreed to run against Infantino and has the backing of UEFA's executive committee.

'(Diallo has) extensive experience across all levels of the game, having led the organisation representing French professional football clubs, served on the board of the French professional league and within FIFA’s dispute resolution structures, before becoming President of the FFF and a member of the UEFA Executive Committee in 2023,' UEFA said.

Former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega has already announced his intention to be a rival to Infantino.

Kozo Tashima, the honorary president of the Japanese Football Association, is also reportedly set to mount a challenge.

Ex-Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger was touted as a potential challenger but it is understood he told European football’s governing body UEFA that he would not stand.

Sports.title: Thomas Frank closing in on Crystal Palace job as he eyes raid on Chelsea set-piece guru marginalised under Xabi Alonso
Sports.content:
Thomas Frank closing in on Crystal Palace job as he eyes raid on Chelsea set-piece guru marginalised under Xabi Alonso

Thomas Frank is closing in on the Crystal Palace job as the former Brentford and Tottenham manager eyes a raid on Chelsea's backroom staff.

Palace are set to approach Chelsea about Bernardo Cueva, who worked with Frank at Brentford before being poached to become the Blues' set-piece specialist.

Cueva arrived at Chelsea in 2024. However, Daily Mail Sport revealed in the last summer how the 39-year-old Mexican’s role was changing after two seasons of work as Xabi Alonso’s side hired Austin MacPhee from Aston Villa as their new lead on set-plays.

Cueva has not been seen since then, either in training at Cobham or at matches at Stamford Bridge, but continued to work for Chelsea in more of an analytical role behind the scenes.

Club sources stressed at the time that it should not be seen as a demotion, and he is still listed on the first-team staff section of the website under the title ‘technical analyst’.

Palace are set to approach Chelsea about Cueva (right), who worked with Frank at Brentford

But Cueva may now be elevated back to the forefront of football if Palace can strike an agreement to bring him in to join Frank’s backroom staff. It is said Chelsea paid Brentford around £1million in compensation to hire him in 2024 at a time when his stock was high.

Chelsea are due to play Palace in two weeks' time at the Bridge on Wednesday, December 2.

Chelsea previously identified Cueva as a prime candidate for a role which had been vacant since Anthony Barry exited for Bayern Munich. Cueva, who also holds a UEFA Pro Licence through the Football Association, was regarded as an impressive acquisition in 2024.

Before joining Brentford in 2020 and helping them secure promotion to the Premier League, Cueva was at Chivas in his homeland of Mexico. He has also had a role with Norway men's national team.

Sports.title: Romelu Lukaku announces 'bombshell' international retirement: Former Chelsea star, 33, U-turns on his Belgium future - leaving Belgian press stunned
Sports.content:
Romelu Lukaku announces 'bombshell' international retirement: Former Chelsea star, 33, U-turns on his Belgium future - leaving Belgian press stunned

Romelu Lukaku has announced his retirement from international football in a 'bombshell' decision that has left the Belgian press utterly stunned.

The former Chelsea and Manchester United forward, 33, vowed in January that the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament with the Belgium national team, although he now appears to have changed his mind over his future.

Describing his international career as a 'great ride', Lukaku took to social media on Monday morning to break the unexpected news.

'16 years old,' his Instagram statement began. 'For 16 years, I gave everything for the national team. I experienced every possible emotion. I played with fantastic teammates for whom I will always be grateful.

'I want to thank them all. I also want to thank all the coaches for pushing me and giving me the confidence to help the team. It was a great ride, and I enjoyed every moment.

'To the Belgian fans, thank you for the support you have given our team. I am proud to have represented my country at four World Cups and three European Championships. I will never forget those moments. I am at peace with my decision to stop here. It was amazing, it was a joy. I am grateful. Thank you.'

Belgium legend Romelu Lukaku has announced his decision to retire from international football

Lukaku vowed in January that the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament

The Belgian forward has fallen down the pecking order and spent a lot of time on the bench

The Belgian veteran accompanied his post with a gallery of photographs from his storied international career, from his debut against Croatia under Dick Advocaat in 2010 to his final chapter wearing the armband.

Lukaku has captained Belgium on a handful of occasions since 2020, alongside the likes of Kevin De Bruyne and Youri Tielemans.

The 33-year-old forward, who became one of the hottest properties in world football after breaking on the scene at Chelsea, has been a regular fixture in the international set-up for almost two decades.

Spearheading Belgium's golden generation, which included star-studded talents such as De Bruyne, Thibaut Courtois and Eden Hazard, Lukaku chalked up an impressive 135 caps for the international team.

He also retires as Belgium's all-time top scorer on 94 goals, just six shy of a century.

Belgian newspapers were caught out by the shock announcement, which was described as an 'unexpected bombshell' by outlet HLN on Monday.

Lukaku's stock within the international set-up has fallen since he promised the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament in January.

After suffering multiple injury setbacks, he featured at the tournament under Rudi Garcia and continued to play a crucial role, scoring three times as a substitute to guide Belgium to the quarter-finals where they were ultimately stopped by eventual champions Spain.

Since Mark van Bommel's appointment in August, following Garcia's departure at the end of his contract, Lukaku has slipped further down the pecking order, with Charles De Ketelaere preferred to lead the line.

Lukaku, pictured with Kevin De Bruyne, was an unused substitute as Belgium beat Italy 4-1

Axel Witsel sent a heartfelt message to Lukaku on Instagram: 'Thanks for everything, legend'

During Belgium's resounding 4-1 victory over Italy on Sunday, Lukaku warmed the bench as an unused substitute - and wasn't even in the squad to face Turkey three days before.

While Belgium were winning in the second half against the Italians, Lukaku was seen warming up on the sidelines in the hope of featuring for one last time, but unfortunately was not given the opportunity.

VTM NIEUWS anchor Maarten Breckx claimed De Bruyne looked 'concerned' while speaking to Lukaku on the bench, suggesting the former Man City star was unhappy to see his team-mate overlooked.

'When it became clear that he wouldn't be allowed to come on, De Bruyne was talking to him. You could see the concern in his eyes,' he said.

'You could tell, especially from Romelu's attitude, that he was dissatisfied and displeased. He had probably counted on getting some minutes...'

With only Jan Vertonghen and Axel Witsel registering more international caps than Lukaku over their careers, boasting 157 and 140 appearances respectively, Belgium are expected to give the 33-year-old forward a send-off he deserves in the near future.

Witsel, who also called time on his Belgium career this year, was one of the team-mates to celebrate Lukaku's retirement on Instagram.

'Thanks for everything, legend. Thank you, what a journey we've had together,' he wrote.

Sports.title: How Vinicius Jr's lavish summer holiday has left him playing catch up: Real Madrid star admits he 'trained less' while on luxury yacht trip and blames Brazil's early World Cup exit - and 'overwhelming' Arsenal rumours - for sluggish start to the season
Sports.content:
How Vinicius Jr's lavish summer holiday has left him playing catch up: Real Madrid star admits he 'trained less' while on luxury yacht trip and blames Brazil's early World Cup exit - and 'overwhelming' Arsenal rumours - for sluggish start to the season

Vinicius Junior has admitted his lavish summer holiday after Brazil's last-16 World Cup exit is behind his slow start with Real Madrid this season.

And the winger says he felt 'overwhelmed' by the interest of clubs such as Arsenal and insecurity around his contract renewal talks in Madrid.

He has scored one goal and provided three assists in 12 games this season, and amid the criticism, manager Jose Mourinho has even said he should have left this summer to go somewhere he is 'respected'.

Vini Jr said: 'I don’t think I prepared better after the World Cup because the impact of this tournament is very significant for all Brazilians. Losing so early was something we didn’t expect.

'So I took advantage of the holidays to enjoy myself, rest, relax, and spend more time with my family. I ended up training less than in recent years. This may have affected my start to the season.

'Also, regarding my contract renewal, with so many clubs interested last summer, I felt really overwhelmed, as did the situation at Real Madrid. But the season is very long.

Vinicius Junior has admitted his lavish summer holiday is behind his slow start to the season (Instagram: vinijr)

The Real Madrid star spent plenty of time relaxing on yachts as he visited Brazil, Jamaica, Italy, and Dubai (Instagram: vinijr)

The 26-year-old got around via private jet and said that he wants to 'enjoy life' (Instagram: vinijr)

'Maintaining such a high level for so long is always very difficult. I believe only Cristiano Ronaldo and (Lionel) Messi have managed to maintain it for so many years, achieving the same numbers.

'I'm human, I make mistakes often, but I always try to improve. I try to understand more about football, about the day-to-day, but I'm 26 years old and I have to enjoy life a little too.

'Last season, until December, I had only scored five goals. Then, I finished with more than 20 goals, as in all other seasons. I believe I am preparing, evolving, because, in the most decisive moment of the season, I am always there.'

Vini Jr spent part of his summer break in his home city of Sao Goncalo, as well as visiting Jamaica, Italy, and Dubai.

His Instagram was full of pictures of him relaxing on yachts, speeding around on a private jet, and showing off his fashionable outfits.

Arsenal enquired about the Brazilian superstar and reports suggested they were willing to offer him a mammoth £18.5million per season - more than any player at the club.

His contract expires at the end of the season and the club's position is that he must lower his demands if they are to agree an extension. They would still be willing to make him their joint-highest earner alongside Kylian Mbappe.

He has often been a target of racism in Spain - there have been more than 20 such cases of alleged abuse towards him since he joined from Flamengo in 2018. The situation has reduced him to tears before, but he has insisted on staying in La Liga so that he doesn't 'give the racists what they want'.

The winger - who has scored one goal and provided three assists this season - was a target for Arsenal and could leave Madrid in January

The winger is currently serving a four-match ban for pulling Villarreal star Nathan Saliba's hair.

And Mourinho said last month: 'If I were in his shoes, I probably wouldn't be here. I would have forced a move to a country where he'd be respected, but out of loyalty to Real Madrid and love for the club, he stayed.

'He believes things can improve, and he still has that smile. Nothing and no one can take it away from him.

'He's a fantastic guy, and it's easy to get along with him. I spend a few minutes alone with him every day.

'I value him immensely because he always manages to live and survive with a smile.'

Vinicius has been a phenomenon at Real Madrid, scoring 129 times in 388 games from the wing.

But the balance of power shifted to Mbappe when he joined from Paris Saint-Germain in 2024 and talk of his future has increased.

There is a chance that, if Madrid go a third season in a row without significant silverware, they choose to rebuild and go in a different direction.

Moving away from the heavy 'superstar' model has worked for PSG and rewarded them with two Champions League titles in a row.

Vinicius had a tricky summer, being knocked out of the last 16 of the World Cup with Brazil and then missing his pre-season return date as his representatives tried to revive talks over a contract extension.

If an agreement cannot be found on a new deal, Madrid could be open to selling in January, rather than lose him for free next summer.

Last year Al Ahli were willing to offer a €1bn five-year contract offer for the 2024 Ballon d'Or runner-up.

Liverpool were also credited with interest earlier this window but are not in the mix for a player who earns around £520,000 a week.

Sports.title: England's evolution: James Trafford and two other stars chisel their names into the XI, Thomas Tuchel learning from Argentina and Jude Bellingham playing like a captain!
Sports.content:
England's evolution: James Trafford and two other stars chisel their names into the XI, Thomas Tuchel learning from Argentina and Jude Bellingham playing like a captain!

England ended world champions Spain's 43-match unbeaten run in dramatic fashion with a 3-2 win on a memorable night in Madrid.

After Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White scored to establish a three-goal lead, the visitors had to cling on after Elliot Anderson was sent off and the hosts scored twice in the final half hour.

The victory means Thomas Tuchel's side top their Nations League group and it provided a strong riposte to criticism of the manager following the World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina in July.

Our chief football reporter, Craig Hope, was at the Metropolitano Stadium, and here are his FIVE big take-aways…

Lesson learned

It would not have mattered had England conceded a late equaliser. To draw comparison with Argentina in the final half hour is unfair and inaccurate. The World Cup semi-final was 11v11 and so, when we draw conclusions from this game, let us do so on the same terms.

Thomas Tuchel was delighted with his England players as they won 3-2 away in Spain

And what did England do at 11v11 with a 1-0 lead? They attacked. And attacked again. This was a major change (and improvement) and is the reason for such encouragement. They have learnt from a mistake, as much as Tuchel will be loathe to admit.

Mexico would be a fairer parallel, but that was against opposition far inferior to Spain. At 11v10, we could not expect England to stay on the front foot here, as they were until the point of Jarell Quansah's needless mistake and Elliot Anderson's subsequent red card.

And that is cause for great optimism - because this game was not in the balance in any way when the teams were at equal number.

For me, and I don't think this is even close, this was the best performance of Tuchel's reign.

Full (back) of cheer

Do England suddenly have a pair of full backs?! After years of trawling and trialling, here in the most testing of surrounds, Ben White and Lewis Hall inked their names into Tuchel's XI.

We can forgive the concession of two goals when down to 10 men - because with 11, Spain barely looked like getting a shot on target. In fact, they didn't.

Much of that was down to the solidity of the full backs. Then, with backs to the wall, the pair became bricks in the resistance. One White block late on was heroic.

Before that, Hall's best work was not in containing Lamine Yamal, but in emulating him. His dribbles were daring and unnerved Spain, who thought they would spend the game in England's half and with the ball. They did neither early on and Hall was central to that.

White's goal had shades of Carlos Alberto on the overlap, and his England redemption arc felt like it reached completion here. Let him now move on now, for England need him.

No more boos, please, only cheers for White (and Hall).

It's time to stop the boos for Ben White after he starred with Lewis Hall at full back

Kon man!

Ezri Konsa is England's best defender. Build the backline around him.

Tuchel said on the eve of the game that he thought Konsa had grown for the move to Arsenal, and this was proof.

Boy do England need a mature, reliable presence at the heart of their defence. Konsa showed here why he can be that man. He scored a fine goal, which is always a sign of a defender ready to take wider responsibility, but it was his cool interceptions and desperate blocks at the other end that were most reassuring.

What Konsa has to do now is build on this - and a man-of-the-match performance at the home of the world champions is a pretty lofty and solid foundation from which to do so.

Traff's a keeper

Tuchel will, and should, be giving serious thought to keeping James Trafford in England's goal for the Nations League quarter-finals.

Jordan Pickford has done nothing wrong. And yet, it feels like one position the manager wants to evolve - and here was his justification.

Trafford can be a little erratic and immature. What better way to grow, emotionally, than with a series of saves to preserve an historic win. He will feel like a different player, and person, to the one who started this game. Like White and Hall, this felt like a coming-of-age night in an England jersey.

Trafford has all the tools. He might just have used them to chisel his name into that team-sheet.

Goalkeeper feels like one position the manager wants to evolve - and James Trafford starred

Spain's fans are left shocked as Ezri Konsa hails the brilliant Trafford in emphatic fashion

Hail Jude

No goals, but England would not have won this game without Bellingham. He terrified Spain, perhaps given their intimate knowledge of his brilliance.

Beating the best is as much a mental challenge as it is physical, and Bellingham believed. He made England believe, too.

His swagger. His majesty. And yes, his skill. Of all the positives from this win, it is hard to look past Bellingham as the biggest reason for England being able to challenge Spain at the top of the world rankings.

Jude Bellingham played like a captain, dropping into midfield when down to 10 men

He won the corner for the second goal and created the third. He then dropped into midfield when down to 10 and played like a captain.

That is what England need - Bellingham the leader, not Bellingham the individual. He has bought into the collective under Tuchel and, with that, his team-mates are buying into his big ideas. They don't come much bigger than what England achieved here.

Sports.title: Young jockey who smoked friend’s vape containing cannabis suspended for two months
Sports.content:
Young jockey who smoked friend’s vape containing cannabis suspended for two months

Josh Myers, an amateur who had his first rides in 2026, tested positive for the banned substance after riding in a race at Brighton in August

View 2 Images Josh Myers tested positive after riding at Brighton (Image: PA)

A young amateur rider has been suspended for two months after testing positive for cannabis.

‌



‌



Josh Myers made his debut in 2026, competing in five races for trainer Olly Murphy, finishing second and third in two of them. He rode the Murphy-trained The Pug four times and after finishing fifth on the gelding at Brighton was asked to provide a urine sample.

‌



The result confirmed the presence of THC-acid (cannabis), a banned substance, above the allowed threshold level. Myers’ licence was suspended in September on an interim basis pending a disciplinary hearing. The BHA disciplinary panel report said that during interview Myers confirmed that he had used a friend’s vape two days before he was due to ride “not knowing that the vape liquid contained cannabis”.

‌



Top jockey breaks bones in face when crashing onto plastic running rails READ MORE :

DAVID YATES: Willie Mullins cannot dictate the state of the ground at the Cheltenham Festival READ MORE :

The report continued: “Having experienced effects from the vape, he had been told by the friend that the liquid in the vape contained cannabis.

“At the time of being tested, therefore, he knew that there was a risk that cannabis or its metabolites may still have been in his system, but he did not inform the BHA of this risk.”

‌



View 2 Images The rider admitted using a friends vape, not knowing it contained cannabis (Image: Getty Images)

The BHA said a licensed jockey and professional athlete would be expected to get in touch if they had consumed a banned substance, which Myers did not do, “despite being aware prior to the testing being undertaken that he had ingested the cannabis-affected vape”.

Article continues below

Myers acknowledged his inadvertent use of cannabis which led to the positive result while the BHA recognised in mitigation that he had cooperated with the investigation and had no disciplinary record. The testing lab also confirmed the jockey’s account was a “plausible explanation” for the results.

The panel suspended Myers for two months, starting from the date of the interim suspension on September 23.

Sports.title: DARREN LEWIS: 'Let’s believe in our team and live this dream'
Sports.content:
When you go about your life today, dare to dream like me. Because Thomas Tuchel’s England national football team has inspired me to put the depressing old news agenda to one side. That heart-stopping exhilaration of racing into a 3-0 lead against a ­formidable Spain team on Sunday night, has got me daring to dream of this country winning the 2028 European Championship.

Watching Harry Kane, Jude ­Bellingham, Anthony Gordon and Ben White playing the current world ­champions off the pitch, has moved a cynic like me, who has seen England flatter to deceive for over 40 years.

Enduring the nerve-shredding tension of our Three Lions, down to 10 men, holding out against the ferocious attacking talents of the Spanish machine, previously undefeated in 43 matches, stretching across two and a half years, really has inspired me to dare to dream.

View 2 Images Ezri Konsa of England celebrates (Image: Michael Regan/The FA via Getty Images)

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

And you should too. Because if Wales can beat New Zealand in the rugby for the first time in 73 years, then why can’t England dare to dream?

British sport has seen so many hoodoos laid to rest over the last 15 years, including Andy Murray winning Wimbledon, England’s men’s cricket team winning the World Cup in 2019 and England’s Lionesses winning Euro 22.

Why shouldn’t we believe our men’s football team will be next in line? The significance of England’s victory on Sunday shouldn’t be underestimated.

‌



Spain, right now, is a country with the most fearsome footballing talent on the planet. Not only are they world champions, they are the reigning European champions as well. England have a recurring history, soaked in our tears, of either shrinking or surrendering in games against elite countries in high-pressure games.

You and me, we’ve cried together – at home or in fan parks – as our hope has been snuffed out time and again.

Most recently by Croatia at the 2018 World Cup, Italy in the Euro 2020 Final and Argentina in the 2026 World Cup ­semi-final. The fear has grown that Tuchel will never inspire our stars to replicate the aggressive, ­high-intensity football they play with for their clubs. No England head coach has ever managed it on a consistent basis since 66.

But on Sunday night they did. On Sunday night they had jaws dropping all over the world, like the geek sticking one on the school bully on the first day of the new term. On Sunday night, England scored three but would have had six had they converted their chances.

‌



On Sunday night, England produced their most entertaining performance since Terry Venables’ England team demolished the Netherlands 4-1 at Euro 96. So yes, I’m daring to dream. I’m daring to believe we can maintain the new, high bar we have set for our national side.

I’m daring to dream we can take a swagger into Euro 2028, right here in the UK. I’m allowing myself to believe Tuchel will take us over the line after our heartbreak under Gareth Southgate in the finals of the last two Euros.

The veteran naysayers, former footballers and ex-England internationals, broken by over 60 years of frustration and near misses, are already out in force. They are rolling their eyes at the people with the passing interest in ­football and the national side, suddenly off to work with a spring in their step this week.

To them, victory over a superpower like Spain only matters if it comes at a World Cup or a European Championship. They don’t rate the Nations League, an international tournament brought in because so many clubs were fed up of releasing their players to perform in friendlies.

‌



But here’s the thing. Lifting the Nations League will help this particular band of brothers to believe they CAN win something. And if they can do it on a smaller scale, they can win big too. So why shouldn’t we dare to dream? In sport, dominance comes in cycles. It might just be that now is England’s time.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino rival confirmed as UEFA finally put forward FIFA presidential candidate
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino rival confirmed as UEFA finally put forward FIFA presidential candidate

FIFA president Gianni Infantino will run for re-election in March, but a new rival candidate has emerged and received the backing of Europe's football governing body, UEFA

View 2 Images Philippe Diallo is set to run against Gianni Infantino (Image: Baptiste Fernandez/Icon Sport via Getty Images)

UEFA have pledged their 'full support' behind French football chief Philippe Diallo to rival Gianni Infantino at the 2027 FIFA presidential election. Diallo, 63, will stand against Infantino in March, as the current FIFA president bids to win a fourth term in office.

‌



‌



Despite Infantino being a deeply unpopular figure with football fans, especially after his botched World Cup sell-off plan, the Swiss' victory has looked likely to be a formality - thanks to support from Africa, South America and the Middle East - until Diallo emerged. The Frenchman's candidacy will be ratified by the French Football Federation Executive Committee on Tuesday, UEFA say.

‌



A statement issued on Monday read: "At a meeting held today and chaired by UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin, the national associations represented on the UEFA Executive Committee and the FIFA Council invited Philippe Diallo, President of the French Football Federation (FFF), to stand as a candidate in the FIFA presidential election in March 2027 and unanimously pledged their full support.

‌



"Philippe Diallo has extensive experience across all levels of the game, having led the organisation representing French professional football clubs, served on the board of the French professional league and within FIFA's dispute resolution structures, before becoming President of the FFF and a member of the UEFA Executive Committee in 2023.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"Against the backdrop of serious concerns over the direction of FIFA, the national associations called for renewed unity and trust within the global football community.

"They also called for a FIFA that places the development of the game in every region of the world at the heart of its mission, upholds the highest standards of governance and works in close partnership with its member associations, confederations and football stakeholders. They expressed their full confidence in Philippe Diallo to provide the leadership needed to achieve this ambition.

‌



"Philippe Diallo has accepted the invitation to stand. His candidacy is due to be formally ratified by the FFF Executive Committee at its meeting tomorrow."

Will Philippe Diallo beat Gianni Infantino? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images UEFA want Gianni Infantino to be replaced (Image: Nicolò Campo/LightRocket via Getty Images)

Ex-Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger, currently FIFA's chief of global football development, was tipped to be a candidate but recently ruled himself out, like Ceferin himself. Now Diallo has emerged as UEFA's pick and the European football governing body's support will be crucial to his hopes of ousting Infantino.

‌



The presidency isn't a two-horse race, however. Earlier this month, Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima announced his intention to stand against Infantino, who's been in the role since 2016, while ex-Tottenham star Ramon Vega has also thrown his hat into the ring.

Infantino remains the favourite to win the election in which he'll require 106 of the 211 votes available. But Diallo's candidacy is set to make the race far more compelling.

Sports.title: How Arsenal star Ben White went from reviled England exile to match-winner under Thomas Tuchel
Sports.content:
How Arsenal star Ben White went from reviled England exile to match-winner under Thomas Tuchel

Ben White was one of England's heroes in their 3-2 win over world champions Spain, having revived his international career under Thomas Tuchel following a mysterious issue under Gareth Southgate

View 4 Images Ben White has completely turned around his fortunes with England (Image: Chris Brunskill/Getty Images)

There were many individual winners on Sunday night in Madrid - James Trafford and Lewis Hall chief among them - but Ben White's unique story makes his performance in England's remarkable victory stand out above the rest.

‌



Picked to start at right-back by Thomas Tuchel, White was outstanding, providing two telling moments in the second half. First in the 57th minute, he gathered Jude Bellingham's pass and slotted underneath Unai Simon to make it 3-0. Then, with the game on the line in the 84th minute, he made a fantastic recovery tackle to deny Nico Williams a sight of goal.

Both moments were crucial, with his goal turning out to be the difference between the two sides as England celebrated one of their best performances of the Tuchel era.

Right-back has traditionally been viewed as a position of strength for England, who can call upon the likes of Reece James and Trent Alexander-Arnold. Yet after missing the World Cup through injury, White has re-emerged onto the international scene with a point to prove.

In the cauldron of the Metropolitano Stadium, he proved it. The Arsenal defender's words post-match hinted at something deeper than happiness at a job well done. "Just proud to be a part of it," he told ITV. "Glad to be here, for sure."

Black Friday special! Click here to sign up to Mirror+ for just £1 a month!

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

'No reason to doubt his commitment'

White's match-winning performance in Madrid came just days after he was booed onto the pitch at Wembley while replacing Alexander-Arnold in the win over Croatia. It seems that the 29-year-old's commitment to the national team is still not clear in the minds of many match-going fans after he quit the squad during the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.

"I hope it doesn’t happen again. He’s a player of us. Since I’m in charge, he’s desperate to come and to be with the group,” Tuchel said when asked about the boos after the Croatia game.

“Since I’m in charge, I can only judge him on what I see and what I experience, and he’s on the highest level. He can really help us to win football matches, and like I said, he’s part of our group, and we protect our group, and I’m protective of our group, he deserves to be with us.”

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

View 4 Images Ben White scored his second goal in eight caps for England (Image: Sebastian Frej/Getty Images)

Tuchel then added: “He’s a high-quality player, and I honestly don’t even know what happened (when he left the 2022 World Cup squad) and what were the deep reasons and the situation that he left camp. So, like I said, until I’m in charge, there is no reason to doubt his commitment or his passion."

That was the message from Declan Rice when he spoke before the Spain match. “Ben has moved on from what's happened in the past, he's totally focused on playing for England. When he's been fit and available he's constantly put himself forward to play for England," White's Arsenal teammate said.

“He loves being here, it's not like he doesn't like being here, he loves playing for England, loves being around the lads."

Shadow of Qatar

There is no question over whether White is good enough to merit a place in England's squad. The question - for some at least - is whether somebody who ruled himself out of contention in the past is worthy of reconciliation now.

The issue is the mysterious nature of his withdrawal back in 2022. England said it was for personal reasons, but reports later emerged of a falling out between the Arsenal defender and Gareth Southgate's assistant manager - and Michael Carrick's recent assistant at Manchester United - Steve Holland on the training pitch in Qatar.

White refused to be considered for selection while Southgate was still in charge and has only been welcomed back into the fold since Tuchel took over. The real reason behind his international exile isn't about to be made public.

View 4 Images Ben White withdrew from England contention in 2022

"Obviously people don't know the full story, because I [have] never said anything and I won't put anyone under the bus or share any of that," White told BBC Radio 5 Live last week. "I think that is probably the best way."

Rice appears to be frustrated by the perception surrounding his team-mate. "It's so long ago now, it's nearly five years and it doesn't need to keep getting brought up," he said. "We need to look forward to the future and what Ben White is going to do in an England shirt, that's the most important thing.

“It's a pointless conversation, Ben has moved on, no-one talks about it around the dinner table, no-one speaks about it in the pool, we just play football and do what we need to do.”

Letting football do the talking

View 4 Images Thomas Tuchel has brought Ben White back into the England fold (Image: Jacques Feeney/Offside via Getty Images)

It was a knee injury which prevented White from going to the World Cup in the summer. He's come back firing this season for Arsenal, providing three assists in seven Premier League appearances, and has a great chance of becoming Tuchel's first-choice right-back.

With Chelsea's James struggling with injuries and Alexander-Arnold not getting regular game time under Jose Mourinho at Real Madrid, Tuchel will value White's performances for title-chasing Arsenal.

White's athletic ability makes him a threat on the overlap - as he showed in scoring on Sunday - but it also makes him a perfect match for England's man-to-man press, while his aggressiveness is also a valuable characteristic.

The former Brighton and Leeds famously said he doesn't watch much football in his own time. He is clearly not fond of speaking to the media. But if he lets his football do the talking, then his international career will have plenty more years left to run.

Sports.title: Top jockey breaks bones in face when crashing onto plastic running rails
Sports.content:
Top jockey breaks bones in face when crashing onto plastic running rails

Ray Dawson was taken to hospital after the incident during a race in Abu Dhabi when he was unshipped from his mount and was thrown onto the rails

View 2 Images Ray Dawson falls onto the rail (Image: TurfeEunapolis/X)

Top jockey Ray Dawson has broken bones in his face after falling onto the rails during a race in Abu Dhabi.

‌



‌



The 33-year-old, who rides for Newmarket trainer Roger Varian in Britain, spends his winters working in the UAE. He has ridden four winners from 35 rides of the 2026-27 campaign and was engaged at Jebel Ali in Abu Dhabi last Thursday.

‌



Dawson was aboard Royal Officer, trained by Bhupat Seemar, in the sixth race on the card when his mount was hampered over 1f out. Replays of the incident showed Dawson being unseated from Royal Officer and landing stomach first onto the top of the running rail.

‌



DAVID YATES: Willie Mullins cannot dictate the state of the ground at the Cheltenham Festival READ MORE :

The rail bends as it breaks his fall and then propels the jockey back onto the turf.

The stewards report said the incident occurred after Royal Officer was “tightened for room, stumbled and dislodged its rider. A post-race veterinary examination revealed the gelding to be lame in the left-fore leg”.

‌



View 2 Images Ray Dawson: suffered facial fractures (Image: PA)

A further notice said: “Jockey R Dawson was transported to hospital for further examination after a race fall during the race and was deemed unsuitable to fulfil his remaining engagements for today’s event.

‌



“The Stewards adjourned an inquiry to a date to be set regarding the race fall involving ROYAL OFFICER (IRE)(R Dawson) as R Dawson was transported to hospital for further examination.”

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Article continues below

Footage of the incident was shared on social media with the comment, “The importance of proper safety fences for the safety of jockeys and horses at racetracks.”

Replying to the post, Dawson said: “Unfortunately I did suffer some broken bones in my face .. the rails helped soften the blow for sure and the plastic material is incredibly important for safety to horses and jockeys . .”
