World.title: The season of the familiar spirits is once again upon us, By Austin Emaduku
World.content:
The most prevalent familiar spirits of this election cycle are the economy and hardship in the land. I can only urge rational people to take a step back from the frenzy of the gathering mob, and calmly appraise and analyse the issues. Given the nature of Nigeria’s non-ideological politics, I can not see any politician or party on the horizon worth burning down the country or shedding blood of another for.

Those unacquainted with my conception of familiar spirits should learn about it from page 228 of my literary/essay collection Colours of My Mind or, better still, Google my essay “The Familiar Spirits of the Nigerian Nation.”

The concept of “familiar spirits” is used metaphorically in that work to describe “the recurring, deeply ingrained structural flaws, sentiments, and destructive patterns that continuously manipulate, deceive, and stall the country’s progress.”

The national malaise that heightens every national election cycle is once again upon us and the sorcerers are abroad conjuring all manner of spirits to “manipulate and deceive.” The prevalent spirit conjured often depends on what the sorcerers determine best mirrors the national mood at any particular point in time and not necessarily the best national interest. Note that I said “national mood” and not “national interest” because the national mood is not necessarily in the best national interest, but what the sorcerers can easily sell.

In one season it can be the spirit of tribe or ethnicity. In another, the spirit of religion. In another, the spirit of money or concerns of the youth, or of anger against past political losses or betrayals, beautifully crafted in populist political language. The costume changes but the conjuring is the same. Given the nature of democracy wherein the opinion of one idiot is equal to those of three experts. And in a season in which the activities of sorcerers and mediums often shape public conversation, with the propensity towards mass hysteria and herd instinct, one can only advocate a calm and rational approach to issues.

I am particularly wary of those whose political analyses are laced with insults, hatred and intolerance towards opposing views of others. Democracy is a contestation of ideas. Support your candidate and let others support theirs. No one is a devil for making their political choices. We must discourage the growing culture of conducting political language with courses and insults. We cannot elevate hate speech as a strategy for winning elections.

Religion and ethnicity used to be the most effectively deployed familiar spirits in the past, but religion seems to have lost its national potency and allure in this election cycle, most probably because the myth of the dangers of the same religion ticket, as represented by the current Muslim/Muslim ticket of the present national administration, has not led to the extinguishing of the other religion or the dipping of the Qur’an into the Atlantic Ocean, as we were all made to believe. The proponents of the religious ticket/candidacy are often not driven by administrative competence but by the religious faith or beliefs of the candidate. While religion may still play some role in the backwoods of regional politics, its national potency has been greatly diminished in this election cycle.

Ethnicity, on the other hand, is still very much in currency. Hopefully, a day will come when we will put this to the test and also burst the myth of its fear of hegemony and threat to national cohesion.

The most prevalent familiar spirits of this election cycle are the economy and hardship in the land. I can only urge rational people to take a step back from the frenzy of the gathering mob, and calmly appraise and analyse the issues. Given the nature of Nigeria’s non-ideological politics, I can not see any politician or party on the horizon worth burning down the country or shedding blood of another for. I have my political preference, but that has not stopped the famous saying of the late sage Bola Ige about the “five fingers of a leprous hand” from coming to mind.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

I am particularly wary of those whose political analyses are laced with insults, hatred and intolerance towards opposing views of others. Democracy is a contestation of ideas. Support your candidate and let others support theirs. No one is a devil for making their political choices. We must discourage the growing culture of conducting political language with courses and insults. We cannot elevate hate speech as a strategy for winning elections.

In my neck of the woods, political commentary on this space has recently ridiculously descended to the low level of invoking local gods and ancestral courses on opposition political supporters. This is how low we have fallen! Wishing death and misfortune upon your kin and kit for their political choices!

To the youths who are often at the receiving end of the outcomes of these inciting statements, my advice is this: be kind with your language while campaigning for your candidates; do not procure enemies for yourselves in the course of supporting your paymasters. The internet never forgets. Your digital footprint will remain there and may return to haunt you tomorrow. Most importantly, maintain your humanity and sanity. Do not burst your bile or an artery in pursuit of stomach infrastructure.

In my neck of the woods, political commentary on this space has recently ridiculously descended to the low level of invoking local gods and ancestral courses on opposition political supporters. This is how low we have fallen! Wishing death and misfortune upon your kin and kit for their political choices! Well, our people say na from all corners people dey enter to full market.

This season, too, will pass and Nigeria will continue to exist.

Austin Emaduku, the author of Colours of My Mind, wrote from Egini, Udu Local Government Area, Delta State.

World.title: Nigeria’s inflation falls to 14.06% in October – NBS
World.content:
Nigeria’s headline inflation rate declined further to 14.06 per cent in October, extending the slowdown in annual price increases recorded in recent months, according to the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS).

The latest figure represents a 0.57 percentage-point decline from the 14.63 per cent recorded in September and a substantial drop from the 18.97 per cent recorded in October 2025.

The statistics agency disclosed this in its October 2026 Consumer Price Index (CPI) figures released on Monday.

On a month-on-month basis, headline inflation stood at 0.43 per cent in October, compared with 0.06 per cent in September, indicating that average prices increased at a faster rate during the month, although the pace remained relatively low.

The latest figures extend the downward trend in annual inflation. PREMIUM TIMES had reported that headline inflation fell to 14.63 per cent in September from 15.39 per cent in August, while monthly inflation slowed sharply to 0.06 per cent.

The October report shows that annual inflation continued to moderate, even as monthly price increases picked up slightly.

Food inflation stood at 19.13 per cent year-on-year in October, down from 19.59 per cent in September and 16.30 per cent in October 2025.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

On a month-on-month basis, food inflation was -0.75 per cent in October, compared with -1.55 per cent in September.

The negative monthly rate indicates that average prices of food items in the CPI basket declined between September and October, although the decrease was smaller than the fall recorded in the preceding month.

The movement comes after food prices also declined monthly in September, when food inflation stood at -1.55 per cent following a rise of 1.02 per cent in August.

Despite the monthly reductions, the annual figure shows that food prices remained substantially higher than they were a year earlier.

This distinction is important for households, particularly low-income families that spend a large share of their earnings on food. A decline in monthly food inflation does not necessarily mean that prices have returned to earlier levels or that all food items have become cheaper.

The October figures suggest that the pace of annual food price increases has slowed, while average food prices recorded another monthly decline.

Urban inflation remains higher than rural rate

The NBS data also showed that annual inflation continued to moderate in both urban and rural areas.

Urban inflation stood at 14.84 per cent year-on-year in October, down from 18.73 per cent in the corresponding month of 2025.

On a month-on-month basis, urban inflation increased to 0.43 per cent in October from 0.53 per cent in September.

Rural inflation was lower at 12.17 per cent year-on-year, compared with 18.60 per cent in October 2025.

The monthly rural inflation rate stood at 0.18 per cent in October, reversing the -0.89 per cent recorded in September.

The figures show that annual price increases remained higher in urban areas than in rural areas, while average prices in both categories rose between September and October.

Core inflation, which excludes farm produce and energy prices, stood at 10.78 per cent year-on-year in October, down from 21.25 per cent in October 2025.

On a month-on-month basis, core inflation was -0.53 per cent in October, compared with 1.11 per cent in September.

The monthly decline indicates that average prices within the core inflation basket fell during the period, after increasing in September.

What the figures mean

The October data point to a continued slowdown in Nigeria’s annual inflation rate, with headline inflation declining for another month and annual food inflation also moderating.

However, the increase in monthly headline inflation from 0.06 per cent in September to 0.43 per cent in October suggests that prices rose at a faster pace within the month.

The negative monthly food inflation rate offers some relief, but the annual food inflation figure of 19.13 per cent indicates that food remains considerably more expensive than it was a year earlier.

Inflation measures the rate at which prices change over time. A declining inflation rate means prices are increasing more slowly, not necessarily that the cost of living has fallen.

For households still struggling with the cost of food, transport and other necessities, the distinction between slower price increases and actual reductions in prices remains significant.

World.title: Actress Olatunde Ogunsola-Oluyemi, daughter of theatre icon Ishow Pepper, dies
World.content:
Actress, screenwriter and cultural researcher Olatunde Ogunsola-Oluyemi has died.

Ogunsola-Oluyemi, who worked across film, theatre and cultural education, was also a Yoruba and English translator and Ewi performer. Her screen credits included Èjá and Okoto The Series.

Her colleague, Wumi Olabimtan, announced her death in an Instagram tribute on Monday. She did not disclose the actress’s age, cause of death or the circumstances surrounding it.

Ogunsola-Oluyemi was the daughter of the late Yoruba theatre pioneer Timothy Olusola Ishola Ogunsola, popularly known as Ishow Pepper, who died on 28 December 1992.

She built her career on a family legacy rooted in the formative years of Yoruba travelling theatre while establishing herself as a performer, writer, translator and researcher.

Career and theatre legacy

Ogunsola-Oluyemi contributed to screen productions in Yoruba and English and helped preserve and interpret Yoruba language and performance traditions.

The late actress announced on 5 February that Olabisi Onabanjo University (OOU) awarded her a PhD in Educational Technology on 31 January 2026.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

She was married to Ayo Oluyemi, a filmmaker and theatre practitioner who chairs the Ibadan Metropolitan College of Theatre Arts and Cinematography (IMECTAC).

Mr Oluyemi had previously credited his wife’s background and experience as the daughter of a Yoruba theatre pioneer with contributing to the institution’s development and continuity.

IMECTAC, formerly known as the Oluyemi Centre for Theatre and Allied Arts, offers training in acting for stage and screen, screenwriting, cinematography and videography. The institution says it has graduated more than 200 students.

Colleague pays tribute

In her tribute, Ms Olabimtan described the deceased as a close friend, sister and confidant whose talent and warmth left a lasting impression on those around her.

“Your final bow came far too soon, egbon mi, ore mi, alabaro mi. Today, I have to say goodbye to someone who held a massive piece of my heart,” she wrote.

“The incredibly beautiful and talented Aunty Tunde. You were one of the dearest, closest souls to me.

“Your laughter was a sanctuary, your talent was effortless, and your heart was completely pure. Mummy Iwa, as I fondly call you, you didn’t just walk through life; you lit it up with your art, your wisdom and your open heart.”

Ms Olabimtan said Ogunsola-Oluyemi’s death had left a void in her life and the entertainment industry.

“The stage of this world feels so empty without you, Dr Olatunde Oluyemi (née Ishow Pepper). Rest peacefully in the arms of the Almighty God.

“You will forever remain the leading lady of my heart. My heart breaks as I say goodbye to you. Every memory we shared stays forever. Sleep well, my beautiful star,” she added.

Several actors, including Ayo Olaiya, Muyiwa Ademola, Muyideen “Lala” Oladapo and Fathia Balogun, among others, took to Instagram to pay tribute to the late actress.

Ademola described Ogunsola-Oluyemi’s death as sad and prayed for her soul to rest in perfect peace.

“May her soul continue to rest in perfect peace. Such sad news, but there’s nothing we can do. The Almighty protects what she left behind. Her husband, children, mother and everyone else”, he wrote.

Meanwhile, Lala, Olaiya and Balogun wrote, “May her soul rest in peace.”

World.title: Sanwo-Olu hails Lagos grassroots talents after Flamingos’ World Cup victory
World.content:
Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu has highlighted the contribution of the state’s grassroots football structures to Nigeria’s historic victory at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup, noting that several members of the Flamingos squad developed through Team Lagos and FC Robo.

Mr Sanwo-Olu made the observation after hosting the victorious team at Lagos House, Marina, on Sunday.

In a Facebook post after the reception, the governor said the players’ success reflected the importance of identifying and supporting young talents across communities.

“We are particularly proud that quite a number of the players are from Team Lagos while some also came through FC Robo, a club close to our hearts and one we have supported over the years,” he said.

He added that the players’ journeys from communities such as Ajegunle and Mushin to the global stage demonstrated the depth of football talent in Lagos.

“From Ajegunle and Mushin to the world stage, these girls have shown that talent knows no boundaries. They have made Lagos proud, and they have given the entire country every reason to celebrate,” Mr Sanwo-Olu said.

The Director-General of the Lagos State Sports Commission, Lekan Fatodu, also highlighted the presence of Team Lagos products in the squad following the team’s success.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The commission’s grassroots sports development efforts include identifying promising athletes in schools and communities and supporting their progression.

From Lagos communities to world champions

The Flamingos’ triumph in Morocco followed a remarkable campaign in which the team recovered from an opening defeat to Poland to win the title.

Nigeria lost 2-1 to Poland in their first group match but responded with a 2-0 victory over Puerto Rico before defeating defending champions Korea DPR 3-1 to advance to the knockout stage.

They subsequently beat Mexico 2-1 in the round of 16 and edged Venezuela 1-0 in the quarter-finals, with Azeezat Oduntan scoring a late penalty.

The team then defeated Brazil 3-1 in the semi-finals to reach its first final in the competition.

In the final played in Rabat on 7 November, Nigeria beat Japan 2-1, with Awawu Bashiru opening the scoring in the 39th minute before Oluebube Umejiaku doubled the advantage two minutes into the second half. Japan pulled one back through Fuki Ito in the 80th minute, but the Flamingos held on to secure the trophy.

The victory made Nigeria the first African country to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup and the first African women’s team to claim a FIFA world title at any age level.

Lagos rewards victorious team

At the reception, Mr Sanwo-Olu urged the players to remain focused on their development, saying their achievement should encourage them to continue improving.

The reception followed the Lagos State Government’s announcement of a ₦300 million reward package for the players and members of the technical crew. Each beneficiary will receive ₦10 million, while the players will also receive iPhones and headphones.

The reward adds to the incentives announced by the Federal Government and the Senate following the team’s historic achievement.

For Lagos, the Flamingos’ success has brought renewed attention to the role of grassroots football structures in identifying and developing young female players.

World.title: Popular Ibadan cleric revisits 2011 prophecy, warns Nigerian leaders
World.content:
Popular Ibadan cleric Solomon Moses Oni Mustapha, popularly known as Baba Sebioba, has warned Nigerian political leaders against taking renewed opportunities to govern for granted.

In a statement sent to PREMIUM TIMES on Monday, Mr Mustapha said an additional term should allow political leaders to correct previous mistakes, fulfil their responsibilities, and serve citizens better.

“An opportunity granted through grace should not be treated as a licence for continued actions that disregard the purpose for which such an opportunity was given,” the statement read.

In delivering the warning, the cleric revisited a prophecy he reportedly made before Nigeria’s 2011 presidential election concerning the emergence of Goodluck Jonathan as president.

Baba Sebioba

Mr Mustapha is the founder and general overseer of the Seed of Christ Golden Church Worldwide.

He is known for his religious pronouncements on elections, security, governance and other national issues, often accompanied by calls for prayer and national reflection.

The cleric has previously commented on flooding, insecurity and Nigeria’s electoral politics. Earlier in 2026, he said he had received prophetic insights about the 2027 general elections but was not prepared to reveal the details.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The latest statement cited an archived newspaper report published on 14 March 2011 that reportedly documented his prediction of Mr Jonathan’s eventual electoral victory.

According to the account, Mr Mustapha also called for prayers and fasting over the country’s political direction. He urged political leaders, particularly those in the South-west, to seek divine intervention.

Mr Jonathan subsequently won the presidential election held in April 2011.

Fresh warning

In his latest message, Mr Mustapha focused on what he described as the responsibility that comes with a “second four years of governance.”

The statement read: “An additional opportunity to govern should ordinarily provide room for reflection, improved leadership, better policies and a renewed commitment to public service.”

It added that a renewed mandate should not automatically be interpreted as an endorsement of every action taken during an administration’s first term.

Although Mr Mustapha did not identify a particular government, his message was directed broadly at political leaders and other public officials entrusted with authority.

“Grace should be respected rather than abused,” the statement read.

The cleric also urged leaders to recognise that their performance would ultimately be assessed through their decisions, fulfilled promises and the impact of their policies on citizens.

“Political leadership is not defined solely by the number of years spent in office, but also by the decisions taken, the promises fulfilled and the impact of those decisions on the people,” the statement added.

Accountability

As Nigeria approaches the 2027 general elections, Mr Mustapha called on the president, governors, legislators, political appointees and other public officials to reflect on their use of power.

He also urged religious leaders, traditional rulers, civil society organisations and Nigerians to promote responsible leadership, peaceful engagement and national reflection.

“The call for people to hear the message should be understood within the context of its warning about the responsibility that comes with power and the consequences of taking opportunities for granted,” it read.

The cleric concluded the warning with the biblical expression: “Whosoever has ears, let him hear.”

He maintained that the statement presents the prophecy as a caution to political leaders rather than a mere comment on political developments.

The cleric advised political leaders to regard another chance to govern as a privilege that demands gratitude and accountable service, not an automatic right.

“It places the responsibility of listening and reflecting on those to whom the message is directed, particularly individuals who occupy positions where their decisions affect the lives of millions.”

World.title: Lagos PDP candidate promises tax exemption for teachers, doctors
World.content:
By Cynthia Alo & Kafayat Kokumo

The Lagos State governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Adedeji Doherty, has promised to exempt teachers and doctors from paying taxes if elected governor, saying his administration would deploy increased federal allocations to improve healthcare, education and residents’ welfare.

Doherty made the pledge during an interview on Channels Television on Monday, where he also proposed a special tax card that would allow residents unable to afford the existing tax burden to pay N10,000 annually and enjoy subsidies on drugs and transportation.

He said his proposed policy would ensure that increased revenue accruing to the state translated into direct benefits for residents.

“When I am governor, I will definitely transfer these palliatives, these subsidies to my people. For instance, the doctors will not pay tax. For instance, the teachers will not pay tax. Those two people will not pay tax,” he said.

Explaining the proposed tax card, Doherty said residents who could not afford to pay N50,000 annually would be allowed to pay N10,000 and benefit from subsidised medication and transportation.

“Out of this N250 billion plus, I will transfer it into cards, whereby for those that cannot pay N50,000 per year in tax, I will create a card that you can pay N10,000 per year in tax, but you will get a subsidy in your drugs and you will get a subsidy in your transportation.

“This is giving money back to the people of Lagos State because I have it. Mr President has given it to me and I am giving it to you,” he said.

The PDP candidate also promised to introduce free education, arguing that the resources available to Lagos State would enable his administration to implement the policy.

He justified his proposed tax exemption for doctors by citing an alleged shortage of medical personnel in the state, claiming that Lagos had about 3,000 doctors against an estimated requirement of 15,000.

“We need close to about 15,000 doctors in Lagos State as we speak, but right now we have only about 3,000. So, if 3,000 doctors are not paying tax, please give me a break,” he said.

Doherty also promised improved welfare packages, including comfortable accommodation, discounted food and car loans, to encourage medical professionals practising abroad to return to Lagos.

“I want those experts in London, in America, in Germany, in Hungary. I want them to come back to Lagos and feel like they are even special. I will make them special, just like the teachers,” he said.

He described teachers as critical to the future of the state, stressing the need to provide them with adequate training and support to prepare children for leadership and professional responsibilities.

On his campaign activities, the governorship candidate condemned attacks on political materials, alleging that some individuals he described as area boys had pulled down his campaign posters around Oregun and the Third Mainland Bridge.

He said his Director-General had reported the incident to the police, adding that he planned to visit the Department of State Services (DSS) after the television interview.

Doherty also expressed support for President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms but disagreed with the manner in which the Lagos State Government was implementing the President’s agenda.

He urged state governors to ensure that residents benefited from increased federal allocations, while advocating investments in the power and manufacturing sectors to stimulate economic growth.

World.title: Ondo: Supreme Court fixes Wednesday to hear appeal over APC Reps ticket
World.content:
By Ikechukwu Nnochiri

ABUJA: The Supreme Court has fixed Wednesday to hear an appeal over the dispute surrounding the All Progressives Congress (APC) House of Representatives ticket for the Owo/Ose Federal Constituency in Ondo State ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The appeal seeks to set aside the October 9 judgment of the Abuja Division of the Court of Appeal, which directed the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to recognise Mr. Abdulghani Arobo as the authentic candidate of the APC for the election.

In processes filed before the apex court, the appellant, Mr. Oluwatimehin Adelegbe, insisted that he won the primary election the APC conducted in the constituency on May 16 and was duly nominated as the party’s candidate for the seat.

The appellant faulted the Court of Appeal’s refusal of his application to tender evidence to prove that he won the primary and that his name was uploaded by the APC to INEC’s portal as the party’s candidate for the House of Reps election.

Listed as respondents in the appeal are Arobo, the APC and INEC.

According to the appellant, the appellate court, in deciding the appeal marked CA/ABJ/CV/1235/2026, wrongly affirmed an earlier verdict that Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court in Abuja delivered on August 5, which recognised Arobo as the APC flag bearer.

In the 18 grounds of appeal filed before the Supreme Court through his team of lawyers led by Mr. Joseph Daudu, SAN, Adelegbe contended that the concurrent judgments of the lower courts occasioned a miscarriage of justice against him.

Alleging that he was denied a fair hearing, the appellant told the apex court that he was not joined as an interested party in the suit that led to his removal as the APC candidate for the election.

The appellant further contended that the refusal of the court to grant a motion on notice, brought pursuant to Order 4 Rule 2 of the Court of Appeal Rules 2021, for leave to adduce fresh or additional evidence, proved fatal to his case.

He identified the additional evidence sought to be tendered as statutory public documents, which included the APC’s official candidate forwarding letter dated 26 June 2026; his Form EC9 affidavit; the INEC Candidate Nomination Portal (ICNP) submission receipt dated 11 July 2026; and a certified true copy (CTC) of the official APC Election Committee result sheet, showing that he polled 13,094 votes.

Adelegbe maintained that the essence of the application was that, had Arobo joined him as a party in the suit leading to the High Court judgment, he would have provided sufficient evidence showing that he was the person declared the winner of the APC primary for the Owo/Ose Federal Constituency.

He argued that, by Order 4 Rule 2 of the Court of Appeal Rules 2021, the appellate court has full discretionary power to receive further evidence on questions of fact, particularly where such evidence could not have been produced at the trial court as a result of his exclusion, through no fault of his, or where special grounds exist.

Besides, while accusing Arobo of deliberately excluding him from the proceedings before the trial court, the appellant contended that unlawful exclusion and non-joinder of a necessary and indispensable party at the lower court constitute the highest threshold of “special grounds” under Order 4 Rule 2, since a party who was unaware of a proceeding cannot be faulted for not tendering documents during a trial from which he was excluded.

On another ground of appeal, he argued that the Court of Appeal erred in law and reached a perverse decision when it affirmed the trial court’s judgment, which was delivered in total breach of Section 36(1) of the 1999 Constitution and without joining him as an indispensable and necessary party, upon the erroneous finding that no final declaration or return had been made in his favour.

He said the appellate court erred in law when it held that he was bound by the trial court’s proceedings under the doctrine of “standing by” and that his interests were adequately represented and defended by the APC.

It was further the position of the appellant that the doctrine of estoppel by “standing by” strictly requires clear proof that the non-party had full, actual notice of the institution and pendency of the suit, possessed a direct interest in the subject matter, and consciously made an informed election to stand by and allow others to fight his cause on his behalf.

Adelegbe noted that he deposed in his uncontroverted affidavits that he was never served with any documents relating to the suit filed by Arobo, on which the trial court’s judgment was based, and hence he “had absolutely no actual or constructive knowledge of the suit until after final judgment was delivered behind his back on 5th August 2026, thereby making it legally impossible to invoke the doctrine of ‘standing by’ against him.”

He added that the Court of Appeal erred in law when it held that Arobo was justified in bypassing the final appellate organ of the APC, the National Working Committee (NWC), after waiting 11 days.

The appellant also faulted the appellate court for holding that Arobo’s suit at the trial court was properly commenced by originating summons under Paragraph 7(1) of the Pre-Election Practice Directions 2026, despite grave, hostile and conflicting factual allegations raised in the suit.

He is, therefore, praying the apex court to issue an order affirming his candidacy and directing INEC to recognise, publish and maintain his name, profile and nomination particulars as the duly nominated candidate of the APC for the constituency.

World.title: Only four MDAs score above 50% in fiscal responsibility index
World.content:
…FRC raises annual surplus remittances from N300m to N2trn

By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief

Only four Federal Government Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) scored above 50 per cent in the 2026 Fiscal Responsibility Index (FRI), raising concerns over compliance with statutory public financial management requirements.

The four MDAs are the Federal Ministries of Water Resources; Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy; Finance; and Housing and Urban Development.

The Acting Chairman of the Fiscal Responsibility Commission (FRC), Mr Charles Abana, disclosed this on Monday in Abuja while presenting the 2026 Fiscal Responsibility Index report.

He called on MDAs to improve compliance with the provisions of the Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2007, stressing the need to strengthen accountability and transparency in public financial management.

Under Pillar I of the assessment, which focuses on policy-based budgeting, the Ministry of Finance topped the list with 90 per cent, followed by Water Resources with 75 per cent, Health with 70.1 per cent, Innovation and Science Technology with 70 per cent, and Defence with 68 per cent.

Other ministries recorded lower scores, including Aviation with 28.2 per cent, Information with 36.7 per cent, Justice with 40 per cent, Police Affairs with 40 per cent, Works with 40 per cent, Youth Development with 40 per cent and Education with 48.4 per cent.

Under Pillar II, which assesses budget-policy linkages, comprehensiveness and transparency, only the Ministries of Water Resources and Finance scored above 50 per cent.

The Ministries of Police Affairs and Labour recorded the lowest scores in the category, with 6.7 per cent and 12.8 per cent, respectively.

Presenting the report, Abana described the exercise as a significant milestone in the commission’s efforts to deepen the institutionalisation of fiscal responsibility principles across the Federal Government.

He said the index was designed to assess the performance of MDAs in implementing statutory public financial management requirements and identify areas requiring improvement.

“The Fiscal Responsibility Index is not merely an assessment document or an administrative scorecard.

“It is an empirical, evidence-based benchmarking instrument designed to measure, score and rank Federal Ministries, Departments and Agencies according to their levels of compliance with established public financial management obligations,” he said.

The index assesses institutional compliance with statutory requirements relating to public financial management practices, budgeting thresholds, procurement transparency and revenue remittance guidelines under the Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2007, and other applicable frameworks.

The 2026 edition evaluates the public financial management performance of federal MDAs across three consecutive financial years: 2023, 2024 and 2025.

Abana also disclosed that some ministries failed to complete the assessment process.

They include the Ministries of Transport; Agriculture and Food Security; Foreign Affairs; Petroleum Resources; Environment; and Industry, Trade and Investment.

He said the commission received and verified physical and electronic documentary evidence submitted by participating MDAs up to the September 4, 2026 deadline.

According to him, the final verification process ensured that supporting documents were examined, outstanding information considered and the data used in preparing the report properly validated.

The FRC boss described the presentation as an important accountability exercise, urging MDAs to embrace the findings and demonstrate a genuine commitment to improving their performance.

He said public institutions must move beyond preparing reports and submitting returns to ensuring that compliance was reflected in actual institutional practices and measurable public value.

Abana added that the findings should encourage stronger collaboration among oversight institutions, improve public confidence in government financial management systems and promote best practices across the Federal Public Service.

Meanwhile, the FRC chairman disclosed that the commission had increased annual independent revenue generated through operating surplus remittances and other internally generated revenue from about N300 million in 2010 to over N2 trillion.

He, however, lamented that the commission continued to face challenges, including limited enforcement powers, inadequate funding, staff shortages and insufficient accommodation, despite more than 16 years of operation.

“The commission has been challenged with limited enforcement powers, inadequate funding, staff shortages, lack of adequate accommodation after over 16 years of its establishment.

“Yet the Commission through the payment of Operating surplus and other IGR has increased independent revenue from just about N300M in 2010 to over N2 trillion annually,” he said.

He called on the Federal Government to strengthen the commission’s enforcement powers, amend the Fiscal Responsibility Act and increase its funding to enable it to discharge its responsibilities more effectively.

World.title: 2027: I want to deliver Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda in Lagos, says PDP’s Doherty
World.content:
Adedeji Doherty

By Adegboyega Adeleye

The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Lagos State, Adedeji Doherty, has described President Bola Ahmed Tinubu as his National Leader, saying he is contesting against the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, to ensure that the President’s Renewed Hope agenda is properly implemented in the state.

Doherty stated this on Monday during an interview on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily, where he explained why he was seeking to become Lagos governor despite his support for Tinubu and his administration’s national agenda.

He said he supported Tinubu’s Renewed Hope agenda but disagreed with the way the APC-led government in Lagos State was implementing it.

According to him, the failure to translate the President’s vision into reality in Lagos had contributed to political tensions, including alleged thuggery and the destruction of campaign materials.

He said, “I am going against the APC governorship candidate in Lagos because they are not doing what they are supposed to do concerning the APC/Mr President’s agenda for the country.

“When you do not crystallise the dream that is being made by your boss, then definitely all these fallouts of thuggery, removing of banners, tearing of posters and things like that, definitely is what is going to happen because you are trying to cover up your inadequacies in government.”

The PDP candidate further described Tinubu as his National Leader, stressing that his support for the President and the Renewed Hope agenda did not extend to the way the agenda was being implemented in Lagos.

He said, “Basically, you know? I’m going to support what I support fully, what my National Leader is doing. I support fully the Renewed Hope agenda, which is the agenda for the entire country, but I do not support the agenda as it is being materialised and crystallised in Lagos State.”

World.title: UK actor Robert Pattinson to be new James Bond
World.content:
(FILES) English actor Robert Pattinson poses upon arrival for the World premiere of the film “Mickey 17” in Leicester Square in central London on February 13, 2025. British actor Robert Pattinson has been named as the new James Bond, according to Amazon MGM Studios on November 16, 2026. (Photo by BENJAMIN CREMEL / AFP)

British actor Robert Pattinson was Monday named as the new James Bond, stepping into the coveted role of the world’s most famous fictional spy.

“Amazon MGM Studios have announced that Robert Pattinson will take on the iconic role of James Bond,” the studio said on the official 007.com website.

Pattinson would succeed Daniel Craig as the super-suave MI6 agent, “ushering in a new era for one of cinema’s most celebrated characters”, the studios added.

It will be the first Bond film since long-term Bond producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael Wilson stepped back and Amazon took creative control of the franchise, after acquiring the series’ parent company MGM.

“James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime,” Pattinson said.

“To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement,” he added in a statement.

Amazon MGM also announced that Oscar-nominated Canadian director Denis Villeneuve, behind such box-office hits as the “Dune” films, would be directing the next Bond movie from a script by “Peaky Blinders” creator Steven Knight.

Knight said in May that Amazon has given him a licence to play with the legendary secret agent created by author Ian Fleming.

“Bond has been bulletproof. People have been able to make mistakes and variations, and the character has survived,” Knight told Screen magazine at the Cannes Film Festival.

“Because the core of it is like a diamond. You can’t touch it,” he added.

Knight also told reporters that he has done research with “the SAS and even more secret outfits” for his reinvention of the next 007 movie.

Pattinson, 40, started out in amateur dramatics before getting his break in “Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire” (2005) as Cedric Diggory, a champion for Hogwarts.

But he rocketed to global fame for his part as brooding teen heartthrob in the romantic vampire saga “Twilight”.

– ‘Extremely inventive’ –

He was paid a reported $2 million for his lead in “Twilight” (2008), but by the time the saga wrapped up with the two parts of “Breaking Dawn” in 2011 and 2012, he was reportedly on $12.5 million plus 7.5 percent of the box office take.

One of his first forays into edgier cinema came with 2012 drama “Cosmopolis”, in which he portrayed a self-destructive currency speculator as his life falls apart.

The film was directed by legendary US auteur David Cronenberg, who described the actor as “extremely inventive”.

He received critical acclaim after later switching to more independent films and was nominated for best actor at the Cannes festival in 2017 for neo-grindhouse crime caper “Good Time” by New York-based brothers Josh and Ben Safdie.

In 2022, Amazon bought storied Hollywood studio MGM, which held distribution rights to Bond’s extensive back catalogue.

But it was not until early 2025 that the company struck a deal with longtime Bond producers Wilson and Broccoli to obtain full creative control.

The franchise had been closely guarded by the Broccoli family since 1962’s “Dr. No”.

They famously insisted on preserving the integrity of the Bond character and brand, resisting spin-offs and licensing that many industry experts expect to see following Amazon’s takeover.

World.title: Tinubu: 1,000 terrorists convicted, 2,000 prosecuted
World.content:
By Kingsley Omonobi

President Bola Tinubu has disclosed that more than 1,000 terrorists have been convicted, while over 2,000 suspected terrorists are currently undergoing prosecution as part of his administration’s efforts to dismantle terrorist networks across the country.

The President also said Nigerian security forces had killed or arrested four of eight identified senior global terrorist leaders, describing the development as evidence of the country’s growing capacity to dismantle terrorist command structures.

Tinubu, who was represented by the National Security Adviser, Mallam Nuhu Ribadu, made the disclosures on Monday at the opening of the 2026 Chief of Defence Intelligence (CDI) Annual Conference in Abuja.

He said the number of convictions and ongoing prosecutions placed Nigeria among countries with high rates of terrorism-related prosecutions globally.

Highlighting the operational successes recorded by security agencies, the President cited the elimination of senior Islamic State leader, Abu Bilal al-Minuki, in May 2026, as well as the arrests of other prominent terrorist figures.

According to him, the operations also targeted Ahmed Ohida’s ISWAP southern expansion network, while Abu Barra of Ansaru and Mamuda of Mahmudawa were arrested in 2025.

“Recent operational successes demonstrate our growing capacity to dismantle terrorist leadership, disrupt expansion networks and deny violent groups freedom of action.

“Under this administration, four of eight identified senior terrorist leaders have been killed or arrested. These gains include action against Ahmed Ohida’s ISWAP southern expansion network, the elimination of senior Islamic State leader Abu Bilal al-Minuki in May 2026, and the arrests of Abu Barra of Ansaru and Mamuda of Mahmudawa in 2025,” he said.

Tinubu, however, identified the remaining four senior terrorist figures as Ba Shuwa of ISWAP, Abdullahi Oro of IS-Sahel, Sadiku of JAS in the North-Central region and Bakura Doro in the Lake Chad Basin.

He said security agencies were sustaining operations against the remaining leaders and their networks, adding that senior bandit leaders, including Halilu Sububu, had also been killed alongside several of their fighters.

On developments in the Niger Delta, the President disclosed that incidents of illegal oil bunkering and vandalism of critical oil and gas installations declined from 32 in the first quarter of 2026 to 21 in the second quarter and 17 in the third quarter.

He said the figures represented a 46.88 per cent reduction between the first and third quarters.

Tinubu added that crude oil and condensate production averaged approximately 1.68 million barrels per day in August 2026, stressing the need to sustain the protection of the country’s energy assets and revenue sources.

He attributed the security gains to improved intelligence sharing and coordinated operations among the Department of State Services (DSS), Armed Forces, Police and other security agencies.

The President said the administration would consolidate the gains and sustain pressure on criminal and terrorist networks, particularly ahead of the 2027 general elections.

“Every Nigerian must be able to live, work and exercise their democratic rights in safety,” he said.

On the changing nature of security threats, Tinubu said technological advancements, particularly artificial intelligence, machine learning, cyber capabilities and unmanned systems, were creating new opportunities for intelligence gathering and security operations.

He said such technologies could help security agencies detect patterns, map criminal networks and generate early warnings of potential threats.

The President called for the integration of AI-assisted analysis, geospatial intelligence and unmanned surveillance through secure and interoperable systems capable of translating information into timely operational decisions.

He, however, cautioned that artificial intelligence outputs must be verified through accountable human judgement, while data protection and cybersecurity safeguards must be incorporated into the systems.

“Technology must strengthen the trusted human intelligence on which effective security depends,” he said.

Tinubu further disclosed that he had directed the Special Adviser on Homeland Security, Major General A.A. Famadewa (rtd), to coordinate the preparation of a Comprehensive National Threat Assessment and a Five-Year Rolling Strategic Defence Operations Plan.

He said the initiative was aimed at placing accurate, integrated and forward-looking intelligence at the centre of Nigeria’s defence planning.

The President also emphasised the importance of collaboration among the Armed Forces, Defence Intelligence Agency, DSS, National Intelligence Agency, Nigeria Police Force, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps and other relevant institutions.

He said intelligence cooperation must extend to regional and international partners, subnational entities, technology companies and research institutions.

Tinubu listed the United States, France, the United Kingdom, China, the United Arab Emirates, Türkiye and Nigeria’s African neighbours among countries with which his administration had strengthened security partnerships.

He pledged to deepen intelligence sharing, training and technological cooperation while safeguarding Nigeria’s sovereignty and national interest.

The President also urged Nigeria’s Defence Advisers and Attachés abroad to strengthen strategic intelligence and defence relationships with their host countries and international partners.

He called on State Office Coordinators to intensify collaboration with local security agencies to improve intelligence gathering and coordination.

Tinubu commended the Chief of Defence Intelligence, Lieutenant General Emmanuel Akomaye Parker Undiandeye, and his team for their leadership and contributions to strengthening defence intelligence and strategic cooperation.

In his remarks, the Minister of Defence, retired General Christopher Musa, commended intelligence personnel for their professionalism and contributions to national security.

Musa urged them to remain proactive, stressing that credible, timely and actionable intelligence was critical to successful military operations.

He also reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to indigenous defence production, describing local manufacturing as essential to developing sustainable military capabilities.

Similarly, the Chief of Defence Staff, General Olufemi Oluyede, described intelligence as fundamental to operational planning, strategic decision-making and effective military responses.

Oluyede called for increased investment in artificial intelligence, advanced data analytics, geospatial intelligence and unmanned systems.

He said the Armed Forces would continue to prioritise intelligence integration, capacity development and technological innovation.

The CDS stressed the need to shift security operations from largely reactive responses to proactive, intelligence-led engagements capable of anticipating and disrupting threats before they materialise.

The conference, organised by the Defence Intelligence Agency, is themed, “Optimising Intelligence through Technological Innovations for Effective Strategic Operations in a Complex Security Environment.”

Vanguard Newspaper

World.title: INEC debunks claim of remote BVAS log-out before voting ends
World.content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has dismissed as false and misleading a viral social media video alleging that the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) would be remotely logged out before the end of voting.

The commission clarified that only the poll official operating the device has the authority to log in or log out of the BVAS during voter accreditation and the subsequent result upload process.

INEC disclosed this in a statement posted on its official X platform on Monday, following the circulation of a video on Instagram alleging that voters would be logged out of the system before the conclusion of voting.

Describing the claim as fabricated, the commission said each polling unit was assigned unique login credentials, which were issued to the Presiding Officer on the eve of an election.

According to INEC, the credentials enable the poll official to log into the BVAS for voter accreditation on election day and subsequently upload the polling unit result sheet at the close of polls.

“The claim that the BVAS can be remotely logged out before the conclusion of accreditation and voting is false,” the commission stated.

It stressed that there was no provision for any external individual or authority to remotely log out the device.

The commission also dismissed claims that election results uploaded offline could be lost, explaining that the IReV application had been upgraded to accommodate offline uploads.

INEC said the enhancement followed experiences during the 2023 general election, when some poll officials were held hostage at their polling units because they could not upload results due to poor or non-existent network connectivity.

It explained that the offline upload feature allows poll officials in areas with poor or no network coverage to upload polling unit result sheets in the presence of stakeholders at the polling unit.

According to the commission, such results remain securely stored on the BVAS pending successful transmission to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV).

” As Poll Officials proceed from the polling unit to the Ward Collation Centre and the device reconnects to the internet, the result sheet is automatically transmitted to the IReV portal without requiring any further manual intervention,” it said.

INEC assured Nigerians that the BVAS and IReV systems operate in accordance with established procedures designed to protect the integrity, transparency and credibility of the electoral process.

The commission urged members of the public to disregard the video, refrain from creating or sharing unverified information and rely on its official communication channels for accurate information.

It reaffirmed its commitment to transparency, accountability and the conduct of free, fair and credible elections.

World.title: Plateau records 5,457 suspected diabetes cases in nine months
World.content:
By Golok Nanmwa

JOS — The Plateau State Government has raised concerns over the growing burden of diabetes in the state, following the record of 5,457 suspected new cases between January and September 2026.

The Commissioner for Health, Dr Nicholas Ba’amlong, disclosed this on Monday during a press briefing in Jos to commemorate the 2026 World Diabetes Day.

Ba’amlong said the figure followed 5,546 suspected cases recorded in 2025, but clarified that the numbers represented suspected cases and not confirmed diagnoses.

He said diabetes remained a major public health concern because many people were living with the condition without knowing their status.

The commissioner also disclosed that findings from the 2024 nationwide Know Your Number, Control Your Number screening campaign showed that 14,359 people were screened in Plateau State, with 2,610, representing approximately 18 per cent, recording elevated blood glucose levels.

He, however, cautioned that the findings did not represent the prevalence of diabetes in the state.

According to him, the figures underscore the need to expand access to screening, diagnosis and treatment services.

As part of activities marking this year’s World Diabetes Day, the Ministry of Health, in collaboration with the Plateau State chapters of the Diabetes Association of Nigeria and the Endocrine and Metabolic Society of Nigeria, conducted a free workplace screening exercise at the Joseph Gomwalk Secretariat Complex, Jos.

Ba’amlong said the exercise targeted 1,000 civil servants and provided blood glucose and blood pressure checks, weight and body mass index assessments, health education, counselling and referrals for further medical attention where necessary.

Speaking on government interventions, the commissioner said the administration of Governor Caleb Mutfwang was working towards extending diabetes education and screening services to underserved communities across the state’s 17 local government areas through existing primary healthcare facilities and community outreach programmes.

He added that the government was exploring partnerships and appropriate medical technologies to improve access to diagnostic services, particularly at the primary healthcare level, while strengthening follow-up and referral systems for people with elevated blood glucose levels.

“Screening is only the beginning. Early detection must lead to appropriate diagnosis and treatment,” he said.

The commissioner urged residents, particularly those with a family history of diabetes, excess weight or high blood pressure, to check their blood glucose levels regularly and seek medical attention when necessary.

He also advised residents to adopt healthy lifestyles through balanced diets, regular physical activity and weight management, while avoiding tobacco and limiting alcohol consumption.

Ba’amlong identified excessive thirst, frequent urination, unexplained weight loss and persistent fatigue as some of the symptoms that could indicate diabetes.

He further urged people living with the condition to adhere to prescribed treatment and attend regular medical reviews to prevent complications.

World Diabetes Day is observed annually on November 14 to raise awareness about diabetes, promote prevention and encourage access to quality healthcare for people living with the condition.

World.title: Anchor University Celebrates 10th Anniversary, Graduates 563 Students
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Funmi Ogundare

As Anchor University Lagos (AUL) celebrates its 10th anniversary, the institution is set to graduate a total of 563 students at its combined sixth and seventh convocation ceremonies for the 2024/2025 and 2025/2026 academic sessions.

Briefing journalists Monday, the Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Samuel Oye Bandele, explained that the convocation ceremonies and the university’s decennial anniversary celebration, themed, ‘Celebrating a University that is Anchored on Christ’, provided an opportunity to reflect on the institution’s decade of growth.

He acknowledged the contributions of its founders and stakeholders, and renew its commitment to academic excellence and transformational impact.

On the convocation, he stated that the ceremonies would celebrate the academic achievements of graduates from two sessions, recognise outstanding performances and formally admit deserving students into the community of qualified graduates.

As part of the anniversary activities, the university has lined up a seven-day programme running from November 16 to 22, featuring community service, an entrepreneurship and innovation exhibition, alumni engagement, a convocation lecture, book launch and thanksgiving.

The decennial and convocation lecture, titled, ‘Anchor at 10: University Education Transformation, Leadership and the Future of Africa’, will be delivered by the Chairman of the Governing Board, National Universities Commission ( NUC) and former Vice-Chancellor of the University of Lagos, Prof. Oluwatoyin Ogundipe, on November 20.

The combined 6th and 7th convocation ceremonies will hold on November 21, while the celebration will conclude with a special thanksgiving service at the Deeper Life Bible Church Headquarters, Gbagada, Lagos, on November 22.

The VC said the institution had continued to strengthen its academic identity, expand its institutional capacity and contribute to Nigeria’s educational development through improvements in academic programmes, infrastructure, research, student development and institutional partnerships.

“The university’s next decade would focus on greater academic visibility, stronger research output, increased internationalisation, improved infrastructure, enhanced digital capacity, expansion of professional programmes and stronger partnerships with industries and other institutions,” Bandele stressed.

He said the institution remained committed to becoming increasingly recognised for academic excellence, Christian character, innovation, responsible leadership and global impact.

World.title: Peter Obi to Hold Anambra Town Hall Meeting in Onitsha Friday
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

David-Chyddy Eleke in Awka

Former Anambra State Governor and Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi, will on Friday, November 20, visit Anambra State for a town hall meeting as part of his nationwide strategic engagements.

A press release by the Director of Media and Publicity of the NDC in Anambra State, Dr. Tony Onyima, stated that the meeting is meant to create a platform for the candidate to interact with Anambra people, most of who he said are already familiar with him.

He said: “The meeting, scheduled for 2:00 p.m., will take place at the Main Bowl of the Archbishop C.J. Patterson Building, All Saints Cathedral, Onitsha.

“Chairperson of the Organising Committee, Prof. Oby Lilian Orogbu, who represents Awka North and South Federal Constituency in the 10th National Assembly, described the event as more than a town hall meeting, saying it would provide an opportunity for Obi to reconnect with his people.”

According to her, “The visit is particularly significant because it represents a homecoming for the former governor, who governed Anambra State for eight years and has strong personal ties to Onitsha, where he grew up and currently resides.

“The organising committee is working to ensure that the event would be unique and successful, and it will potentially be the biggest of Obi’s town hall engagements.”

The release disclosed that the programme would feature other activities, including courtesy visits and roadshows, as part of the former governor’s itinerary.

World.title: Lawmaker Defends Choice of Jos for Tinubu’s Campaign Launch, Dismisses Opposition Coalition
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Yemi Kosoko in Jos

Senator Diket Plang has described the decision by the All Progressives Congress (APC) to launch President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s North-central campaign in Jos as a strategic and historic move, citing the city’s political, cultural and religious significance.

Speaking during an interactive session with journalists in Jos, Plang said the choice of Plateau State’s capital reflected the party’s understanding of Nigeria’s political dynamics and the importance of the North-central region.

According to him, Jos occupies a unique place in the country’s political history and serves as a meeting point for diverse ethnic groups, making it an ideal location for a major national political event.

The senator said the city symbolizes national unity, noting that virtually all ethnic groups in Nigeria are represented in Jos.

Plang also dismissed opposition activities and anti-government sentiments expressed by some youths, describing them as political propaganda that should not be mistaken for the views of the wider electorate.

He argued that public displays of dissatisfaction are sometimes orchestrated and do not necessarily reflect the true mood of voters ahead of elections.

Expressing confidence in President Tinubu’s re-election prospects, Plang said the APC remains the party with the strongest grassroots structure nationwide, extending from the federal level to polling units across the country.

He maintained that emerging opposition coalitions and newly formed political movements lacked the organisational reach required to effectively challenge the ruling party.

The senator also predicted a favourable electoral outcome for Plateau State Governor Caleb Mutfwang should he seek a second term, while questioning the authenticity of a viral video attributed to former Plateau APC chairman Letep Dabang, suggesting it may have been manipulated.

On the Tinubu administration, Plang said concerns previously raised over the Muslim-Muslim ticket had diminished, arguing that the president had demonstrated inclusiveness in governance and could attract substantial support across Northern Nigeria in future elections.

World.title: NDC Decries Attack on Kwankwaso, Demands Arrest of Perpetrators, Sponsors
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

* Party accuses APC supporters of political violence, warns against intimidation of opposition candidates

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has condemned the alleged attack on its vice-presidential candidate, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, in Bichi, Kano State, demanding the immediate arrest and prosecution of those responsible for the incident and their sponsors.

The party described the incident as a deliberate assault on its candidate, supporters and the nation’s democratic process, warning that the growing spate of political violence against opposition figures could undermine the credibility of the 2027 general election.

In a statement issued on Monday by its National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, the NDC accused supporters of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of being behind the attack, describing the incident as part of an alleged pattern of intimidation targeting opposition candidates and their supporters across the country.

The opposition party said the attack was not an ordinary disruption of a political activity but a calculated attempt to instil fear among its members and supporters.

“This was not a mere disruption. It was a deliberate, violent assault on our candidate, on our supporters, and on democracy itself,” the party declared.

The NDC alleged that the increasing incidents of violence against opposition figures reflected the ruling party’s resort to intimidation in the face of growing political opposition.

It stated: “The spate of violent attacks on opposition candidates and supporters across the country is a clear sign that the APC has lost the argument, lost the people, and has now resorted to thuggery and intimidation to cling to power.”

The party, however, insisted that the incident would not discourage its members or derail its political activities ahead of the 2027 elections.

“The NDC will not be intimidated. We will not be silenced. We will not retreat,” it declared.

The party called on the Nigeria Police Force, the Department of State Services (DSS) and other relevant security agencies to launch an immediate investigation into the Bichi incident, identify and arrest those involved, and ensure that anyone found culpable faces the full weight of the law.

It also demanded that the security agencies investigate those allegedly behind the attack, stressing that political violence should not be allowed to become a feature of Nigeria’s electoral process.

The NDC further urged the security agencies to guarantee the protection of all political candidates and their supporters, irrespective of their party affiliations.

It said the responsibility for maintaining peace during political activities rested squarely on the relevant security institutions, warning that failure to bring perpetrators of political violence to justice could encourage further attacks.

“Nigeria deserves a free, fair and peaceful election — not a reign of terror,” the party said.

Reaffirming its determination to pursue its political ambitions despite the alleged intimidation, the NDC expressed confidence in its capacity to mobilise Nigerians behind its campaign for political change.

World.title: Atiku Thanks Yobe Residents for Massive Welcome, Commends Gov for Fair Campaign Ground
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

*Says ‘Tinubu must go’ chants signal Nigerians’ desire for change

Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has expressed deep gratitude to the people of Potiskum and Yobe State for the extraordinary welcome they gave him and his campaign team, as well as to the Governor for providing a level playing field for the ADC’s Affordable Life campaign.

In a statement issued by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said the reception that greeted his arrival from Azare, Bauchi State, and followed him into Potiskum was a moving testament to the people’s faith in the promise of a more affordable life.

“The welcome from the moment we entered Potiskum from Azare was simply breathtaking. The sea of heads, the joyful faces, the chants and the warmth of the people will remain in my heart. To the people of Potiskum and to the good people of Yobe State, I say thank you. You opened your doors and your hearts to us, and we are deeply grateful.

“I also thank the Governor of Yobe State for ensuring that our campaign could proceed on a level playing field. Democracy is strengthened when every party can meet the people freely and present its message. We appreciate the opportunity to bring our vision to Yobe.

“The Presidency may need artificial intelligence to conjure a crowd, but in Potiskum the people came out in flesh and blood, unfiltered, unedited and impossible to fabricate. Our Affordable Life campaign needs no artificial crowd; the people’s presence and their voices speak for themselves.

“The Presidency’s AI must have forgotten that crowds need seats and that people do not fly. Perhaps in Tinubu’s imaginary rally, the supporters were expected to hover through the speech.

“The ADC’s Affordable Life campaign is not mere sloganeering. When I hear the crowd chanting ‘Tinubu Must Go’ at our rallies, I take those words personally. They are a call for change and a reminder of the responsibility that will come with the people’s mandate. When President Tinubu leaves office on 29 May 2027, good governance and an affordable life must follow. I solemnly pledge to take immediate steps to make life affordable again when elected president at the January 16 presidential election. That is my promise to our teeming supporters.”

Atiku said the welcome from Yobe would stay with him as the campaign continued across the country.

“Yobe has reminded us that when a message speaks to people’s struggles and aspirations, they will come out in their numbers to be heard.”

World.title: Inflation Drops to 14.06%
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

James Emejo in Abuja

The Consumer Price Index (CPI) which measures the rate of change in prices of good and commodities declined remarkably 14.06 per cent in October compared to 14.63 per cent in September, the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS), said Monday.

The NBS, in its CPI report for October 2026, said headline inflation rate declined by 4.91 percentage points from 18.97 per cent recorded in the corresponding period of 2025.

However, the report indicated that the rate at which average prices increased month-on-month picked up, with headline inflation rising to 0.43 per cent in October, compared with 0.06 per cent in September.

Food inflation, a major component of household expenditure, stood at 19.13 per cent year-on-year in October, compared with 16.30 per cent recorded in the corresponding month of 2025.

Month-on-month, however, food inflation remained negative at -0.75 per cent, indicating that average food prices continued to decline, although at a slower pace than in September when the rate stood at -1.55 per cent.

Month on month, food prices averaged -0.40 per cent in October compared to -2.86 per cent in September.

The 0.80 percentage point moderation in the monthly decline suggested that the relief from falling food prices became less pronounced during the review period, the NBS noted.

The statistical agency attributed the development to increase in average prices of several food items, including vegetable oil (75cl), Titus sardines (125g), prepacked green peas, frozen mackerel, croakers, local rice, fresh catfish, beef tripes, palm oil (75cl) and loose millet flour.

World.title: Sunbeth Energies Expands Self-Service Fuelling Operations to Ibadan
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Peter Uzoho

Sunbeth Energies Limited, one of Nigeria’s fastest growing energy companies, has launched an additional self-service fuelling station in Ibadan, Oyo State, marking the fourth location in its growing retail network.

The launch extends the company’s fuelling solution to the South-West, giving more motorists access to a service designed around convenience, transparency and customer control.

The new station gives motorists the option to manage their fuelling transactions independently, from selecting the quantity or value of fuel they wish to purchase to making payment and dispensing fuel.

The company unveiled the latest station Monday, saying instructions displayed at the pumps guide customers through the process, while trained Customer Assistants are available to provide support whenever necessary.

Maintaining its pioneer status, the expansion builds on the company’s experience across its existing stations in Lagos, Abuja and Port Harcourt.

Its Ogba station in Lagos, where the self-service offering was first introduced in July 2026, has now surpassed 100 days of operations without any reported service challenges.

Speaking during the launch, Head, Retail Roll-Out Projects at Sunbeth Energies,

Adegbemiro Adeboye, said: “Our ambition is to make this service accessible to motorists across Nigeria, so that every Nigerian has the opportunity to experience a fuelling option that gives them greater control, transparency and confidence in their purchases.

“We believe that building trust in the downstream petroleum sector starts with giving customers a clear understanding of what they are paying for and greater control over the transaction.

“The successful operation of our first self-service station for over 100 days without any operational issues is an important demonstration of the reliability of the technology and the potential of this service to transform the retail fuelling experience in Nigeria.”

“As the company expands into new locations, he said they would continue to listen to customers across their regions, gather feedback and use real operational data to improve the service.

This, Adeboye said, would help them to understand the challenges motorists face in different markets and develop solutions that respond to local needs.

“Our focus is on building a service that works reliably for Nigerian conditions and continues to improve with every deployment”, he added.

The Ibadan launch marks another step in Sunbeth Energies’ efforts to develop its self-service offering across the country, combining technology, customer feedback and operational learning to deliver a more transparent and customer-led retail fuelling experience.

Sunbeth Energies operates in Nigeria’s downstream petroleum sector, focusing on the bulk trading, distribution and supply of refined petroleum products.

Through strategic partnerships, operational excellence and innovation, the company contributes to Nigeria’s energy security and the development of the downstream petroleum sector.

World.title: NURTW-TOAN Dispute: Court Reaffirms Arrest Order Against NURTW Chairman, Secretary
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Wale Igbintade

The National Industrial Court of Nigeria, Lagos Division, has reaffirmed its earlier order directing the arrest and committal to prison of the Lagos State Chairman of the National Union of Road Transport Workers (NURTW), Alhaji Mustapha Adekunle, popularly known as Sego, and the union’s Secretary, Usman Teslim, over alleged contempt of court.

Justice Isaac Essien, who presided over the matter, directed security agencies to arrest the two officials and produce them before the court at the next adjourned date.

The judge also adjourned further proceedings in the committal case till January 25, 2027, following a petition written to the President of the National Industrial Court challenging the ongoing proceedings.

Justice Essien said the court would await the decision of the NICN President on the petition before taking further steps in the matter.

However, the adjournment did not affect the existing committal order, which the judge reaffirmed while directing the relevant security agencies to ensure the two officials were brought before the court on the next date.

Earlier, the judge cautioned members of the Tricycle Owners and Operators Association of Nigeria (TOOAN), who allegedly present themselves as members of the Tricycle Owners Association of Nigeria (TOAN), against disrupting proceedings.

He urged those attending the court sitting to maintain decorum and allow the court to conduct its proceedings without interference.

The contempt proceedings stem from allegations that NURTW officials continued to interfere with the activities of TOAN despite a December 11, 2025 judgment of the National Industrial Court recognising the association as an independent trade union.

The judgment had affirmed TOAN’s independent status, forming the basis of the subsequent allegations that the NURTW officials had acted in disregard of the court’s decision.

The case is expected to resume on January 25, 2027, when the court will continue proceedings in the committal matter.

World.title: Who really qualifies for SASSA grants? South Africans demand answers over foreign nationals
World.content:
South Africans are demanding that government put citizens first when it comes to social grants, with many claiming that foreign nationals are benefiting at their expense.

The comments came in response to a SASSA grant post on The South African’s Facebook page, where the question of who qualifies for state support quickly took over the discussion.

Gedion Mthunzi asked directly: “Why is the money given to foreigners?”



Clive Pillay argued that birthright should come first, writing: “South Africans must get their money first cause they were born here.”

Tebogo Malema called for a complete ban, saying: “They must stop foreigners to receive grants.”

Many of those commenting said they felt overlooked by a system they believe should serve South Africans before anyone else.

sassa Fraud fears add to the frustration

For some, the concern is not only about eligibility but about money going missing.

Tau Sehaole wrote: “It’s a must and is not enough, much money is paid to the foreign nationals some stolen.”

Ietsie V Alles Pretorius suggested the money ends up in the wrong hands, asking where else it could go: “To their pockets!!! Where else!!!”



None of the commenters provided evidence to support these claims, but their comments reflect a deep mistrust of how social grant money is managed.

What the law actually says

Under the Social Assistance Act, permanent grants such as the older persons grant, disability grant and child support grant are limited to South African citizens, permanent residents and recognised refugees living in the country.

Applicants must produce a valid identity document, which SASSA verifies against the Department of Home Affairs’ records, and most grants also require applicants to pass a means test.

The SRD grant has slightly broader eligibility. Following court rulings, it is also open to certain asylum seekers and special permit holders, provided they meet the income and other qualifying requirements.

Undocumented foreign nationals do not qualify for any SASSA grant.

SASSA has previously encouraged anyone with information about grant fraud to report it through its official fraud hotline rather than relying on claims made on social media.

For the commenters, however, the bigger issue is fairness, and many say they want the government to show where every rand of grant money goes clearly.
