World.title: El PP propone una ‘ley de nietos’ para que los exiliados vascos por terrorismo de ETA puedan votar en las elecciones autonómicas
World.content:
El PP mete a ETA en campaña. Y lo hace con una propuesta, oculta en su programa, hasta ahora. Los populares quieren que quienes abandonaron Euskadi a causa del terrorismo puedan “participar” en las elecciones autonómicas del País Vasco y de Navarra, ejerciendo “su derecho al voto en el municipio en el que estuvieran empadronados” antes de abandonar el territorio. Alberto Núñez Feijóo desgranará este lunes la medida, que se incluye en su oferta electoral Reconstrucción Nacional para las urnas del 29 de noviembre, durante un mitin en Pamplona convocado para esta tarde. Allí comparecerá junto a UPN, con quienes concurren en una papeleta conjunta por la circunscripción navarra. Feijóo llega hoy a ese mitin con tensión añadida tras la agresión sufrida por el candidato del Partido Popular por Gipuzkoa, Jon Echevarría, y otros miembros de Nuevas Generaciones, en Hernani el sábado. Un ataque que ha coincidido con el anuncio de la promesa de una ley de nietos vasca.

“El Partido Popular propondrá una ley de nietos vasca, una reforma legal para facilitar la voluntaria participación en las elecciones de aquellas personas que fueron expulsadas de Euskadi en los momentos más duros de la violencia y el terror en las calles del País Vasco”, avanzan fuentes de Génova. La nueva propuesta del PP aparece en el apartado 132 de su programa, que no fue desvelado del todo en el acto de presentación de la semana pasada. Génova ha querido reservar algunas de las medidas bajo llave para ir anunciándolas en los distintos mítines de la caravana del líder del Partido Popular. En el caso de la ley de nietos vasca, estaba ya previsto que se diera a conocer este lunes en Pamplona.

Tras el ataque, Feijóo cambió su agenda y mañana martes recalará en Gipuzkoa para hacer campaña con Echevarría, joven del PP con un perfil muy mediático como tertuliano de televisión y como figura activa en las redes sociales. “Gracias, presidente. No tenemos miedo. Vamos a recorrernos toda Guipúzcoa”, proclamó Echevarría en X tras anunciar Feijóo que estará en la provincia guipuzkoana este martes. El Partido Popular no logró escaño allí en 2023 y en los próximos comicios se lo disputa con EH Bildu, según las encuestas. Génova no presentó cabeza de lista al Senado debido al pacto con Vox, que concurre en esa circunscripción a la Cámara alta en lugar de hacerlo el PP.

“Feijóo revelará la medida 132 del programa, y lo hará el día antes de viajar a Guipúzcoa para apoyar a Jon Echevarría y al resto de compañeros del Partido Popular vasco que están siendo agredidos, amenazados y amedrentados por los violentos cuyos referentes políticos sostienen el Gobierno de Pedro Sánchez”, subrayan al respecto fuentes del gabinete del jefe de la oposición. Según ha podido saber este periódico, el apartado 132 del programa quedará redactado así: 132. “Quienes tuvieron que huir de ETA podrán volver a votar en su municipio. Promoveremos la reforma de la ley electoral para que todos aquellos que tuvieron que abandonar el País Vasco y Navarra por causa del terrorismo de ETA puedan volver a ejercer el derecho al voto en el municipio en el que estuvieran empadronados”.

En Santander, este domingo, el líder del PP conectó a “la gentuza” de EH Bildu con el ataque y pidió al presidente Sánchez que transmitiera a sus socios “que no violenten la campaña”. La propuesta llega además después de que Feijóo acusara al presidente Sánchez de “ingeniería electoral” por el desarrollo de la ley de nietos derivada de la Ley de Memoria Democrática. El Tribunal Supremo ha suspendido el voto de los hijos de los nacionalizados por esta norma al considerar que la instrucción que desarrolla la ley aprobada en el Congreso excede el objeto de aplicación. Antes de visitar Pamplona, Feijóo tiene este lunes otro acto con el sector agrario en Lleida, sobre las 12.30, donde también hablará ante los medios de comunicación.

World.title: Ángel Gaitán, el mecánico más famoso de España, entrevista a Abascal tras el plantón a Jordi Wild: “Tienes mi voto”
World.content:
El líder de Vox se sienta con el tertuliano de ‘Horizonte’, que pide 150 euros por una llamada telefónica de menos de 10 minutos para temas de coches

Hay muchas entrevistas en esta campaña electoral. Y luego está la de Santiago Abascal y Ángel Gaitán, que comienza así: “Bueno, compañero, ¿te puedo tutear?”. El líder de Vox plantó a Jordi Wild el pasado jueves y, ante las críticas recibidas en redes sociales, optó por acudir con este mecánico, el más famoso de España.

De Aranjuez y de 39 años, dejó el bachillerato para vender coches en el concesionario familiar y en apenas cuatro años ha generado un auténtico imperio en redes sociales. Su figura genera rechazo y admiración a partes iguales. Ahora mismo cuenta con cuatro millones de seguidores en TikTok, otros 2,3 en Instagram, 722.000 suscriptores en YouTube y 175.000 en X. “Si te presentas a presidente del Gobierno, te voto sin pensarlo”, se lee a menudo entre sus comentarios. Gaitán pide 150 euros por una llamada telefónica de menos de 10 minutos por asesoramiento en temas del coche. Dice que tiene listas de espera. Y 653,50 euros por solo comprobar tu vehículo.

Los algoritmos promueven sus mensajes cada dos por tres porque generan críticas, me gustas, comentarios. Opina de política, de medios, de periodismo. Es tertuliano con Iker Jiménez. Gaitán dice en esta charla con Abascal que el día que el doctor Cabrera dijo en Horizonte que iba a votar al líder de Vox, le mandó un WhatsApp de inmediato para cerrar la entrevista. Cabrera, por las dudas, dijo otro día en estas tertulias: “Me vais a matar, pero viva Franco”.

Gaitán fue hasta un monte de Toledo el pasado jueves y puso dos sillas. Una para él y otra para Abascal. El líder de Vox comenzó recordando su pasado familiar y cómo vivió bajo la amenaza de ETA. “En España se vive ahora una libertad a medias”, dijo Gaitán después. Al rato, preguntó: “Para todos los que dicen que no has trabajado en tu vida. ¿Tú crees que se cambiarían por ti? Para mí esto es un trabajo, ¿eh?”.

Abascal contestó que su dedicación a la política es una contribución para la defensa de sus principios y sus valores. “Vengo a que no destruyan mi patria. No me acompleja que me digan que me he dedicado toda mi vida a la política”. Abascal lleva 25 años viviendo de la política (y tiene 50). La única vez que trabajó en el sector privado fue cuando montó un bar en Vitoria. El negocio fracasó y él perdió hasta la casa familiar, que había hipotecado. Al rato, Gaitán preguntó.

—¿Eres creyente?

—Yo tengo fe. Tengo la cabeza…

—Donde hay que tenerla.

La historia del mecánico Gaitán, por cierto, comenzó por accidente. Se rompió el codo en 2021 y su hijo le aconsejó que subiera vídeos de mecánica a TikTok. El primero tuvo medio millón de visitas en menos de 24 horas. A partir de ahí, millones y millones de visitas. El pasado año facturó 4,7 millones de euros.

El mecánico cuestionó también sobre la violencia de género y las medidas que tomaría si llega el Gobierno. “Detener la invasión migratoria [...] Me irrita el concepto de violencia de género”. Gaitán siguió: “Todos conocemos personas cercanas que han ido al calabozo por denuncias falsas”. El líder de Vox guardó silencio. La realidad, sin embargo, es bien distinta. El Observatorio del Consejo General del Poder Judicial responde a esto que “es incorrecto afirmar que denuncia equivale automáticamente a detención”, ya que “cada caso es objeto de una valoración individualizada por parte de las Fuerzas y Cuerpos de Seguridad y, posteriormente, queda sometida al control judicial”.

Gaitán siguió con su cuestionario. “Otra pregunta que me hace, digamos, el colectivo gay o lesbianas. ¿Qué derechos no les tocarías nunca si entrases y qué harías con la ley del aborto?”. Abascal respondió: “Los homosexuales van a acabar votando todos a Vox. Yo no distingo a las personas; todos somos iguales. ¿Quién protege a los homosexuales? Pues Vox”.

Vox, sin embargo, considera que el matrimonio es la unión entre un hombre y una mujer, con el objetivo de formar una familia, a la que añade el calificativo de “natural”. En 2019, el propio Abascal dijo en una entrevista en Antena 3: “Es una unión civil como la que podrían tener dos hermanas viudas”. Y en otras entrevistas también ha rechazado de plano que las parejas homosexuales puedan acceder a la adopción.

Sobre el aborto, el líder de Vox dijo que “es un mal”. “Para el no nacido que es abortado y para la mujer. Hay que hacer una ley para proteger la vida y que, en los casos de abortos no deseados, dé alternativas. No venimos a perseguir a nadie”. Luego habló sobre inmigración y dijo que las ayudas sociales tendrán que ser para los españoles. “Y en su caso”, matizó, “para extranjeros legales que hayan estado trabajando”.

Vox también propone en su programa electoral cuotas para alumnos “de otras culturas” en las aulas y excluir a los indocumentados del sistema sanitario. Minutos después, Abascal interrumpió la entrevista un segundo:

—Tienes una avispa en el pecho.

—No pasa nada. Soy más de campo que las amapolas.

Y Gaitán siguió. Turno para la vivienda. “Nadie, ni nosotros, cambiando todas las políticas, va a lograr que esto cambie. No hay una varita mágica. ¿Qué creo que hay que hacer?”. Y culpó a la inmigración. “Hay que liberalizar el suelo”, continuó después. Sin embargo, cuando el Gobierno llevó la ley del suelo al Congreso, él y sus 33 diputados se abstuvieron y la nueva ley de liberalización del suelo no salió adelante. Hubo tiempo también de cómo gestionar lo público de manera “eficiente”.

—¿Cuánto cobra un presidente del Gobierno?

—7.000 u 8.000 euros —dijo Abascal.

—Es poco dinero.

—Sí, pero no voy a presentarme para cambiar eso.

Abascal dijo después que la política tritura. “Hay una competencia por ver quién me hace la entrevista más difícil. Dan lecciones unos a otros para ver cuál es la fórmula de matarme”. Gaitán dijo: “¿Por qué hay que matarte? ¿Qué pasa, los que pensamos de manera diferente no tenemos hueco en España? ¿Tenemos que tener miedo a decir que yo estoy contigo?”. Abascal zanjó el asunto rápido:

—El futuro es nuestro.

—Yo cada vez lo tengo más claro.

Abascal pidió el voto después a la gente de izquierda: “Yo quiero a España. Sánchez tiene que dar cuenta ante los tribunales”. Y comenzó el turno de preguntas económicas. “¿Vas a tocar la pensión actual?, ¿será universal y gratuita la sanidad?, ¿vas a tocar leyes laborales?, ¿alguien que cobra 30.000 euros le va a quedar más dinero?”. Abascal estuvo rápido: no contestó.

“Pfff”, dijo. “Te sugiero que le hagas una entrevista a Figaredo, que es el que tiene el programa económico. Vox no es para ricos ni pobres. Es para todos los españoles”. Antes de terminar, Gaitán habló de las tragedias y los medios que tiene el Estado para acudir en cuanto suceden estas catástrofes. Y, de paso, criticó la actuación del Gobierno en la dana.

En la dana, Gaitán pidió donaciones a sus seguidores, pero las paralizó porque supuestamente las hacía pasar como beneficios de empresa. Hizo hasta un concurso de me gustas en sus redes para ver qué pueblo valenciano recibía más y, así, llevar ahí las ayudas. Criticó hasta Cáritas. Y la organización tuvo que salir a desmentir su bulo.

Antes de terminar la entrevista, eso sí, Abascal llamó psicópata a Sánchez. E insistió: “No me creo los datos sobre nada. Sobre inmigración, economía…”. Gaitán, al cierre, se quitó la sudadera y enseñó una camiseta donde ponía Ceuta. Vox fue el único partido que votó en contra de las ayudas al pueblo ceutí el pasado septiembre. El mecánico cerró la entrevista tajante:

—Pues tienes mi voto, compañero.

World.title: Rosalía logra nueve nominaciones a los Grammy de 2027
World.content:
Un gramófono a la entrada de los 67º premios Grammy, el 2 de febrero de 2025 en Los Ángeles, California.

La Academia de Grabación ha anunciado este lunes las nominaciones a los premios Grammy del próximo 2027. Y, este año, en las categorías reinas dominan los nombres de mujer.

La artista que logra un mayor número de nominaciones es Raye, con un total de 11. Hasta ahora, Beyoncé era la única mujer que había logrado un número tan alto de candidaturas (precisamente, el año pasado). Rosalía va segunda, con nueve, y las siguen Ella Langley, Olivia Rodrigo y Phoebe Bridgers, con siete. Taylor Swift suma este año cinco, con lo que llega a un total de 63 en su carrera.

De las nueve nominaciones que ha logrado la española están las tres principales: mejor álbum del año, por Lux, mejor canción del año por Berghain y mejor grabación del año, también por Berghain. El reconocimiento llega apenas cuatro días después de convertirse en ganadora de cinco Grammy Latinos.

Más información RAYE, la cantante que se negó a ser moldeada por la industria y buscó su propio éxito

Hasta ahora, Rosalía solo había sido nominada a un total de cuatro categorías de los Grammy, y había ganado dos: mejor álbum de rock, música urbana o alternativa latina, tanto por El mal querer en 2020 como por Motomami en 2023. Este año, las nueve que acumula son a mejor álbum del año (Lux), mejor canción (Berghain), mejor grabación (Berghain), mejor vídeo musical (Berghain), mejor canción latina (La Perla), mejor interpretación de música alternativa (Reliquia), mejor interpretación de música global (Porcelana, con Dougie F), mejor interpretación en solitario de pop (Sauvignon Blanc) y mejor álbum de música alternativa (Lux).

Las mujeres se convierten en claras ganadoras de, al menos, las nominaciones. Solo en disco del año, la más importante de los Grammy, hay siete, y un solo hombre. Aquí, Rosalía y su Lux competirán contra Raye y This Music May Contain Hope, así como contra Taylor Swift y The Life of a Showgirl, Olivia Rodrigo (You seem pretty sad for a girl so in love), Phoebe Bridgers (Lost Weekend), Olivia Dean (The Art of Loving), Ella Langley (Dandelion) y, el único nominado, Bruno Mars (The Romantic).

Rosalía, en la actuación inagural de los Latin Grammy, el 12 de noviembre de 2026 en Las Vegas. Kevin Winter (Getty Images for the The Latin Recording Academy)

En cuanto a la grabación del año, aquí la batalla estará entre Berghain, de Rosalía y Bjork junto a Yves Tumor, contra The Fate of Ophelia, de Taylor Swift; Where Is My Husband, de Raye; The Cure, de Olivia Rodrigo; Man I Need, de Olivia Dean; Choosin’ Texas, de Ella Langley; I just might, de Bruno Mars; y Dracula, de Tame Impala y Jennie.

En canción del año la lista es muy similar, con siete de ocho mujeres: Berghain, de Rosalía y Bjork junto a Yves Tumor; el fenómeno musical en Estados Unidos que ha sido Choosin’ Texas, de Ella Langley (la canción que más tiempo ha estado en la lista de números uno de Billboard, hasta 27 semanas); The Cure, de Olivia Rodrigo; Hate that I made you love me; de Ariana Grande; Man I Need, de Olivia Dean; Risk It All, de Bruno Mars; Where Is My Husband, de Raye; y en este caso no The Fate of Ophelia, sino I Knew It, I Knew You, de Taylor Swift.

El éxito de su tema Where Is My Husband! catapultó a RAYE (escribe su nombre en mayúsculas) a la fama internacional a finales de 2025. Nacida en Londres en 1997, la artista firmó su primer contrato discográfico en 2014. Pero en junio de 2021 anunció a través de sus redes sociales que pasaba a ser artista independiente y que no quería ser moldeada por una industria a veces exigente. “Ya no soy una estrella del pop educada. Quiero hacer mi álbum ahora, por favor, eso es todo lo que quiero”, escribió entonces en X.

Raye, en un concierto en Londres en febrero de 2026. Joseph Okpako (WireImage)

Además, aseguró que no le tomaban lo “suficientemente en serio” como para gestionar su propio éxito. Su sueño siempre fue publicar su propio álbum, y lo consiguió después de un periodo de redención, alejada de las drogas, el alcohol y volviendo a reconectar con sus raíces. Su último disco, This Music May Contain Hope, está ahora nominado al mejor álbum del año.

En cuanto a mejor nuevo artista del año, competirán en esta categoría la gran revelación de la música country, Ella Langley, contra Angine de Poitrine, Geese, Slayyyter, Sienna Spiro, Don Toliver, Remi Wolf y The Womack Sisters.

Entre otras curiosidades, destaca que Beyoncé se convierte en la primera artista que supera por primera vez las 100 nominaciones a los Grammy. Por su parte, gracias a esta nominación con su The Life of a Showgirl, Taylor Swift rompe un récord: al de la artista con más álbumes consecutivos nominados al mejor del año, cinco, empatando con Kendrick Lamar. En cambio, resulta llamativo que Harry Styles, con una exitosa gira mundial, quede fuera de los Grammy, sin una sola nominación.

Este año los Grammy suman un total de cinco categorías nuevas, entre ellos una de mejor música asiática, que ha hecho que algunas bandas de dicho continente, como BTS, no estén de acuerdo y no remitan su música. Eso hace que los premios lleguen a un total de 100 galardones. En la gala se entregarán apenas una decena. Los premios se celebrarán el 7 de febrero de 2027 en el Crypto.com Arena en el centro de Los Ángeles (California).

World.title: Robert Pattinson será el nuevo James Bond
World.content:
El londinense Robert Pattinson será, a sus 40 años, el nuevo James Bond, según se ha anunciado en las redes sociales del personaje, creado por Ian Fleming. Pattinson tendrá que compaginar este personaje con el de Batman, del que acaba de terminar su segunda película como protagonista.

El filme, que dirigirá Denis Villeneuve, que ya ha trabajado con Pattinson en Dune, es la primera producción de Amazon Prime Video con el agente secreto; Amazon ha optado por un actor muy popular, de las estrellas de su generación, en vez de lo ocurrido anteriormente con los 007 previos: buenos intérpretes, aunque no estrellas.

Su elección, el primer nuevo Bond tras dos décadas, en las que se hizo cargo del personaje Daniel Craig, era un rumor que corría por Hollywood. Hace tres fines de semana hicieron pruebas de cámara Collom Turner —el favorito de Brosnan, uno de los 007 previos—, Jack Lowden —el preferido de los fans más clásicos— y Josh O’Connor. Rápidamente se supo que Villeneuve y los productores Amy Pascal y David Heyman, a quienes Amazon Studios les había otorgado el mando del proyecto, estaban valorando sus habilidades en las secuencias de acción, es decir, su capacidad de hacer acrobacias, su presencia ante la cámara y su talento en las réplicas y contrarreplicas con un hipotético guion. Más tarde, medios especializados subrayaron que había más intérpretes en liza, bien porque sus nombres no habían sido publicitados, bien porque el trío no había convencido esos días. Y a ellos se sumaron Nicholas Hoult y Pattinson a finales de octubre. Curiosamente, eran los dos intérpretes finalistas en la última elección de Batman. Y Pattinson ha vuelto a derrotar a Hoult.

“James Bond es uno de los personajes más legendarios del cine, y que se me confíe 007 es el honor de una vida”, asegura Pattinson en un comunicado oficial. “Estoy profundamente agradecido a Denis, Amy, David, Tanya y a todos en Amazon MGM Studios por su confianza en mí. Decir que este papel es un sueño hecho realidad es quedarse corto. No podría estar más entusiasmado con esta colaboración y el trabajo que me espera con este equipo fantástico”.

Amazon MGM Studios tomó el control creativo de la franquicia de James Bond hace dos años. Los Broccoli, familia heredera de la saga del agente 007, vendió los derechos, que hasta entonces controlaban los hermanastros Michael G. Wilson y Barbara Broccoli, desde que sucedieron a su padre, el productor Albert Cubby Broccoli. Amazon había comprado MGM en 2022 por 8.500 millones de dólares (8.000 millones de euros), con su vasto catálogo de más de 4.000 películas y 17.000 programas de televisión. En el paquete también se incluían los derechos de distribución de las películas de James Bond. Pero no el poder de decisión creativa. Eso se lo compró a Broccoli y Wilson por otros 1.000 millones de dólares.

Los actores que han interpretado a James Bond. En la fila de arriba, desde la izquierda, Sean Connery, George Lazenby y Roger Moore. En la fila de abajo, Timothy Dalton, Pierce Brosnan y Daniel Craig. EL PAÍS

En The Hollywood Reporter apuntan que Villeneuve llamó ayer domingo por la mañana a Pattinson para anunciarle la decisión, y Pascal hizo lo mismo con los descartados. Sin embargo, fuentes de la industria como Matthew Belloni, responsable del podcast Puck, daban por hecho lo de Pattinson, porque el londinense había firmado un contrato por tres películas y un suculento porcentaje de la taquilla; el resto había firmado por cuatro filmes, y con ingresos menores.

En ese mismo comunicado oficial, Villeneuve, que estrenará junto a Pattinson el 18 de diciembre Dune 3, comenta: “Antes que nada, quiero expresar mi profundo agradecimiento a los actores extraordinarios que nos acompañaron en este viaje. Estábamos rodeados de un talento extraordinario, pero solo puede haber un 007. Me alegra mucho dar la bienvenida a Robert Pattinson como nuestro nuevo James Bond. Tiene el alma atemporal de 007 y aporta un espíritu completamente nuevo. No puedo esperar para empezar”.

Más información Las 26 películas de James Bond, de la peor a la mejor

Hace 21 años, Daniel Craig, entonces con 35, fue anunciado en octubre de 2005 como el nuevo Bond, en un evento en el que apareció en una lancha militar a toda velocidad por el río Támesis, en el centro de Londres, perfectamente trajeado, aunque años después confesaría que “muerto de miedo y de nervios”. Craig trajo a la franquicia un 007 más duro. Lo ha encarnado en cinco películas, acabando su ciclo en 2021 con Sin tiempo para morir. Su mayor éxito fue Skyfall (2012), que recaudó más de 1.000 millones de dólares en taquilla.

Dos empleadas preparan las figuras de cera de los actores que han reencarnado a James Bond en la gran pantalla en el Museo de Madame Tussauds de Londres (Reino Unido) en diciembre de 2015. JONATHAN HORDLE (EFE)

Hay que recordar que a Bond siempre le han encarnado actores sin aura de estrella. Sean Connery era poco conocido antes de Bond, al que empezó a poner rostro en 1962, en Agente 007 contra el doctor No. George Lazenby nunca había actuado más allá de algunos anuncios, y tras una única película, Al servicio secreto de su Majestad, fue despedido por su falta de carisma. Tuvo que volver Connery en un último trabajo, Diamantes para la eternidad, porque la primera opción, Roger Moore, priorizó su trabajo en la serie El Santo. Después, sí, Moore fue presentado en un hotel de París, y le dio la gran pátina de ironía y pop al personaje. En 1987 entró un gran bond, Timothy Dalton, actor de prestigio teatral y poco cine a sus espaldas, porque el elegido, Pierce Brosnan, estaba atado contractualmente para la serie Remington Steele. Después de dos entregas protagonizadas por Dalton, llegaron las cuatro de Brosnan, que se despidió de 007 en Muere otro día (2002). En realidad, en cine solo Craig había participado previamente en buenas películas, como Camino a la perdición, Layer Cake, Some Voices, The Mother y Múnich.

Si se cuenta a David Niven, que dio vida a 007 en la versión de 1967 de Casino Royale, que no perteneció oficialmente a la saga, Pattinson será el octavo actor en interpretarlo en el cine (hubo una serie de televisión previa). Este 2026 está siendo un año fructífero para el intérprete que empezó en la saga Harry Potter y se hizo popular con otra, Crepúsculo. Está acabando Batman II, ha estrenado La odisea, El drama y Primetime, con la que podría ser hasta candidato al Oscar, y el 18 de diciembre estará en las multisalas de casi todo el mundo con Dune 3. Y después, ya en 2027, estrenará The Take, de Fernando Meirelles.

World.title: Outcry over “cruel” plan to send failed asylum seekers to Rwanda
World.content:
Some 46 human rights, civil society and trade union organisations have signed a letter objecting to the “cruel” plan presented by the Netherlands and four other EU member states on Monday to begin sending asylum seekers whose applications have been rejected to Rwanda.

The plan, presented in Vienna on Monday, will pave the way for people to be sent to “deportation hubs” in Rwanda, on the idea that it will help secure national borders and break apart human trafficking networks. The reality, the signatories say, is that this is just a euphemism for forced deportation and will deteriorate security.

Dutch foreign affairs minister Tom Berendsen joined counterparts from Austria, Denmark, Germany and Greece at the conference. The letter of objection notes that the vulnerable people will be sent to a place that they have never been to, have no connection to, and which has a serious ongoing record of human rights violations.

“It signals that member states accept the risk of serious human rights violations against one of the most marginalised groups in society, in return for a deterrence goal that evidence clearly suggests they will not reach. Such cruel measures drive people into further insecurity, and risk making migration routes more dangerous,” the letter states.

Berendsen said at the press conference after the event that “effective return is important” and that through the deal the Netherlands is “taking a concrete step towards a better migration system by establishing a return hub in Rwanda.”

He also spoke of the need for economic development in Rwanda, though how the deal will work is unclear. According to broadcaster NOS, Rwanda wants economic support in return, and the five countries will share the costs, which have not been made public. Rwanda will initially offer around 100 places, and only single men will be sent at first.

A spokesperson from asylum foundation Stichting Vluchteling told Dutch News: “We are against this concept as a humanitarian organisation. Member states are responsible for these people. We’re very concerned about the situation in Rwanda. We see human rights abuses on press freedom. We don’t believe there will be the possibility for independent monitoring from member states.”

The spokesperson said the talk of improving human rights through this agreement was nothing but “pretty words”.

They said that the move sends a signal that Europe does not want to accept its responsibility for asylum seekers. “This is super dangerous. Even if one person is sent over the next couple of years, it sends a signal that we don’t want you here and that we’re willing to go quite far to remove you.”

There is a critical shortage of asylum beds in the Netherlands, with many taken by people whose applications have been rejected but are stuck in legal limbo. But the spokesperson said “this is not a numbers crisis, it’s a political crisis. The focus should be on obligations that member states have, which is that we’re responsible for people who are rejected.”

The letter also warns that the EU’s proposed new rules for border agency Frontex would allow it to support returns to non-EU countries, including a possible role in running “return hubs”. Frontex already operates with “a de facto lack of accountability”, the organisations say, and the proposal would remove the obligation to assign at least one fundamental rights monitor to each operation.

The Dutch foreign ministry’s own country report on Rwanda, which the immigration service IND uses to assess asylum claims, records extrajudicial killings, enforced disappearances and torture in unofficial detention centres.

The letter also warned that “by relying on third countries to take on its protection obligations, the EU makes itself dependent on non-EU states, enabling third countries to leverage migration in line with their own political agenda.”

World.title: King raises history of slavery at ceremony to mark First Salute
World.content:
King Willem-Alexander has acknowledged the role of the Dutch Caribbean islands in the transatlantic slave trade during a ceremony to mark the 250th anniversary of the Netherlands’ recognition of the United States.

The king was speaking on Statia Day, a national holiday on the island of Sint Eustatius to mark the First Salute, when a Dutch cannon was fired from Fort Orange to return a salute from the American ship Andrew Doria.

The event on November 16, 1776, is seen as the first formal recognition of the USA by a foreign power after the Declaration of Independence in July that year.

At the time the island was a Dutch colony with around 70 slave plantations. Today it is a special municipality of the Netherlands with a population of around 3,300.

During his speech on Monday, the king referred to the recently published study into the royal family’s role in slavery, which concluded that the house of Oranje-Nassau earned more than €500 million from the colonies since the 17th century.

Prime minister Rob Jetten had also been due to attend the ceremony, but he was forced to stay in the Netherlands for crisis talks with his coalition partners after last week’s budget vote brought his cabinet to the brink of collapse.

Common history

“The First Salute is a milestone in history, but our common history goes far wider,” the king said. “There is also the story of Statia as a place to commemorate slavery.

“In the 17th and 18th centuries several thousand people from west Africa landed here. After an inhumane journey of two months, packed into the bowels of ships with no more than two square metres per person, there was no salute for them on their arrival.”

He said that he had been moved by the results of four years of research into slavery, led by Leiden university professor of colonial history, Geert Oostindië, which he commissioned and paid for.

“I know that life on this isolated island is not easy for many people,” he said. “Groceries are expensive, there are few jobs to be had and healthcare is limited.” He added he would continue to work for “fair opportunities and a good life for everyone.”

World.title: More than 14,000 bogus police officers recorded this year so far
World.content:
The number of cases of people being approached by bogus police officers is continuing to rise despite efforts to warn elderly residents to watch out for doorstep conmen.

In 2023 police received just over 500 reports of people being tricked by criminals posing as officers who tried to persuade them to hand over cash and valuables, but in the last three years the number has exploded.

Police suspect that organised gangs are behind the trend, which saw the number rise to 13,000 last year and 14,176 in the first 10 months of 2026. Nearly 3,300 official crime reports have been filed of theft by bogus police officers, suggesting around a quarter of attempts are successful. The oldest victim was 103.

Criminals typically appear on the victim’s doorstep and tell them that thieves are operating in the area. They then offer to take in cash and other valuable items such as jewellery for safekeeping.

Some offenders dress in clothes resembling police uniforms, while others wear casual clothing and tell their victims they are working with CID.

Police said genuine officers will never offer to take away items from householders and anyone with doubts about an officer on the doorstep should call 112 to find out if police are making enquiries in their neighbourhood.

Information campaign

Last year police and Omroep MAX, which broadcasts daytime TV programmes on NPO, ran an information campaign highlighting the doorstep techniques used by bogus officers.

“We do a lot of work to prevent and detect these offences,” said Sybren van der Velden Walda, national co-ordinator for high impact crime. “But it’s evidently so lucrative that criminals keep posing as police officers to rob people.”

So far this year 783 people have been arrested on suspicion of pretending to be police officers, one of whom was a 13-year-old boy who stole a bank card and €20,000 worth of jewellery. Police say it is likely he was working for gangsters.

“We see it is a vulnerable group who are recruited by organised criminals to do things like this,” said Van der Velden Walda.

He added that the prevalence of bogus officers was making it harder for his colleagues to carry out genuine police work.

“Elderly people won’t open the door any more because they don’t trust police at the door,” he said.

World.title: Preventative health made accessible for internationals
World.content:
For many new internationals, going to a Dutch doctor, or huisarts, takes a bit of time getting used to. With a more hands-off approach to healthcare than in many other countries, you often don’t get to your huisarts until you have symptoms you want checked.

But what if you want to understand your health before symptoms appear? Knowing what to check, and which lifestyle changes could make a difference, isn’t always straightforward.

Enter Blue Health Intelligence, a health-tech startup that offers a 360-health check, providing insight into cardiovascular health, metabolism and liver and kidney functions within an hour, sharing results immediately in a consultation with a doctor.

“In countries such as Japan, Germany and the UK, periodic health checks are already embedded in the healthcare system, but that is not yet the case in the Netherlands,” says Onno Huyghe, CEO and co-founder of Blue Health Intelligence. “By gaining earlier insight into their health, people can stay healthy for longer and health issues can be prevented. We aim to make prevention more accessible to many people.”

According to the World Health Organization (WHO), approximately 1.8 million deaths from noncommunicable diseases are avoidable each year in Europe. About 60% are linked to changeable risk factors – such as tobacco and alcohol use, high blood pressure, unhealthy diets, obesity and physical inactivity – while the remaining 40% could be prevented or delayed through timely diagnosis and high-quality health care.

For €299, you get a 360-degree health check that uses hundreds of data points, the results of which are discussed immediately on-site with a doctor and uploaded to the Blue app. The 10 tests administered include an ECG, 3D body scan, blood analysis and an ultrasound.

“You don’t always realise how much your health risks increase as you get older,” says customer Petra. “For me, the health check at Blue Health was a real eye-opener. Under professional guidance, you’re efficiently taken through all the tests in a short time.”

If something is discovered, Blue Health Intelligence offers a free follow-up before passing that information on to your huisarts.

As common as an annual dental check-up

“Our participants gain a comprehensive understanding of their health and potential health risks,” says Leanne Verdonck, physician and co-founder of Blue Health Intelligence. “Our goal is for a regular health check to become just as common as going to the dentist.”

At its modern, state-of-the-art facility on Amsterdam’s Prinsengracht, Blue Health Intelligence has made preventative healthcare affordable. It follows the growing trend in the health and wellness sector of getting insight into people’s potential health risks, advising them on healthy lifestyle changes in a personalized plan that is then shared in the app.

Having recently secured €3.4 million in funding, Blue Health Intelligence plans to expand its capacity in Amsterdam and even internationally, including in Paris and Milan, while continuing to develop its preventative health platform.

More than 2,500 people have already booked a health check with Blue Health Intelligence. Due to high demand, bookings are now offered through a waitlist. If you choose to join, Blue will contact you when it’s your turn to book, with appointments a few days away.

Click on the link if you want to join.

World.title: Dutch influencer still held by ICE with no reason given, family
World.content:
Dutch influencer and OnlyFans model Vera Dijkmans, who was arrested five days ago by US ICE agents, remains in custody without any reason given for her detention, according to her family, who also say she is being held in dire conditions.

Dijkmans has millions of social media followers and often does promotional work with UFC fighters. She was arrested at Newark airport where she’d travelled to from Miami for an event.

Her details don’t show up on the ICE database and no details have been made public as to why she was detained. Her mother, who has travelled there to protest for her release, said “we fear for her life”, adding that “she is in a room with twelve other women, receives little food and drink, and there is barely any fresh air. The conditions are inhumane,” AD reported.

Dijkmans is staying in the US on a B2 visa that allows you to be in the country without working for up to six months. She had applied for a permanent residency there and may have missed an appointment for that application procedure, her mother speculated to AD.

The US government warned people this year that using social media for commercial purposes was not allowed on a tourist visa.

ICE, which was expanded by the Trump administration to round up and deport people from the country who do not have the correct paperwork, often targets people who have failed to comply with visa rules.

Delaney Hall, the immigration detention centre in Newark where Dijkmans is being held, is run by private prison company GEO Group, which was awarded a 15-year, $1 billion contract by ICE in 2025 to detain up to 1,000 people there. It is notorious for its harsh conditions.

The Dutch foreign affairs ministry told AD it is aware of Dijkmans’ situation and is providing consular assistance, though it did not say what that entails.

World.title: Man recovered after operation to remove 10kg tumour from stomach
World.content:
Surgeons in Groningen have removed a tumour weighing more than 10 kilograms from the intestines of a man in a ground-breaking operation.

The benign tumour, described as being the size of a large basketball, had been growing slowly in the patient’s stomach for around 25 years and almost entirely filled his stomach cavity.

It was discovered by accident when the man, 68-year-old Ronald van de Kimmenade, went to hospital with a lung infection. Further investigations revealed he had been gaining weight since 2000 without suspecting the cause.

“He had no symptoms at that time that indicated the huge aberration in his stomach,” said surgeon Sijbrand Hofker.

Hofker initially decided not to operate because the tumour was not malignant, but changed his mind a year later when it became so large that it threatened to cause massive blood loss.

The 10-hour operation involved removing Van de Kimmenade’s intestines with the tumour, keeping them refrigerated and replacing them afterwards. It is the first time in Europe that a so-called “autotransplant” has been performed successfully.

No donor organ

Hofker explained on the university hospital’s website that Van de Kimmenade was not eligible for a regular transplant with a donor organ and a standard operation would have left him dependent on tube feeding for the rest of his life.

“I spent a lot of time beforehand studying images of his intestines and the tumour. I had to work out exactly what route we would follow during the operation so that we could remove the tumour and reconnect the major arteries.

“What you don’t know beforehand is what it will actually look like when you come to perform the operation. You have to estimate based on your experience if it is technically possible and if the patient can endure the operation.

“Our aim was to remove the tumour without the patient losing his intestines so that he could lead a normal life.”

Van de Kimmenade, who underwent the operation a year ago, said the operation had been lifesaving.

“Before the operation I had to undergo a huge number of blood transfusions. I had 35 bags of blood in a year,” he said.

“I was frequently tired, had little energy and threw up when the temperature changed.

“Now I have occasional check-ups and that’s all. I’m back at work and am going to keep working for longer. Beforehand I was glad to have retired. Now I think: if I sit still I’m just going to get old and I’m still much too young for that.”

World.title: Heirs seek to stop $180m Van Gogh sale, citing Nazi-era duress
World.content:
The heirs of a German Jewish publisher have asked Sotheby’s to withdraw a Van Gogh painting from auction in New York this week. They say their family was forced to sell it in Amsterdam in 1936 under the pressure of Nazi persecution, and it should be withdrawn from the auction.

Châtaigniers en fleurs (Blossoming Chestnut Trees), which Van Gogh painted in May 1890, weeks before his death, is the top piece in Sotheby’s sale of the Blaquier-Arrieta collection on Wednesday, according to the Volkskrant.

The auction house has put an unofficial estimate of around $180 million (€156 million) on the work, which would beat the artist’s auction record of $117.2 million (€106 million), set at Christie’s in 2022.

Samuel Fischer, a Jewish publisher in Berlin, bought the painting in 1909, according to Sotheby’s catalogue. In the early 1930s it was placed with an art dealer in Amsterdam.

The heirs say the family fled Berlin for Vienna in 1936 and that the painting was sold three months later, after their publishing house had suffered heavy losses under Nazi rule.

In an email seen by The New York Times, the heirs’ lawyer, Gunnar Schnabel, asked Sotheby’s to prove that the painting was sold at market value and that the sale would have happened without Nazi pressure. Otherwise, he wrote, “no auction may take place.”

Sotheby’s says its research has not shown that the painting was sold under duress, and that it is in talks with the heirs. It told ARTnews that the painting sold for 68,000 Swiss francs in June 1936, which it considers a good price.

International guidelines backed by the Netherlands and the United States say that sales made under financial pressure from Nazi persecution can count as involuntary, but the guidelines are not legally binding.

The Argentine collectors Carlos Pedro Blaquier and Nelly Arrieta de Blaquier bought the painting in 1975. It has not been shown in public since 1964. As of Monday, Sotheby’s had not said whether it would stay in Wednesday’s sale.

World.title: Bird flu found on four farms in Gelderland in last week
World.content:
Nearly a quarter of a million birds have been slaughtered at four poultry farms in Gelderland in the last week in an effort to contain an outbreak of bird flu.

On Sunday the food standards agency NVWA confirmed that 60,000 chickens were exterminated at a battery farm in Oldebroek, 20km from a farm in Hierden where 19,000 ducks and chickens were killed the previous day.

Earlier in the week 165,000 birds were slaughtered at two other poultry farms in Hierden after bird flu infections were detected.

Local mayor Tanja Haseloop-Amsing told Omroep Gelderland that the development was a “huge blow” for the affected farmers and their employees.

“Our thoughts are with them and we wish them strength in these difficult times,” she said. “I am asking people to keep away from the business and respect the privacy of the owner and his surroundings.”

All poultry farmers in the Netherlands have been ordered to keep their birds in coops since October 28 after the first cases of bird flu were detected in Groningen. Infected birds have also been found in Germany, Denmark and the UK.

The NVWA has set up three exclusion zones around the infected businesses. All transport is banned within a 10km radius and farms within 3km of the infection will be screened for outbreaks.

Any farm within 1km of an infection site will be intensively monitored for 14 days.

World.title: Ukraine blames Russia for graffiti glorifying WWII Ukrainian nationalists on Polish monuments
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Around a dozen public monuments in Poland, including one dedicated to the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising, have been defaced with graffiti glorifying the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA), a World War Two nationalist partisan group that was responsible for the massacre of Poles and Jews. Ukraine’s embassy in Warsaw has condemned the vandalism and blamed it on Russia, which has previously been accused by the Polish authorities of orchestrating provocative graffiti on monuments. W sobotę, 14 listopada, w Warszawie doszło do kolejnych dwóch dewastacji pomników. Napisy „Slava UPA” pojawiły się na Pomniku Bohaterów Getta przed Muzeum Historii Żydów Polskich POLIN oraz na Pomniku Żołnierzy 1 Armii Wojska Polskiego przy ulicy Andersa 13. To kolejna odsłona… pic.twitter.com/Y7NDsfpjxn — Miejski Reporter (@MiejskiReporter) November 14, 2026 The latest spate of vandalism was first reported in early November in the western city of Poznań, where three World War two memorials were painted with graffiti saying “Glory to the UPA” (Slawa UPA). While the UPA is remembered by many in Ukraine for fighting for independence from Moscow-imposed Soviet rule, in Poland it is primarily associated with leading the Volhynia massacres, in which around 100,000 Polish civilians, mostly women and children, were slaughtered as part of an ethnic cleansing operation. Local police in Poznań told the Gazeta Wyborcza daily that they were searching for a young man dressed in black who is believed to be the culprit, but have so far not been able to identify him. Similar graffiti was subsequently reported on seven monuments, including ones dedicated to Polish World War Two heroes and anti-communist protests that took place in 1970, in Gdańsk and Gdynia, neighbouring cities on Poland’s northern Baltic coast. On Friday, local police in Gdańsk confirmed that they had detained a 17-year-old Ukrainian on suspicion of “painting offensive slogans propagating hatred”. They shared blurred-out images of the suspect as well as cans of spray paint. He has been charged with promoting fascist ideology, incitement to violence and hatred based on nationality, and desecration of monuments. If convicted, he could face up to three years in prison. Previously, on Tuesday this week, MOST, a Polish-based Belarusian independent media outlet, published findings that an anonymous person on messaging service Telegram, which is popular among Russians, Ukrainians and Belarusians, had been offering $500 plus travel expenses for a job in Poznań. When an undercover MOST journalist responded to the advert, he was told that the job would involve spray painting “Glory to the UPA” on monuments. The recruiter confirmed that the job was illegal, “but if you cover your face and do everything quickly, they won’t find you”. They also revealed that similar jobs were available in other Polish cities, including Warsaw, Wrocław and Lublin. Subsequently, similar inscriptions appeared in Warsaw on the Monument to the Ghetto Heroes, which honours the Jews who rose up against their German-Nazi oppressors in 1943; a monument commemorating the Polish First Army, which fought in World War Two; and a monument to sappers who served in the war. The vandalism was condemned by Poland’s Jewish Historical Institute (ŻIH), which called it a “disgraceful attack on the memory of the victims of the Holocaust and the heroes of Jewish resistance”. Noting MOST’s findings and the vandalism of other monuments, ŻIH said that “this points to the possibility of an organised provocation intended to incite hatred and divide society”. Warsaw police told PAP that they are investigating and seeking to identify the perpetrator. An unnamed police source also told Gazeta Wyborcza they see the incidents in all four cities as related to one another, pointing to the similar style of the inscriptions. On Sunday afternoon, Warsaw’s mayor, Rafał Trzaskowski, condemned the vandalism and shared images of the municipal authorities cleaning the graffiti off the Ghetto Heroes Monument. “Given the scale of similar incidents in other cities, we must consider the possibility that this is a planned provocation,” added the mayor. “Let us not let ourselves be divided – the authorities are working to identify both those who carried out these acts and those who ordered them.” Nie ma zgody na wandalizm w Warszawie. Minionej nocy służby miejskie wyczyściły pomniki oszpecone przez wandali – między innymi Pomnik Bohaterów Getta. Sprawców szuka policja. Patrząc na skalę podobnych incydentów w innych miastach, musimy brać pod uwagę, że mamy do czynienia… pic.twitter.com/5xMgPhnHf8 — Rafał Trzaskowski (@trzaskowski_) November 15, 2026 A day earlier, on Saturday, the Ukrainian embassy had also condemned the acts of vandalism, calling them a “disgraceful provocation”. “In our view, these unlawful acts are a manifestation of the hybrid war that Russia is attempting to wage by any means in European states, and in Poland in particular,” wrote the embassy. “The objective is clear: to incite hostility between Poles and Ukrainians, undermine mutual trust, and weaken support for Ukraine.” Writing in both Polish and Ukrainian, the embassy appealed to Ukrainians “not to be tempted by offers of ‘easy money’ in exchange for painting graffiti, damaging property, or carrying out other illegal tasks” and to report any such offers to the Polish police. “Let us respect the laws of the country in which we reside, as well as historical memory and each other’s dignity,” they added. “Polish-Ukrainian solidarity is our shared strength. Let us not allow the enemy to destroy it.” Poland has been a primary target for Russia’s so-called hybrid actions in Europe, which have included acts of sabotage, espionage, disinformation and efforts to stir hostility towards Ukrainians. Such operations are rarely carried out by Russian operatives themselves. Instead, Russia often recruits people already on the ground, often members of Poland’s large Ukrainian and Belarusian migrant communities, as well as Poles themselves in some cases. In July this year, a Ukrainian teenager was indicted by Polish prosecutors on charges of painting dozens of pro-UPA slogans in public places, including on a monument to victims of the Volhynia massacres. An 18-year-old Ukrainian will stand trial in Poland accused of working on behalf of Russia to stir tension between Poland and Ukraine by painting dozens of inscriptions in public places glorifying the Ukrainian Insurgent Army, which massacred Poles in WWII https://t.co/0w0gVYiGpp — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 16, 2026 There have long been tensions between Poland and Ukraine over the massacres, which Poland recognises as a genocide. Ukraine rejects that label, and also continues to honour the UPA for its role in fighting for independence. The issue has recently flared up again this year after President Volodymyr Zelensky named a Ukrainian military unit after the “heroes of the UPA”. That sparked widespread anger in Poland and prompted Polish President Karol Nawrocki to strip Zelensky of his country’s highest honour. World.title: Polish president vetoes law on removing harmful online content, warning of “censorship”
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. President Karol Nawrocki has vetoed a government bill creating new powers to block harmful online content. Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition, argued that the measures were too far-reaching and could be abused to introduce “censorship”. Government figures have strongly criticised the president’s decision, arguing that it will leave young people in particular more exposed to dangerous content. It also means that Poland still has not fully implemented the European Union’s Digital Services Act (DSA). ❌ Nie dla cenzury Internetu! pic.twitter.com/WusnK7LImD — Kancelaria Prezydenta RP (@prezydentpl) November 13, 2026 Previously, in January this year, Nawrocki had vetoed an earlier bill intended to implement the DSA, describing the measures as “Owellian”. That prompted the government to split the legislation in two. In September, Nawrocki agreed to sign one of those bills, which appointed the president of the Office of Electronic Communications (UKE) as Poland’s digital services coordinator, responsible for overseeing enforcement of the DSA. A second bill was then needed to introduce the actual powers to block harmful online content. In October, it was approved in parliament by the ruling coalition, which ranges from left to centre right. The right-wing and far-right opposition either voted against it or abstained. Among the new powers included in the legislation were authorisation for the heads of UKE and the National Broadcasting Council (KRRiT) to order the blocking of online content containing violence or threats based on race, nationality, ethnicity, religion or political affiliation. It also allowed the immediate blocking, at the request of a prosecutor or the police, of content involving the acceptance of a contract to commit murder or inciting or assisting in suicide or self-harm. “Perpetrators of serious crimes should not be allowed to use the internet to spread violence and threats,” said digital affairs minister Krzysztof Gawkowski. “The state must have effective tools to quickly respond to such threats. The safety of internet users must transcend political divisions.” The government also argued that last month’s series of stabbings in schools and this month’s deadly terrorist attack in Kraków – which have raised concern about the online radicalisation of young people – have emphasised the importance of tough controls over digital content. There are "strong traces of right-wing extremism" in the activity of the man who carried out the mass shooting in Kraków, says Poland's justice minister. His search history included websites relating to Anders Breivik, the Norwegian far-right terrorist https://t.co/UhVbkWSaCq — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 10, 2026 However, on Friday, the final day by which the president had to make a decision on the bill, Nawrocki announced that he was vetoing it. He argued that “the government has clearly mixed up European obligations with its own political interests”. The measures in the bill threaten to create a “censorship official” and “essentially give the government arbitrary control and the ability to decide what we can and cannot say, write or publish, said the president. Decisions on whether content is permitted or not should be “the exclusive competence of the justice system and independent judges”, he argued. Nawrocki also said that the powers in the vetoed bill were “disproportionate”, allowing an entire domain to be blocked due to a single example of illegal content. “The security of citizens cannot be a pretext for weakening their freedoms,” said Nawrocki. “We must not create a false choice: either the security or the freedom of its citizens. A responsible state must ensure and balance both.” Dlaczego Prezydent RP Karol Nawrocki zawetował ustawę o DSA? ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/1BUJVFEftl — Kancelaria Prezydenta RP (@prezydentpl) November 13, 2026 Deputy digital affairs minister Dariusz Standerski, however, said that the president was “not defending free speech” but instead “once again siding with global [digital] platforms and allowing them to decide what users see”. “The vetoed provisions concerned illegal content, not opinions or views expressed online,” added the ministry, which also noted that all decisions on blocking content were subject to appeals and judicial review. Prime Minister Donald Tusk, meanwhile, accused Nawrocki of “waging war on the government at the expense of Polish children and Polish security”, which would both be threatened by the absence of the vetoed measures. Z prezydenckiego weta zadowoleni są hejterzy, rosyjskie farmy trolli, pedofile, ekstremalni nihiliści i lobbyści. Ofiarami tego weta są polskie dzieci, rodzice, bezpieczeństwo wszystkich obywateli. Tego nie da się w żaden sposób usprawiedliwić. — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) November 14, 2026 Aleksandra Wójtowicz, an analyst on new technologies at the Polish Institute of International Affairs (PISM), told the Fakt newspaper that the measures do “not in any way relate to alleged censorship”. They are intended to force digital platforms to remove illegal content, she explained. Wójtowicz added that the measures would actually have protected free speech by giving Polish users whose accounts were unjustly deleted by social media platforms the right to appeal against those decisions outside of the platform itself. However, Nawrocki’s veto was praised by Przemysław Czarnek, deputy leader of the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), Poland’s largest opposition party. Czarnek told TV Trwam that the proposed measures had been intended to “fight the opposition” rather than actual hate speech. World.title: Poland research hub launched at Oxford University
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! A new hub has opened at the University of Oxford to support research cooperation with Poland, offering grants for academic projects, visits, training and workshops. The Oxford Poland Hub, which its organisers describe as Poland’s first initiative of its kind anywhere in the world, will also hold public events exploring Polish history, language and culture. We’re proud to have worked on the Oxford-Poland Hub & helped make it a reality together with great partners 🇵🇱🇬🇧 Huge thanks to: 🔹 @UniofOxford & @JesusOxford, esp. Prof Paulina Kewes & Dr Marek Naczyk 🔹 Ministry of Science and Higher Education & Minister @MarcinKulasek 🧵 pic.twitter.com/LghfpOhptC — Polish Embassy UK 🇵🇱 (@PolishEmbassyUK) November 12, 2026 “The launch of the Oxford-Poland Hub is an exciting new chapter in Oxford’s longstanding relationship with Poland,” said the University of Oxford’s vice-chancellor, Irene Tracey. “[It] will create new opportunities for academic exchange, collaborative research and partnership between Oxford and Poland.” The centre is initially funded for three years by Poland’s National Agency for Academic Exchange (NAWA), with support from the science and higher education ministry. It will operate within The Oxford Research Centre in the Humanities (TORCH). “The Oxford Poland Hub…gives us a permanent institutional presence at one of the world’s leading academic centres,” said Wojciech Karczewski, NAWA’s director general. “We see it as an investment in long-term partnerships that will enable researchers from Poland and Oxford to tackle increasingly ambitious research challenges together.” The University of Oxford is the oldest university in the English-speaking world and one of the most prestigious. It ranked first globally in the latest Times Higher Education World University Rankings. The new centre will offer grants of up to £5,000 (26,400 zloty) to support research projects or academic visits and up to £10,000 for academic workshops. Training scholarships are due to be introduced from the hub’s second year. All researchers affiliated with the University of Oxford will be eligible to apply for funding if their work involves collaboration with researchers based in Poland. The hub will focus on humanities and social sciences as well as cooperation with Oxford’s libraries and museums. The hub will also organise public lectures, exhibitions and events related to Polish history, language and culture for the academic community and Oxford’s residents, including its Polish community. 🇵🇱🇬🇧 Oxford-Poland Hub oficjalnie otwarty! Polska nauka zyskuje nowe możliwości współpracy z Uniwersytetem Oksfordzkim. W uroczystym otwarciu wziął udział minister nauki i szkolnictwa wyższego Marcin Kulasek. Centrum powstało dzięki współpracy Ministerstwa Nauki i Szkolnictwa… pic.twitter.com/bZaCdM3Y53 — Ministerstwo Nauki i Szkolnictwa Wyższego (@MNiSW_GOV__PL) November 10, 2026 The hub was inaugurated on Monday at Jesus College, one of Oxford University’s colleges, with Poland’s science and higher education minister, Marcin Kulasek, and Rafał Wiśniewski, chargé d’affaires at the Polish Embassy in London, among those attending. “Poland and the United Kingdom have for many years developed strong cooperation in science and higher education through joint research projects, academic mobility programmes and institutional partnerships,” Kulasek said. “The Oxford–Poland Hub opens a new chapter in this cooperation.” The centre is directed by Paulina Kewes, a professor of English literature at Oxford who was born in Poland. Professor Norman Davies, the renowned historian of Poland and an honorary fellow at St Antony’s College, Oxford, attended the launch. The inaugural lecture, given by Dariusz Wójcik, a professor at the National University of Singapore and honorary research associate at the University of Oxford, discussed Maria Czaplicka, the renowned Polish academic who in 1916 became Oxford’s first female lecturer of anthropology. A Belgian court has overturned an order to seize funds from Poland’s air-traffic control agency, PANSA, as part of pharmaceutical giant Pfizer’s efforts to enforce a €1.3 billion claim for COVID-19 vaccines Poland ordered but later refused to receive and pay for. The ruling, issued on Thursday, followed a legal challenge by PANSA to the freezing of its funds. It argued that it was not a party to the dispute between Pfizer and the Polish state. ❗️Dziś Francuskojęzyczny Sąd Pierwszej Instancji w Brukseli wydał korzystny dla strony polskiej wyrok w sprawie zajęcia opłat trasowych należnych @PANSA_PL , pobieranych za pośrednictwem EUROCONTROL. Sąd uznał zajęcie za bezzasadne i uchylił postanowienie, na podstawie którego… pic.twitter.com/EHvHZnL6ab — Ministerstwo Zdrowia (@MZ_GOV_PL) November 12, 2026 In July this year, PANSA announced that it had been cut off from the fees paid to it by the European Organisation for the Safety of Air Navigation (Eurocontrol), which manages air traffic in Europe. Around 80% of PANSA’s revenue comes from those fees. Eurocontrol is based in Belgium, which is where Pfizer has been fighting its legal battle against Poland over the unpaid vaccines. The move to freeze PANSA’s funds was part of Pfizer’s efforts to claim money it had been awarded from Poland by a Belgian court in April this year. Prime Minister Donald Tusk pledged government support to ensure PANSA had sufficient funds to maintain its operations and assured that air safety would not be compromised. Poland’s air-traffic control agency has been cut off from most of its revenue as part of efforts by pharmaceutical giant Pfizer to enforce a Belgian court ruling requiring Poland to pay €1.3bn for Covid vaccines it ordered but then refused to receive https://t.co/Nd9IyLqmmf — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 11, 2026 On Thursday this week, PANSA announced that its legal challenge to the seizure of its assets by bailiffs had been successful, though it noted that the ruling can still be appealed. Poland’s health ministry, which has been involved in overseeing the legal battle with Pfizer, said that the Belgian court had confirmed that PANSA’s funds belong to the agency itself, not to the State treasury. “The agency is a separate legal entity; it possesses its own assets and manages its own finances independently. It is not liable for the obligations of the State treasury; therefore, its funds cannot be used to satisfy Pfizer’s claims against Poland,” wrote the ministry. In comments to Polish Radio, PANSA chief Magdalena Jaworska-Maćkowiak said the agency had become a hostage in a case “that did not, in fact, concern us”. “It stemmed from an entirely separate dispute,” she noted. “This created extreme difficulties, as we were relying on a ‘bridge’ financing arrangement that, under current law, could not provide us with long-term stability.” Pfizer, meanwhile, said Thursday’s court decision affected only one avenue of its efforts to enforce payment of the April ruling. “We are taking ​appropriate steps through ​established legal ⁠and contractual mechanisms to ensure compliance with the court’s [April] decision,” it added, quoted by Reuters. Sąd w Brukseli uznał sprzeciw PAŻP wobec zajęcia komorniczego dokonanego na wniosek Pfizer za zasadny i uchylił postanowienie z 25 czerwca 2026 r., stanowiące podstawę zajęcia komorniczego. Rozstrzygnięcie jest zatem korzystne dla PAŻP, ale wyrok nie jest jeszcze prawomocny. — PANSA (@PANSA_PL) November 12, 2026 The dispute stems from Poland’s refusal in 2022 to accept and pay for COVID-19 vaccine doses ordered from Pfizer under European Union procurement agreements. In April 2022, the then health minister, Adam Niedzielski, invoked a force majeure clause following Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 Poland, which by then had already sold or donated some of its surplus vaccines, argued the mass influx of Ukrainian refugees strained its public finances, while its cases of Covid infections had dropped. Romania later made a similar decision to not comply with the contract. In 2023, Pfizer sued both countries in Belgium, the country where the contracts were signed. Over the course of the case, Poland also argued that Pfizer had potentially abused its market position. A Belgian court has ordered Poland to pay US pharmaceutical giant Pfizer around €1.3 billion for Covid vaccines ordered by the European Commission on behalf of member states during the pandemic but which the Polish government later refused to receive https://t.co/1ZtPgl8Y3o — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 2, 2026 But in April, a Belgian court rejected those arguments and ruled in Pfizer’s favour, ordering Poland to accept approximately 64 million vaccine doses and pay more than 5.6 billion zloty, plus interest and legal costs. Poland appealed against the judgment in August 2026. The health ministry said on Thursday it would not disclose details of its legal arguments or planned procedural steps while the proceedings remain ongoing.
