On self-reliance, he said that 'Aatmanirbharta' in national security meant having the freedom to make strategic choices, control critical technologies and maintain resilient supply chains, emphasising that self-reliance did not imply strategic isolation or manufacturing everything domestically.

He highlighted the importance of developing self-reliant space capabilities for India's preparedness for future warfare, citing the disruption of Starlink services during the Ukraine conflict. He said space has already become a key enabler of modern warfare and stressed the need for India to strengthen its capabilities in satellite-based intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance, communication and precision navigation.

World.title: Indian inventor patents new technique to transmute elements, reports gold in tests
World.content:
BENGALURU: What if one chemical element could be converted into several others, including gold? An Indian inventor from Bengaluru has received a patent for a process that could do this using specially generated frequencies, without conventional nuclear reactors or radioactive reactions.

There is no fission or fusion reaction here. His experiments report the presence of gold, silver and several other elements in processed samples.

Rajah Vijay Kumarâs invention, called Gravitoradiophysical Nuclear Transmutation (GNT), has been granted Indian patent (No. 5683222), nearly eight years after it was filed on Nov 21, 2017. The patent was granted in the second half of 2025.

âThe GNT could eventually find applications in energy, medicine, genetics, industry and space,â Kumar, director and chief scientific officer, Scalene Energy Research Institute, Organization de Scalene Foundation, told TOI.



How it works

To understand the process, it helps to know what makes one element different from another. Every element has atoms, and at the centre of each atom is a nucleus. The number of protons in this nucleus determines the elementâs identity.

Gold, for example, has 79 protons, while mercury has 80. Turning mercury into gold would therefore require changing the structure of its nucleus by removing (or displacing) one proton and one electron, something an ordinary chemical reaction cannot do.





.

Kumarâs proposed process uses a specially designed reactor to achieve this. Its central component, called the âBoom Tubeâ, a tubular reactor that produces continuous free fall and weightlessness at molecular levels, fitted with antennas made from an aluminium alloy and connected to a high power high frequency generator. The apparatus also has systems to regulate temperature and pressure in a vacuum environment.

The process works in two proposed stages. First, one frequency is used to separate the target element from the chemical compound containing it. A second frequency is then applied to bring about the proposed change in the element's nucleus.

The process works in two proposed stages. First, a disassociating frequency depending on the interested elements is used to separate the target element from the chemical compound containing it.

Then, an element specific transmutation frequency is then applied to bring about the proposed change in the element's nucleus. The exact mechanism of action is still being studied.

As Kumar explains: âEvery element has a unique frequency, or set of frequencies, that can break its chemical bonds and separate it from a compound. For the initial experiments, I chose mercury, which it describes as one of the heavier elements that could be handled relatively safely in its experimental setup.

The aim, however, was not simply to make gold.â

Larger ambition

The larger ambition was to develop a process that can convert different elements and isotopes for possible applications in energy, medicine, industry and space exploration.

The patent describes experiments in which a mercury compound, mercuric sulphate, was mixed with distilled water and processed through the reactor. An untreated portion was retained for comparison.

An accredited laboratory, reportedly unaware of which samples had been processed, analysed both.

The results reported gold at 1.91 mg per litre in the first processed sample and 2.3 milligrams per litre in the second. Silver was also detected at 11 milligrams per litre in the second test. Other elements, including magnesium, manganese, phosphorus and zinc, were reported in the processed samples. The mercury came down from 33.45 gm to 8.67 gm while sulphur almost remained unchanged at around 8.5 gm.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The laboratory used a technique called Inductively Coupled Plasma Atomic Emission Spectroscopy (ICP-AES), which identifies and measures the quantities of elements in a sample. The research team acknowledges that considerable work under different conditions remains before the process can be perfected or considered for large-scale applications.

There is also an important scientific caveat. Detecting gold, silver or other elements in a sample does not, by itself, mean the technology or process is ready for wider use immediately. The laboratory technique measures what is present, not how it was formed. Independent experiments, including tests of the elementsâ atomic structure, would be needed to understand exactly the science of how such claimed transmutation has occurred.

World.title: Covert Cafe: NCB busts secret basement Meow Meow lab in Ahmedabad
World.content:
NEW DELHI: What at first glance seemed like a popular local cafe in Ahmedabad's Sarkhej area concealed a clandestine "Meow Meow" aka Mephedrone lab tucked away in its basement. Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) has dismantled a clandestine mephedrone manufacturing laboratory whose entrance was cleverly disguised from inside the house behind what appeared to be an almirah and a removable section of tiled flooring.

The NCB arrested the owner, Mudasar Ahmed Khan, and seized crores worth drugs in both liquid and powder form. The joint operation was carried out on Sunday with Gujarat Police. During the raid, officials recovered 25 different chemicals weighing 130 kg including methylamine, bromine, and hydrobromic acid. Complete laboratory apparatus, such as heating mantles, digital magnetic stirrers, round-bottom flasks, and separating funnels, was also confiscated.



The arrested resident, Mudasar Ahmed Khan, lived at the premises with his family and ran the cafe which served as a delivery point for the contraband, the NCB said. During interrogation, Khan admitted to learning the synthesis process using DIY techniques on YouTube and websites.

.

"He procured the raw materials and equipment from suppliers in Mandsaur and Ahmedabad and through online e-commerce platforms. Background checks revealed that Khan has four prior criminal cases registered against him, including charges of attempted murder, rioting, criminal intimidation, and mischief by fire.





The agency noted that this bust reflects a wider trend of synthetic drug laboratories operating out of residential spaces, farms, and industrial units across India, following similar recent seizures in Greater Noida, Jewar, and Prayagraj.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"While the government notified 2-bromo-4-methylpropiophenone as a controlled substance in March 2026 to curb mephedrone production, traffickers are increasingly adopting alternative synthesis methods to bypass regulations," the NCB said.

The threat therefore requires continuous intelligence development, close monitoring of precursor supply chains and rapid sharing of information among enforcement agencies, regulators and industry, officials said. The NCB has urged chemical manufacturers and traders to strictly enforce KYC norms and report suspicious bulk orders. Local police have also been instructed to monitor unusual chemical odours and abnormal power usage, while citizens are encouraged to report suspicious activities confidentially via the toll-free Manas helpline at 1933.

World.title: Census 2027: Self-enumeration begins in four states, house-to-house count from December 1
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Self-enumeration for the population enumeration phase of Census 2027 began on Monday across

, Punjab, Goa and non snow-bound areas of Uttarakhand. It will run till Nov 30, followed immediately by house-to-house enumeration starting Dec 1.

Population enumeration â which follows completion of houselisting operations across all 35 states/UTs, barring Manipur â shall collect household and individual data across 40 fields, including caste of the respondent. The question relating to the caste is open-ended and the reply will be recorded as declared by the respondent. No documentary proof or verification of oneâs caste is required.

A notification issued by the home ministry on Sept 5 had advanced the population enumeration phase of ongoing census in the four states in view of the assembly polls there early next year.



It is scheduled to run from December 1 to January 4, 2027, preceded by a self-enumeration window from November 16 to 30. A revisional round will be undertaken between Jan 5 and 9 next year.

Though Manipur is also due for assembly polls along with the above four states, the census exercise there has been postponed until further notice in view of demands that the national register of citizens (NRC) exercise be undertaken first in the state.





Both phases of Census are already complete in Ladakh and the snow-bound areas of J&K, Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh.

In the remaining states and Union territories, population enumeration will be conducted from Jan 25 to Feb 28, 2027 followed by a revisional round from Mar 1 to 5, 2027. The provision for self-enumeration in these states/UTs will be available from Jan 10 to 24, 2027, prior to the commencement of house-to-house visits by enumerators.

The reference date for Census in these States/UTs will be 00:00 hours of March 1, 2027.

Houselisting operations, which comprise Phase I of Census 2027, have been across all 35 states and Union Territories, except Manipur.

For the first time, Census 2027 is being conducted using digital tools, with self-enumeration introduced as an additional facility. It is a secure, convenient and user-friendly web-based facility available in 16 Indian languages.

All information collected under the Census Act, 1948, shall remain strictly confidential and is used solely for statistical purposes and development planning.

World.title: A decade out of power: Why Congress is struggling to make a comeback in Uttarakhand
World.content:
"If you know the enemy and know yourself, you need not fear the result of a hundred battles. If you know yourself but not the enemy, for every victory gained you will also suffer a defeat.

If you know neither the enemy nor yourself, you will succumb in every battle."

The 'Art of War' by Sun Tzu seems to perfectly encapsulate what

needs to understand for the upcoming Uttarakhand assembly elections.

The

, led in the state by chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami, is seeking a historic third consecutive term. At a recent event in Dehradun, Union home minister Amit Shah set an ambitious target of winning more than 65 of the state's 70 assembly seats.



The Congress, meanwhile, hopes to capitalise on dissatisfaction with the government and return to power after a decade in opposition.

On paper, the Congress has a substantial list of issues to take to voters. The BJP, too, faces the challenge of defending its record in a state where the pendulum of power had previously been in constant swing.

But the electoral arithmetic presents a more complicated picture as we saw in 2022.





BJP can lose ground and still win comfortably; Congress can make gains and still remain distant from power.

So, can Congress turn voter dissatisfaction into a legitimate political direction, or will it simply reiterate its criticisms and fail to make waves?

A state that once voted out its governments

Since the state was formed in 2000, its first four assembly elections produced a change of government every five years. The Congress won 36 seats in 2002, the BJP secured 35 in 2007, the Congress edged ahead with 32 against the BJP's 31 in 2012, and the BJP swept to power with 57 seats in 2017.

And then came 2022, an election that broke the pattern and highlighted BJPâs growing strength in the state. BJP won 47 of the state's 70 seats, becoming the first party to secure consecutive terms since Uttarakhand's formation.

But Congress had also made gains. Compared to 2017, its performance had improved from 11 seats to 19, while its vote share rose from approximately 33.5 per cent to nearly 38 per cent.

The 2024 Lok Sabha election reinforced the challenge, with the BJP winning all five parliamentary constituencies in Uttarakhand.

More significantly, Congress trailed in 63 of the state's 70 assembly segments, including 14 of the 19 constituencies it had won in 2022.

Following the defeat, the Uttarakhand Pradesh Congress Committee tasked former minister Nav Prabhat with assessing the party's performance. The preliminary assessment identified a familiar set of problems: infighting, poor communication and a lack of coordination among party leaders.

Congress had conducted similar reviews after its defeats in the 2014 and 2019 Lok Sabha elections and the 2017 and 2022 assembly elections. Yet the organisational weaknesses identified in those exercises continued to surface.

The Harish Rawat question

Harish Rawat remains one of Congress's most recognisable figures in Uttarakhand, but his prominence has also been tied to the party's internal power struggles.

Rawat was overlooked for the chief minister's post in 2002, despite the party emerging as the largest formation.

After returning to power in 2012, Congress was hit by a major crisis in 2016, when nine MLAs rebelled against his government, triggering President's Rule and a prolonged political and legal battle. Several rebels later joined the BJP.

The mistrust has persisted in the run-up to 2027. The controversy involving Gaurav Kumar, an alleged conman posing as Rahul Gandhi's private secretary, exposed tensions within the state unit.

Bhavna Pandey alleged that Kumar demanded Rs 2â3 crore, claiming the central leadership wanted state president Ganesh Godiyal replaced. Godiyal alleged a conspiracy, while Rawat denied any political plot and called for a police probe.

Personal rivalries, including Rawat's falling-out with former aide Ranjeet Rawat, have added to the uncertainty. The November reshuffle distributed key responsibilities among senior leaders, but whether it can contain competing ambitions remains unclear.

Congress's challenge is to draw on Harish Rawat's experience and support base without allowing the campaign to become another contest over leadership.

Congress has plenty of issues, but no clear message

The Congress has sought to make women's safety and accountability central to its criticism of the government. Garima Mehra Dasauni, the party's chief spokesperson in Uttarakhand, said Congress has compiled a list of alleged crimes against women involving senior BJP leaders in the state.

.

Dasauni also argues that the BJP's electoral success cannot be understood simply through its development claims.

In her assessment, religious and communal mobilisation, alongside welfare measures, has helped the party consolidate support. She also points to the political value of ration distribution and other welfare schemes, particularly among economically vulnerable households.

.

This raises an important question for the Congress: how does it challenge welfare politics without appearing to dismiss the benefits that people receive?

Welfare politics is not new to the Congress either. The National Food Security Act, which made access to subsidised foodgrains a legal entitlement, was enacted in 2013 under the Congress-led United Progressive Alliance government.

However, the BJP has made welfare delivery a key component of its electoral strategy, raising questions about how the Congress can distinguish its own welfare agenda from that of the ruling party.

The challenge for Congress, political observers suggest, is not a shortage of issues to raise but the absence of a common thread that ties them together and presents voters with a clear alternative.

Political scientist Hilal Ahmed explains:

"The Congress is raising all these issues but they lack a narrative between them.

What connects their concerns? BJP can easily answer all these separate claims."

.

For the Congress, this creates a difficult strategic choice. It must distinguish itself from the BJP, but it cannot assume that voters will automatically respond to a campaign built around governance failures and economic grievances.

Ahmed describes the Congress as having âa little bit of a victimhood mentalityâ and calls it âintellectually weakâ.

He also warns that its response to the BJP remains fragmented rather than forming a coherent and constructive critique.

His assessment of the potential electoral consequences is stark: âBJP might not win but neither will Congress.â

The BJP's advantage

The BJP's position in Uttarakhand is stronger than the Congress's current organisational condition. Combining the appeal of PM Modi, CM Dhamiâs work on ground and the promise of continuity through the double-engine government, it seeks to retain its position.

The BJP will also seek to hold together a broad social coalition, while appealing to women, young voters, ex-servicemen and the Sikh community. Its reported plans for younger candidates and greater emphasis on local feedback suggest an effort to refresh its organisation.

At the same time, the party is linking voter-list revision to its rhetoric around identity and belonging. At a Dehradun meeting, BJP leader Bhatt urged workers to remove those described as âinfiltratorsâ, saying: âOnly the original people of Devbhoomi should decide the government.â

The economic question

One of the most important arguments in Ahmed's analysis concerns the state's economic and social structure.

Migration is not simply a consequence of unemployment; it also reflects the concentration of education, healthcare, transport and jobs in towns and the plains.

.

Ahmed argues that Congress has failed to develop a convincing response to the BJP's rhetoric around identity. It could challenge the government's economic priorities and what he describes as a decade of policy paralysis, but must offer more than general claims about unemployment.

The BJP's vulnerabilities, and Congress's opportunity

The Dhami government's record offers Congress several openings: the Ankita Bhandari case and continuing questions over the alleged VIP angle, recruitment paper leaks, unemployment, migration, land rights and allegations of corruption.

But identifying these vulnerabilities is easier than turning them into electoral support. Congress must show how it would address them, particularly concerns over employment, regional inequality and the protection of local land rights.

The Uttarakhand Kranti Dal's attempt to revive the politics of statehood could also put pressure on Congress to articulate a stronger regional agenda.

The party has begun preparing through leadership meetings, multiple Parivartan Yatras, village outreach and a campaign against the government's record.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

As Ahmed argues, Congress also has a lot of âprofessional politiciansâ â leaders who pursue political stature and may abandon Congress in the face of defeat, a scenario reminiscent of 2016.

What will decide 2027?

The BJP is approaching the election with the advantages of incumbency and a well-established organisation, but it is not without vulnerabilities.

The Congress, meanwhile, has a substantial list of issues with which to challenge the government. But none of these issues will automatically produce a victory.

The Congress needs to answer three questions.

Who leads the party in Uttarakhand?

What is its political alternative?

Can it rebuild its organisation?

The art of war is also the art of elections. The Congress is yet to demonstrate that it understands both itself and its electoral 'enemy'.

World.title: Evening news wrap: Terrorist killed in J&K Kulgam encounter; SC grants bail to 2 Bilkis Bano case convicts & more

Security forces killed a Lashkar terrorist in a Kulgam encounter in Jammu and Kashmir.

in Jammu and Kashmir. The Supreme Court granted bail to two convicts in the Bilkis Bano gangrape case.

. Congress moved the Supreme Court seeking permission to pose 48 questions to the Election Commission over alleged 'Vote Chori'.

J&K: Lashkar terrorist killed in Kulgam encounter days after attack on CRPF personnel

A Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) terrorist was killed in an encounter with security forces in Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam district on Monday. The operation was launched following intelligence inputs about the presence of terrorists in the area, days after an attack on CRPF personnel left three security personnel injured.

The Supreme Court has suspended the life sentences of two convicts, Bipinchand Kanaiyalal Joshi and Pradip Ramanlal Modhiya, in the 2002 Bilkis Bano gangrape and murder case and granted them bail. The court noted that the two had spent more than 17 years in prison, while also taking into account the severe disability of one of the convicts.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has expressed hope that the proposed meeting between US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin will advance nuclear disarmament efforts.
