A large-scale march is planned for 28 November. Organisers are urging people across the country to take part and show their support for Georgia’s European integration.

“Mzisa Gabeshia – thank you for your fight,” reads the banner held by a Saturday march participant in the photo below.

On 14 November, 75-year-old Mzisa Gabeshia was buried in the town of Martvili. For months, she had held solo protests in support of Georgia’s European integration and the demonstrations in Tbilisi.

News of her health problems emerged recently. She had been battling a serious illness. Activists from Tbilisi travelled to Martvili to attend her funeral and pay their respects.



“Mzisa Gabeshia – thank you for your fight,” reads a banner held by one of the march participants

The photo below shows Teona Tamazashvili, mother of young programmer Tamar Bachaliashvili, who was found dead in her car in May 2023 under suspicious circumstances. Investigators classified her death as suicide, but her family rejects this conclusion.

Tamazashvili regularly joins the Saturday marches, calling for the investigation to be reopened. She urges fellow citizens to support her weekly protest outside the prosecutor’s office every Monday.

“The mother of a murdered child is calling you,” reads the banner she is holding.



Young singer Sofo Batilashvili, pictured below, is a regular participant in pro-European protests in Tbilisi. Last week, a court fined her 3,000 lari (about $1,150) for posting a video on social media of herself performing “Ole Ola”, a song containing profanities directed at the ruling party.

“Vakho Sanaia, all the way!” reads a banner held by a participant in the Saturday march (pictured below).

In October, prominent TV presenter and Formula journalist Vakho Sanaia was sentenced to 30 days of administrative detention over Facebook posts and videos that a court deemed insulting to parliament speaker Shalva Papuashvili and other members of the ruling party.

Context

The “Saturday marches” are part of an ongoing protest movement that has continued in Georgia for more than two years.

Protesters are demanding that Georgia return to the path of European integration and that all political prisoners be released. They are also calling for the repeal of all anti-democratic laws passed by the ruling Georgian Dream party over the past two years.

Protesters and opposition parties point out that part of Georgian society still does not recognise the results of the parliamentary election held in autumn 2024. They are calling for early parliamentary elections.

Over the course of nearly two years of protests, dozens of people have been arrested. Many have been charged with criminal offences and sentenced to prison.

For the first time in independent Georgia’s history, the country has around 150 prisoners of conscience, including women. Among them is Mzia Amaglobeli, founder of the independent media outlets Batumelebi and Netgazeti. She was sentenced to two years in prison for slapping a police officer.

The protests continue despite an intensifying crackdown on civil society and the media.

News in Georgia

World.title: Georgia’s former prisons chief and ex-prison director accused of helping organise beating of inmate
World.content:
The beating of crime boss Peikrishvili

The Georgian Prosecutor’s Office has charged seven people over the October beating of a crime boss in a prison cell, Davit Peikrishvili. The accused include Giorgi Pataridze, former head of the Special Penitentiary Service, Ramaz Pirtskhalava, former director of Prison No. 8, where the incident took place, and five inmates.

Deputy Prosecutor General Amiran Guluashvili said inmates beat Davit Peikrishvili at Penitentiary Institution No. 8 over four days, from 16 to 20 October.

According to the Prosecutor’s Office, the alleged attackers were inmates Avtandil Bilanishvili, Vato Kipiani, Shota Kipiani, David Kacharava and Pavel Gotsiridze. Prosecutors charged them with intentionally causing less serious bodily harm as part of a group. The offence carries a prison sentence of four to six years.

On 14 November, a court ordered their pre-trial detention as part of the investigation.

The authorities released Giorgi Pataridze, former head of the Special Penitentiary Service, and Ramaz Pirtskhalava, former prison director, on bail of 10,000 lari each (around $3,000). Prosecutors charged Pataridze with exceeding his official powers and Pirtskhalava with abusing his official powers.

Both offences carry prison sentences of up to three years.

The beating forms part of a long-running feud between members of Georgia’s criminal underworld. The dispute began outside prison and continued after some of those involved ended up in the same facility.

Georgian media and social networks have long discussed the alleged links between people involved in the case and the country’s elite circles. Their arrests have therefore attracted considerable attention.

In particular, media outlets often describe crime boss Avtandil Bilanishvili as a friend of Bera Ivanishvili, the son of billionaire Bidzina Ivanishvili. The latter founded the ruling Georgian Dream party and is widely regarded as the country’s de facto ruler.

The prosecution’s version of events

According to investigators, decisions by the prison service leadership made the violence possible.

The Prosecutor’s Office says that on 16 October 2026, four inmates were transferred to Davit Peikrishvili’s cell at the request of Vato Kipiani. The transfer followed instructions from then head of the Penitentiary Service Giorgi Pataridze and a decision by the director of Prison No. 8. The four inmates were Ramaz Pirtskhalava, Vato and Shota Kipiani, and Avtandil Bilanishvili.

David Kacharava and Pavel Gotsiridze were already in the same cell.

The Prosecutor’s Office says this arrangement alone violated the requirements of the Penitentiary Code and the prison’s internal regulations.

According to the prosecution, five inmates began beating Peikrishvili that same day and continued the attacks regularly until 20 October.

He suffered multiple injuries to various parts of his body, including four broken ribs, fractures to the transverse processes of his vertebrae and a concussion.

The Prosecutor’s Office classifies the injuries as less serious bodily harm that caused a prolonged health disorder.

The Prosecutor’s Office said it would submit a motion to the court within the timeframe set by law, seeking pre-trial measures against the accused. The investigation remains ongoing.

Former head of the Special Penitentiary Service Giorgi Pataridze

What Davit Peikrishvili told the court

On 12 November, Davit Peikrishvili addressed a court hearing and said that his attackers beat him because he refused to give them access to his phone. He claimed that prison officials and senior penitentiary service officials were involved.

Peikrishvili also stressed that the prosecutor bore responsibility for failing to keep the location of his phone secret.

“They showed me my phones in the cell. By then, they had already beaten and tortured me. […] The prosecutor’s responsibility is obvious. […] They then took me to Vivamedi clinic and sent me back. Gotsiridze and Shota Kipiani, together with prison staff, watched me to make sure I did not tell anyone what had happened. They kept me in isolation. My only hope was to survive until Monday, when a lawyer could come to see me.

“Before that, I had a lawyer whom I had been friends with for 11 years. I am also the godfather of his son. But he told me he could no longer represent me because he did not trust the prosecutor,” Peikrishvili said.

Background

Paata Gogiashvili, Peikrishvili’s lawyer, first raised concerns about a possible beating on 20 October.

On the same day, Peikrishvili was transferred to Vivamedi clinic. The clinic’s director confirmed to Tabula that medical staff had admitted him with injuries to his hands.

At the time, the Penitentiary Service denied that Peikrishvili’s cellmates had assaulted him. In its initial statement, the agency said that Peikrishvili had unexpectedly left the room during a meeting with his lawyer, smashed a window in the corridor and threatened to hurt himself with a shard of glass.

The statement referred to a threat of self-harm, not an actual injury inflicted by the prisoner.

The Justice Ministry’s General Inspectorate initially investigated the incident. On 25 October, it transferred the case to the Prosecutor General’s Office to ensure an objective investigation.

The following day, the Prosecutor’s Office asked the Justice Ministry to suspend Giorgi Pataridze, head of the Special Penitentiary Service. Pataridze left his post that same day.

Peikrishvili’s family later reported another possible case of violence.

On 25 October, the brothers’ mother said that inmates had also beaten Davit’s brother, Giorgi, in his cell. The Penitentiary Service again denied that any assault had taken place. According to the Public Defender’s Office, Giorgi Peikrishvili had not raised any concerns about his safety at the time.

The Prosecutor’s Office opened criminal proceedings against Davit and Giorgi Peikrishvili on 2 October. It accuses the brothers of laundering money on an especially large scale. The charge carries a prison sentence of up to 12 years.

On 23 September, Tbilisi City Court ordered the pre-trial detention of Davit and Giorgi Peikrishvili and their personal bodyguard, Aleksandre Chapodze.

Who are the Peikrishvili twin brothers?

The Peikrishvili brothers, Davit and Giorgi

The names of brothers Giorgi and Davit Peikrishvili have been linked to Georgia’s criminal underworld in the media for many years.

The brothers became particularly “well known” in 2010 through the so-called illegal bookmakers case, which also involved former footballer Giorgi Demetradze.

Their names later surfaced in a case involving an attack on a cryptocurrency exchange and in a case concerning an alleged plot to assassinate them in Ukraine.

The relationship between the Peikrishvili brothers and crime boss Vato Kipiani dates back at least to 2010.

At the time, Davit Peikrishvili won around $140,000 betting on the FIFA World Cup but could not collect his winnings. According to investigators, Giorgi Demetradze and Vato Kipiani helped him resolve the issue.

In 2011, a court sentenced Giorgi Demetradze to six years in prison. Davit Peikrishvili reached a plea agreement and served a two-year prison sentence.

Vato Kipiani was acquitted in the case.

Peikrishvili’s name also surfaced in a case linked to a high-profile murder in Tbilisi in 2016. Crime boss Soso Jokhadze was shot dead in his own car.

Badri Natobadze, a friend of the Peikrishvili brothers, was convicted of the murder.

In the following years, media outlets reported a theory that Jokhadze’s murder could trigger a new wave of revenge attacks and clashes. In this context, they also mentioned Vato Kipiani, who had links to Jokhadze’s circle.

In January 2020, the security services of Georgia and Ukraine carried out a joint operation and foiled an alleged plot to kill the Peikrishvili brothers. Authorities arrested six people in Georgia and one in Ukraine.

According to a statement by the Prosecutor’s Office at the time, Vato Kipiani had commissioned the explosive device intended to kill Peikrishvili. Ukrainian authorities later deported Kipiani to Georgia, where police arrested him in 2021.

Local media cited the feud that followed Soso Jokhadze’s murder as one possible motive for the alleged plot. However, investigators never established the exact motive.

Vato Kipiani

In October 2023, an attack took place at a cryptocurrency exchange in Tbilisi. The attackers stole around $740,000.

Media reports identified Davit Peikrishvili as the alleged organiser of the attack. Prosecutors charged the brothers in connection with the case. A court of first instance sentenced them to 11 years in prison, but an appeals court later acquitted them.

On 22 September 2026, law enforcement officers arrested Davit and Giorgi Peikrishvili during a special operation in Tbilisi. They also arrested Davit Peikrishvili’s personal bodyguard.

Initially, the Interior Ministry charged the brothers with group violence and extortion. Their lawyer said they denied the charges.

On 2 October, the Prosecutor’s Office brought an additional charge against the brothers: laundering money on an especially large scale.

According to the Prosecutor’s Office, between 2020 and 2026, the brothers split up funds of illegal origin and used other people’s bank accounts to move the money. They then consolidated the funds in their own accounts through multiple bank transfers.

The agency said the brothers accumulated the equivalent of around 10 million lari (approximately $3.7 million) in various currencies in their accounts. Investigators allege that they used the money to repay bank loans and purchase movable and immovable property.

The charge carries a prison sentence of up to 12 years.

World.title: ‘Armenia is replacing one dependency with another’: Former Security Council Secretary Armen Grigoryan’s assessment
World.content:
Article by Armenia’s former Security Council secretary

“Armenia is replacing one dependency with another”: Former Security Council Secretary Armen Grigoryan’s view

“The idea of Armenia joining the European Union seems attractive at first glance. But we often confuse what we want with what is possible,” says Armen Grigoryan, a former secretary of Armenia’s Security Council.

He published an article arguing that EU membership is an unrealistic prospect and contradicts the formula Armenia’s authorities have declared. That formula calls for “replacing dependence on a few with dependence on many”.

“This is not a genuine alternative or a diversification of foreign policy. It is simply a way to replace one dependency with another, one that offers fewer prospects and ignores regional realities,” he writes about Armenia’s prospects for European integration.

In Grigoryan’s view, the EU membership agenda once again leads Armenia into a dead end. It forces the country back towards forms of dependence that “have proved unsustainable”.

“Just as we once believed that Russia would solve our security problems, we now mistakenly expect the EU to solve the economic problems that will arise on the path to EU membership,” he argues.

Discussing potential risks, the former official said Armenia could once again face the harsh reality it has experienced since 2020. That was when the 44-day war in Nagorno-Karabakh began. He argues that “an external partner may not take responsibility for solving the problems we expect it to address”.

Grigoryan also raises the question of “how to reduce dependence on Russia without deepening that very dependence even further”. However, he does not offer a direct answer under this subheading. Instead, he speaks of the need for independent decision-making and closer cooperation with the EU, the US and other countries.

Below, we publish an abridged version of the article by the former Security Council secretary, which has sparked considerable debate in Armenia’s political circles.

Historical overview

“If we look at Armenia’s recent history, a very clear and harsh pattern emerges. Every time Yerevan has tried to move closer to the West, it has faced mounting pressure from Russia and ultimately ended up even more firmly in Moscow’s ‘embrace’.

In the 1990s, under Levon Ter-Petrosyan, attempts to build closer ties with European and Euro-Atlantic institutions ended with Armenia joining the Collective Security Treaty Organisation (CSTO) and signing a Treaty of Friendship, Cooperation and Mutual Assistance with Russia in 1997. This strengthened Armenia’s military and political ties with Moscow.

In the 2010s, under Serzh Sargsyan, an attempt to sign an Association Agreement with the EU ended with the decision on 3 September 2013 to join the Customs Union. Armenia subsequently joined the Eurasian Economic Union.

Today, this history appears to be repeating itself, but under a much more dangerous scenario.

“While Armenia continues negotiations and takes steps towards EU membership, I see a growing risk that the country could become involved in the Russia-Belarus Union State.”

Armenia has no immunity against pressure from Moscow

“Statements and steps towards EU membership are sharply worsening relations between Armenia and Russia.

Faced with Russia’s harsh and aggressive countermeasures, Armenia’s state immune system simply cannot withstand Moscow’s economic, political and hybrid pressure.

As a result, without real security guarantees from the West, Armenia cannot reduce its dependence on Russia. Instead, it becomes even more vulnerable to Russian pressure.”

The European integration agenda contradicts regionalisation

“An unrealistic EU membership agenda runs counter to the natural process of regionalisation. Armenia lies at the crossroads of three major regional powers: Russia, Iran and Turkey. Yerevan’s relations with each of them are closely interconnected and require a delicate balance.

Iran has repeatedly outlined its ‘red lines’, opposing any expansion of Western military and political presence in the region. Given its strained relations with the West, Tehran views the EU as part of the collective West.

Armenia’s attempts to join the EU could jeopardise its friendly relations with Iran. And Iran is not just a neighbour for Armenia, but a vital ‘lifeline’.

Although Turkey is a NATO member, it pursues an independent regional policy. Together with Azerbaijan, Ankara seeks to resolve regional issues with the participation of countries in the region. The ‘3+3’ format is one example of this approach.

Yerevan’s attempts to expand the West’s presence in the region could create further tensions in its relations with Turkey and Azerbaijan.

Russia views Armenia’s EU membership agenda as a threat to its interests in the region and responds with strong opposition.”

Armenia risks losing the foundations of its economic stability

“In spaceflight, a rocket must reach the second cosmic velocity of 11.2 km per second to escape Earth’s gravitational field. If it fails to reach the required speed, it cannot remain in orbit and falls back under the force of gravity.

Armenia lacks the ‘speed’ it needs to escape the economic gravitational pull of the Russia-led Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) and Russia itself.

If Armenia finds itself in an ‘intermediate’ position during a prolonged and drawn-out EU accession process, it risks losing the foundations of its current economic stability: cheap energy supplies and access to the Russian market. It could then fall back even more painfully into complete dependence on Russia.”

Will Yerevan consider imposing sanctions on Russia and Iran?

“On its path towards EU membership, Armenia will also face the question of whether to join sanctions against Russia and Iran. This could seriously damage relations with these two countries, which are vital to Armenia’s security and economy.

Amid discussions about possible increases in the price of Russian gas, and even supply cuts in some cases, Armenia is increasingly exploring ways to import more gas from Iran. However, this raises an important contradiction.

Under the sanctions imposed on Iran, the European Union prohibits the purchase, import and exchange of Iranian natural gas. At some point on its path towards EU membership, Armenia will have to align its legislation and foreign policy with EU requirements.

This means Armenia will have to stop importing gas from Iran. The future of the Armenian-Iranian ‘gas-for-electricity’ programme will also come into question.

This creates a contradiction. Armenia needs alternative suppliers to reduce its dependence on Russian gas. Yet, on its path towards EU membership, it may have to limit its access to Iranian gas as well.”

Cooperation should extend beyond the EU and US

“Armenia can develop political, economic and security cooperation with European partners without making EU membership a foreign policy goal.

Our task is not to replace dependence on Russia with dependence on another power centre, but to strengthen Armenia’s independence.

We can deepen cooperation not only with the EU and the US, but also with India, China, Central Asian states, the Gulf countries, Japan, South Korea and other partners, each through its own agenda.

Armenia’s foreign policy options are not limited to choosing between two geopolitical centres.

The more diverse our economic, political and security ties become, the more opportunities we will have to balance external dependencies.”

Article by Armenia’s former Security Council secretary

World.title: Abkhazia’s capital temporarily bans high-rise construction in city centre. What happens next?
World.content:
Authorities have temporarily banned buildings taller than 18 metres, or roughly six storeys, in the historic centre of Sukhum.

The decision, proposed by Mayor Timur Agrba and approved by the city council, will remain in force until the city adopts a new master plan.

Abkhazia’s capital last approved a master plan during the Soviet era, in 1987. Since then, the authorities have not adopted a comprehensive new urban development plan, although both officials and the public have periodically called for one.

Whenever another high-rise appears near the waterfront, Sukhum residents grow increasingly vocal in demanding tighter controls on construction. They believe these buildings are damaging the city’s historic character.

According to Timur Agrba, the city administration receives proposals for buildings of various heights. Officials reject some of them, but without a proper master plan, the city authorities have virtually no regulatory grounds for refusing projects, apart from the need to preserve the city’s historic character.

The authorities plan to start drawing up a new master plan in 2027, a process that could take several years. That is why Agrba proposed temporarily restricting the height of new buildings. However, the measure effectively contradicts existing legislation: the coefficient set out in the current Urban Planning Code allows buildings taller than 18 metres.

The restriction may therefore prove to be purely temporary and, possibly, not particularly effective.

Authorities cannot revoke construction permits they have already issued, so the new restriction will apply only to future projects.

They may also grant exceptions for certain buildings that serve an important social purpose or are significant for the republic or the city.

Sukhum’s chief architect, Bislan Bagateliya, confirms that the city centre’s architectural character calls for low-rise development. He supports restricting high-rise construction until the authorities have a clear understanding of how the city should develop.

The terminology, place names and views expressed in this article are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the editorial position of this website.

World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 16. To boost payment security and meet new legal standards, customers making cash payments or transfers over 500 AZN at Milliön terminals must now verify their identity digitally.

Identity verification can be completed quickly using the Bir ID (via the Birbank app), SİMA, or MyGov mobile applications.

Select your desired service and enter the payment amount at the terminal.

If the amount exceeds 500 AZN, the screen will prompt you to choose a verification method (Bir ID, SİMA, or MyGov).

Select your preferred app to generate a QR code on the terminal screen.

Open the corresponding app on your smartphone and scan the QR code to confirm your identity.

Once successfully verified, proceed to complete your payment.

Important Reminder: To ensure a smooth transaction, please verify that you have at least one of these digital ID apps active on your phone before making large payments.

World.title: Azerbaijan joins ECO talks on regional cooperation in Islamabad (PHOTO)
World.content:
Photo: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan

BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 16. A delegation led by Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs of Azerbaijan Elnur Mammadov participated in the 30th meeting of the Council of Ministers of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO), held in Islamabad, the capital of Pakistan, on November 16, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs said.

During the meeting, the deputy minister outlined Azerbaijan’s position on strengthening cooperation within the ECO framework, the institutional development of the organization, and potential collaboration in the spheres of trade, economy, transport, energy, and digitalization.

The contribution of the 17th ECO Summit, held last year in Khankendi, and the inaugural "ECO Week" to the advancement of regional cooperation was highlighted, as was the importance of implementing the agreements reached.

The role of transport, energy, and digital infrastructure projects, initiated and supported by Azerbaijan, in enhancing regional connectivity was noted. Furthermore, the importance of supporting the activities of ECO institutions based in Azerbaijan was emphasized.

The deputy minister also briefed on Azerbaijan’s efforts to ensure sustainable peace and stability in the region, the reconstruction and construction work underway in the territories liberated from occupation, and the return of former internally displaced persons.

At the conclusion of the meeting, a final document titled the "Islamabad Communiqué" was adopted.

During the visit, the Prime Minister of Pakistan, Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif, received the heads of delegations from the ECO member states, including Deputy Minister Elnur Mammadov.

World.title: Tajikistan cuts power losses to 12.5% in first nine months of 2026
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 16. Electricity losses in Tajikistan's power system fell by 2.7 percentage points year-on-year to 12.5% in the first nine months of 2026.

According to the Ministry of Energy and Water Resources, Minister Daler Juma presented the figures on November 12 during an address to the Majlisi Namoyandagon, the lower chamber of the Majlisi Oli (Supreme Assembly).

To further reduce losses, Tajikistan is implementing projects to install smart meters, upgrade metering systems and rehabilitate power grids.

The country is also working to expand regional energy cooperation and integrate its power grid into the Central Asian Unified Power System. In this regard, Juma highlighted the importance of implementing the regional CASA-1000 project, constructing the South–North power transmission line and connecting the northern part of Tajikistan's power system to the regional grid.

Juma also reported on efforts to improve the regulatory framework for the energy sector. A draft Energy Code of the Republic of Tajikistan is being developed to establish a unified legal framework. Its adoption is expected to help attract private investment, develop a competitive electricity market, promote digitalization and improve the efficiency of energy sector management.

The minister also emphasized the importance of meeting the petroleum product needs of the national economy and the population. He noted that building up the necessary reserves and ensuring an uninterrupted and stable supply to the domestic market remain among the government's energy policy priorities.

The Ministry of Energy and Water Resources will next focus on continuing construction of the Rogun Hydropower Plant, rehabilitating existing power plants, developing renewable energy sources, modernizing electricity networks, ensuring petroleum supplies to the domestic market, and improving water resource management.

World.title: Azerbaijan, UK discuss strengthening strategic partnership prospects
World.content:
Photo: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan

BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 16. Azerbaijan and the United Kingdom have discussed prospects for strengthening the strategic partnership and achieving practical results in areas covered by the Joint Declaration on Strategic Partnership, the Azerbaijani Ministry of Foreign Affairs reported.

The issue was discussed during a phone conversation between Azerbaijani Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov and UK Secretary of State for Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Affairs Ed Miliband on November 16.

Bayramov once again congratulated Miliband on his appointment as Secretary of State and wished him success in his endeavors.

During the conversation, the sides discussed the current state and future prospects of bilateral relations, as well as the importance of continuing high-level political dialogue.

In this context, they highlighted the significance of the meeting between the two countries' leaders during the recent European Political Community (EPC) Summit and the adoption of the Joint Declaration on Strategic Partnership between the Republic of Azerbaijan and the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland for the development of bilateral relations.

The parties also discussed regional security issues and exchanged views on the current situation in the South Caucasus.

Bayramov informed his counterpart about Azerbaijan's efforts to ensure lasting peace and stability in the region, open communications, and expand economic cooperation.

The conversation also covered other regional and international issues of mutual interest.

World.title: British actor Robert Pattinson named as the new James Bond
World.content:
British actor Robert Pattinson will be the next James Bond, Amazon MGM Studios announced on Monday, taking on the role after Daniel Craig's departure from the long-running spy series.

The Bond franchise — about a British secret agent known for his charm, his tailored tuxedos and a fondness for martinis "shaken, not stirred" — is among the longest-running and highest-grossing in Hollywood history.

The franchise made its debut in 1962 and the movies have brought in more than $7 billion in global ticket sales since Sean Connery brought Agent 007 to the big screen in Dr. No.

More than two dozen Bond films have been released. The upcoming movie will be the first Bond adventure under Amazon MGM Studios, which took creative control of the film franchise under a new joint venture with longtime rights holders Michael Wilson and Barbara Broccoli in 2025.

Denis Villeneuve, an Oscar nominee known for movies such as the Dune trilogy and Arrival, is set to direct the new film, with a script written by Briton Steven Knight.

Pattinson, whose film credits this year include The Odyssey, The Drama and Primetime and who will also feature in Villeneuve's "Dune: Part Three" to be released next month, succeeds Craig, who bowed out of the role after 2021 movie "No Time to Die."

"James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime," Pattinson said in a statement.

"I'm deeply grateful to Denis, Amy, David, Tanya, and everyone at Amazon MGM Studios for their belief in me.

"To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team," Pattinson said, referring to producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman and executive producer Tanya Lapointe.

World.title: Netanyahu rival demands probe into PM's office over election fraud claims
World.content:
Benjamin Netanyahu's main rival is demanding an investigation into the Israeli Prime Minister's Office, following explosive allegations it may have fabricated claims of electoral fraud.

Gadi Eisenkot, who is currently steering negotiations to form a new coalition government, said Mr Netanyahu posed "a tangible, direct and immediate threat to Israeli democracy".

For weeks since Israel's inconclusive election on October 27, Mr Netanyahu and his Likud party have been claiming the election was "stolen", describing the surge in support for Arab-Israeli parties at the ballot box as illegitimate and the result of voters being paid off.

On Sunday night, Israel's Channel 12 reported that the prime minister's chief of staff, Ido Norden had contacted the Israeli police commissioner's office with a complaint about members of the United Arab List (UAL), the party often referred to as Ra'am in Hebrew.

The network said Mr Norden's source was actually a former employee of the Prime Minister's Office.

The intervention led to the homes of three UAL members being raided on the morning of the election without search warrants and the men arrested on allegations of electoral fraud, after envelopes of cash were discovered.

Mr Netanyahu used the arrests to ramp up his rhetoric on election day, accusing Arab-Israeli or Palestinian-Israelis of trying to steal the election.

Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, gives a thumbs up following the exit polls at his party headquarters, on the evening of Israel's national election. (Reuters: Shir Torem)

But the men were released days later.

It has also been reported that the head of Israeli intelligence agency Shin Bet, David Zini, tried to wire-tap three members of the other Arab-Israeli party, the Joint List ahead of the election amid suspicion of foreign interference in the poll.

His request was denied by Israel's Attorney-General, a public servant and the country's legal advisor, and his agency failed to provide more evidence to back up the demand.

Reports have also suggested Mr Zini, who was hand-picked to be Shin Bet chief by Mr Netanyahu, wanted some Arab-Israeli politicians arrested on election day.

Eisenkot calls for Netanyahu to stand down as PM

The Netanyahu government has been highly critical of the Attorney-General, Gali Baharav-Miara, relentless accusing her of blocking its agenda.

Gadi Eisenkot said the affair was further reason why Mr Netanyahu should not "remain at the helm of government for even one more minute".

"Under no circumstances must Israel be dragged into another election with him as prime minister.

"It is clear that as long as he remains in office, Israel can no longer expect elections that are fair and lawful."

Another member of Mr Eisenkot's Yashar party, former Shin Bet director Yoram Cohen, wrote to the Attorney-General on Monday, local time, demanding a criminal investigation into whether the police and intelligence agencies were being used by Mr Netanyahu to undermine the election.

Taunts, heckling mar swearing in of new Israeli parliament Benjamin Netanyahu uses a speech traditionally used as a toast to rail against Arab Israeli members of the Knesset, two weeks after a deadlocked election result.

"The fear that the state's enforcement powers were used to advance political interests in the midst of election day requires a thorough, independent and impartial investigation," Mr Cohen wrote.

Former prime minister Yair Lapid described the situation as an "orchestrated" attempt by Mr Netanyahu's office and his Likud party to steal the election.

"As more and more details come to light, it becomes clear," he posted on X.

"This wasn't an attempt to disrupt the elections. It was an attempted coup."

Likud described Mr Eisenkot's comments as "outrageous incitement" and "appalling".

"While the prime minister extends a hand for unity, Eisenkot and his colleagues issue inflammatory, incendiary statements every day in venomous language," it said.

"Eisenkot is inciting against the chief of staff, a law-abiding citizen who passed information to the police about suspicions of a serious criminal offence, as he was obligated to do."

The United Arab List and the Joint List secured 19 out of the 120 seats in the Israeli parliament, the Knesset.

Israel Police launches internal probe

Israel Police has confirmed an internal investigation is underway, with the force's deputy commissioner looking at "all systemic, organisational and command-related aspects concerning the allegations made against Israel Police".

"It should be emphasised that all police actions, including the activity carried out on the morning of election day, were conducted with a commitment to transparency and accountability to the public, and with the aim of safeguarding the integrity of the elections," a spokesperson said in a statement.

Ido Norden, Mr Netanyahu's chief of staff, has threatened Channel 12 with a defamation suit worth 2.5 million shekels (1.14 million AUD).

Mr Norden's lawyers claimed threats had been made against his life since the report went to air.

"[The report] constitutes an act of fraud on a national scale, masquerading as "journalistic work," and represents a new and dangerous low in the contamination of public democratic discourse in Israel.

"Your decision to disseminate these baseless, false claims—along with malicious lies—in the midst of an investigation into the conduct of the elections, is intended solely to exert an improper and unlawful influence on the outcome of the elections in Israel."

World.title: Robert Irwin named Queenslander of the year
World.content:
Wildlife conservationist Robert Irwin has been declared the Queenslander of the year at tonight's awards.

The 22-year-old was named the 2027 Australian of the Year for Queensland for his environmental advocacy and work at Australia Zoo.

Robert Irwin is the son of Australian conservationists Steve and Terri Irwin, and the grandson of Australia Zoo founders Bob and Lyn Irwin.

Gout Gout was born in Ipswich after his parents migrated from South Sudan. (AP: Heiko Junge)

The young Queenslander of the year was Ipswich sprinting champion, Gout Gout.

Gout Gout broke the world under-20 record for the 200 metre dash in April, with a time of 19.67 seconds.

He ran the 200m in 20.04 seconds at the 2024 Australian All School Athletics Championship, becoming the fastest 16-year-old in history.

The now 18-year-old plans to compete in the 2028 Olympics, followed by the 2032 Brisbane Olympic Games.

Carmel Crouch has helped others into employment for more than four decades. (Supplied: STEPS Group Australia)

The senior Queenslander of the year award was taken out by disability advocate Carmel Crouch.

The 80-year-old was a founding board member of STEPS Group Australia, which helps people with disabilities gain skills and land jobs.

Under her leadership, the group pioneered STEPS Pathways College, which teaches students with disability and autism.

Ms Crouch has since broadened her reach to migrants, refugees and First Nations communities through a series of social enterprises.

Noel Brown is a soothing presence at Cairns Hospital. (Supplied: Australian of the Year Awards)

The Local Hero for Queensland award was taken out by Noel Brown, who is the specialist First Nations greeter at Cairns Hospital.

The 65-year-old provides warm smiles, conversation and cultural connection to Aboriginal patients going through the Cairns medical system.

Inspiring stories

National Australia Day Council CEO Carrie Leeson congratulated the Queensland award recipients.

"The achievements of our Queensland award recipients are nothing short of inspirational," Ms Leeson said.

"Robert is continuing his family's legacy and sharing their passion for conservation with a new generation, while Gout is a teenage sprint sensation breaking world records.

"Carmel is helping people gain independence and dignity, while Noel provides understanding and support when it's needed most."

World.title: Inquest examines what led to deaths of four babies born at home
World.content:
The mother of a baby who died in northern New South Wales four years ago was afraid she would be forced to have a caesarean if she went to hospital, an inquest has heard.

What drove her decision to continue with plans for a freebirth, despite medical advice that her baby was in distress, will be examined by the New South Wales Coroners Court in Lismore.

The inquest will investigate the neonatal deaths of two other babies born by freebirth in northern New South Wales, and a fourth born by homebirth in the Hunter Valley, between 2022 and 2024.

A freebirth means a baby was born without medical assistance, often supported by family, friends, a doula or "birth keeper".

Homebirths were deliveries supported by a registered midwife outside a clinical setting.

During the two-week inquest, Deputy State Coroner Joan Baptie will hear evidence about the advice and treatment given to the babies' mothers, before, during, and after the births, and how it influenced their birthing decisions.

The counsel assisting the coroner said the inquiry did not seek to place blame on the parents for their decisions, but rather sought to understand the barriers preventing parents engaging with health services.

On the first day of the inquest, the court heard the mother of Baby R, who cannot be named for legal reasons, was about three weeks past her due date when she had an ultrasound that revealed the baby was in distress.

Despite advice from the sonographer to go to Tweed Valley Hospital immediately, the court heard the woman still wanted a homebirth.

Counsel Assisting the Coroner, Tracey Stevens, said she consulted her birth keeper, Sita Kali, for advice, despite knowing she had no medical training.

Ms Stevens said the birth keeper noted the woman's anxiety, and advised her to go home, rest and calm down before making a decision.

Within hours, the woman went into labour. The baby was born with the cord around its neck, was pale, had faeces on its face, and had breathing difficulties.

Twelve hours later, emergency services were called, but the baby died.

In a statement after the baby died, the mother said: "I was afraid to go to hospital and be forced into a caesarean. I still thought the baby was ok."

Expert midwives giving evidence at the inquest said this mistrust of clinicians was driving some women to choose freebirths outside the medical system.

Professor Hannah Dahlen and Dr Alison Teate said while doulas and birth keepers did not have the same clinical expertise as midwives, they played an important role in supporting childbirth.

Professor Dahlen supported women being able to make an informed choice about how their babies were born.

She said that included letting doulas and birth keepers be involved in the birth process.

"I'd like to see us work together rather than this great divide," Professor Dahlen said.

She said trust was key to the safe delivery of babies.

World.title: Conjoined twin girls born in remote Papua New Guinea
World.content:
Medical staff are rushing to help a rare set of conjoined twins born in remote Papua New Guinea, with hopes of bringing the girls to Australia for treatment.

It is the country's second case of conjoined twins in just over a year after the birth of twin boys Tom and Sawong in October 2025 captured global attention.

Doctors reveal mission to help conjoined twins A team of doctors involved in the separation of conjoined Papua New Guinean twins Sawong and Tom have spoken for the first time about the rare and complex case.

Conjoined twins are very rare, estimated to occur only once in every 50,000 births and once in every 200,000 live births.

Many are stillborn or die soon after they are born.

The girls, who have not yet been named, were delivered two weeks ago at Nonga Base Hospital on the island of East New Britain, about 800 kilometres from the capital, Port Moresby.

It is unclear at this stage whether they share any major organs.

Conjoined twins born in remote Papua New Guinea will be flown to Port Moresby. (Supplied: Manolos Aviation)

Enquiries are being made about transferring the sisters to Australia because Papua New Guinea's heath system does not have the resources to treat conjoined twins.

Jurgen Ruh, a pilot who founded an NGO that provides emergency care to women in PNG, said he was reaching out to contacts in four different countries asking for help.

"Our favourite is Australia. It's closest," he told the ABC.

"But I'm going to put four hands in the fire and whichever comes first, we will action."

He said the hospital had very limited facilities but medical reports he had seen indicated the girls were doing OK.

"They're breathing a bit faster than normal, but apart from the vital signs we have seen, they look pretty normal," he said.

" We are hopeful that we've got all organs separate and they're just joined basically at the chest. "

Surgery separates Fijian conjoined twins In what was described as an "exceptionally rare" case, doctors in Saudi Arabia say a complex operation to separate 13-month-old Fijian conjoined twins has been successful.

Mr Ruh helped seek overseas care for twins Tom and Sawong.

He said he could not believe there was another case of conjoined twins born in Papua New Guinea so soon after.

"I thought I wasn't going to see it in my lifetime again," Mr Ruh said.

His NGO, Mountain Area Medical Airlift (MAMA) Foundation, has sent staff to Nonga to help fly the twins to Port Moresby this week.

A local private hospital and commercial airline have also agreed to assist.

The CEO of East New Britain's health service, Ako Yap, said he was grateful for the support.

"I give my full authority for partners to escalate further treatment for the twins and we hope and pray for a better outcome all around," Dr Yap said.

World.title: 104 flights cancelled due to weather conditions at Sydney Airport
World.content:
Airline travellers have experienced major delays at Sydney Airport due to severe weather conditions, with 104 flight cancellations recorded so far.

Wind and cloud activity had impacted flights to and from Sydney Airport, with the bulk of cancellations affecting domestic routes.

In a statement, an Airservices Australia spokesperson confirmed the delays, recommending passengers check with their airline for flight updates.

"Aircraft delays are being experienced in Sydney today with factors including cloud and wind affecting air traffic operations," they said.

"Airservices is working with industry to safely manage air traffic demand throughout the day."

Wind and cloud activity had impacted flights to and from Sydney Airport. (ABC News: Billy Cooper)

There was also Virgin Australia ground crew industrial action related to pay and working conditions that took place on Monday.

A Virgin Australia spokesperson said there were a number of "contingencies in place" to ensure the industrial action did not impact operations or passengers' travel.

The airline was working to minimise the weather-related disruption to guests.

Qantas has also experienced disruptions and cancellations across their network. (ABC News: John Gunn)

A Qantas spokesperson said the adverse weather had resulted in a ground delay program being put in place by Airservices Australia, affecting all airlines.

"[This] has caused disruptions and cancellations across our network. A small number of services were cancelled overnight in preparation for the ground delay program," the spokesperson said.

"Customers were contacted directly and re-accommodated on alternate flights within 24 hours of their original booking."

The airline was working to up-gauge some aircraft to increase capacity and recover cancelled flights.

Hours of waiting and frustration

Toula Vorinos's Virgin flight to Melbourne was due to depart Sydney at 10am this morning before it was cancelled.

At 8pm she was still waiting at the airport, and had managed to secure a seat on a Jetstar flight leaving at 9:15pm.

"We got a notification when we got off the boat on the way to the airport ... and we've been waiting since literally 7:20 this morning," she said.

" We were told about the weather conditions … I feel frustrated and tired. "

Toula Vorinos's flight was due to leave Sydney at 10am but was cancelled. (ABC News: Nabil Al-Nashar)

Brownwyn Jackson from the Sunshine Coast was struggling to get accommodation near the airport after the cancellation of her connecting flight to Hobart.

"So, have been trying for the past two hours to get another flight that didn't happen, so now trying to get accommodation and an alternative flight tomorrow [Tuesday] hopefully," she said.

"I've got accommodation in Hobart booked for a week, so it's quite a waste of money as well, plus the extra night tonight, so very frustrating."

Ms Jackson said she received no notice about the disruption, and found out from another passenger when she went to check-in.

Barbara Evans is staying in Sydney until she gets a flight home to Launceston. (ABC News: Nabil Al-Nashar)

Barbara Evans got notified that her evening flight to Launceston was not going ahead while at the airport.

She had arrived three hours prior to departure, and has since been trying to work on alternatives to get home.

"I can't get down there even via Melbourne tonight. I can't do it on Jetstar tomorrow, I can't do it direct on Virgin tomorrow," she said.

"I could do it by going to the Gold Coast and then the Gold Coast to Adelaide … it's totally crazy.

" And that ticket is $1,400 one way, so I decided to stay two nights, and find a hotel and kill a day in Sydney. It's better. "

Aidan Osmani told the ABC it was "frustrating" after his flight to Brisbane for a work trip was cancelled, and his rescheduled flight was going to the Gold Coast.

He had been waiting at the airport for more than an hour-and-a-half.

"It is what it is, and just have to be patient and wait," he said.

World.title: Test cricket hopefuls let last chance slip to bang the door down
World.content:
Australia's Test aspirants have missed their last chance to impress before the squad is named for next month's series opener against New Zealand.

With selectors set to name a squad later this week for the first Test in Perth, both Sam Konstas and Jack Clayton failed to make significant scores in one-day matches today.

Konstas was caught for six as New South Wales chased quick runs against South Australia in a rain-affected contest in Sydney, while Clayton made 24 for Queensland against Tasmania.

It is unlikely either score will count against the pair given the matches were white-ball fixtures, but high scores would not have hurt their chances regardless of the format.

Australian selectors have decisions to consider about the makeup of their team for the first Test against the Black Caps at Perth Stadium on December 9.

Selectors have already confirmed Marnus Labuschagne will be dropped, while Steve Smith is on track to return from a neck injury.

That could theoretically be the only change to the Australian side that lost in Cape Town last month, but questions remain around Cooper Connolly's selection.

If Australia was to go in another direction, there are any number of options, with a batter able to come in at number three or in the middle order at number six or seven.

Konstas has been the leading run-scorer in the Sheffield Shield this year with 426 runs at an average of 85.2, including two centuries.

Selectors believe the 21-year-old has benefited from his time in the Test side two years ago.

Clayton sits third on the charts with 355 at 71, with Greg Chappell saying last week there was no reason why the 27-year-old could not play Tests this summer.

Jack Clayton made 24 off 29 for Queensland against Tasmania but missed out on a big white-ball score to push his case for Test selection. (Getty Images: Bradley Kanaris)

Jake Weatherald hit his first century of the season last week for South Australia in his push for a recall, but has not reached 50 in six other Shield innings.

Connolly meanwhile has not played a Shield game this summer while on Australian duties, with scores of 27 and 0 in the two ODIs against England.

Asked last week whether Shield runs or the future would be the most important aspect this summer, chief selector George Bailey suggested both were key factors.

"We're asking all those questions all the time, and I think we'll land with how we think this squad will structure up," Bailey said.

"It has been really pleasing to see the start of the Shield year, and it's provided us plenty of options to ticking some or all of the boxes you've mentioned there."

Bailey has indicated Australia will likely name a 14-man squad for the first Test, with the ability to change it between matches.

This week's squad announcement will come almost three weeks before the first Test, with another Sheffield Shield round to start on Sunday.

Several Test players will feature in that round, but Bailey said there were stakeholder requirements to name the squad earlier.

"We've got some thoughts around what that squad is starting to look like as it is," Bailey said last week.

"I don't like the idea of a bat-off or a bowl-off in a one-off game."

World.title: Australia and UK close on deal to send record wave of British backpackers out bush
World.content:
PoliticsFederalImmigration Australia and UK close on deal to send record wave of British backpackers out bush Paul Sakkal and Natassia Chrysanthos November 17, 2026 — 3:56am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Regional employers crying out for backpackers to fill pubs and cafes are set to win a reprieve on Tuesday, when Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke is expected to wind back a proposed crackdown on working holidaymakers. The number of backpackers, notably young Brits, has soared in recent years. They were the main target of Burke’s migration overhaul announced in September, which followed policy releases from the Coalition and One Nation aimed at tapping into public anxiety about migration. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese with his British counterpart, Andy Burnham, in September. The pair have discussed changes to working holiday visas. Dominic Lorrimer The government has been examining delaying until next year the rollout of a ballot system for backpackers seeking to extend their stay, lifting the 5000-person cap on third-year working holiday visas and imposing longer regional work requirements on visa holders. Two sources familiar with Burke’s announcement said Labor was close to an agreement with the UK to ensure the British backpackers arriving in Australia in record numbers helped fill skills shortages in the regions rather than spending all their time in the cities.



Related Article Exclusive

Immigration Labor quietly pauses working holidaymaker visas as stoush over backpackers brews Pubs, clubs and agriculture groups have campaigned against Labor’s backpacker proposals. The backlash highlights the tough trade-offs in the migration debate, where cutting historically high arrivals risks harming key sectors such as universities, health and construction depending on the visa class. Conservatives argue that Labor’s plan focuses too heavily on backpackers, urging a tougher crackdown instead on international students – a sector Labor is already squeezing. Last week, Burke said Australia must find a way to reduce the number of UK backpackers arriving and staying in the country under a free-trade deal signed by the governments of Scott Morrison and Boris Johnson in 2021. It allows British citizens to live in Australia for up to three years without specific work requirements. “We can find a way to bring that back to something more sensible and in the national interest, without jeopardising the other parts of the free-trade agreement,” Burke said.



Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has had two meetings with UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham in as many weeks. Last Thursday, the pair discussed changes to working holidaymaker visas on the sidelines of the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey. This followed a discussion with Burnham at the Commonwealth summit in the Caribbean earlier this month, which Albanese described as “very constructive”. Under the free-trade deal, Australian and British backpackers gained rights to live in each other’s countries for three years, and the visa age limit was lifted from 30 to 35. For British backpackers, there was an extra sweetener: from 2024, they no longer needed to work 88 days in Australia’s regions to stay on, a condition for all other nationalities. The move was criticised by the Nationals at the time, who warned that farmers would lose up to 10,000 workers a year.



Numbers have since surged. There were 217,827 working holidaymakers in Australia at the end of September this year, according to the latest data, which represents a record for that quarter. Of them, 51,248 were British – a figure that has doubled since two years ago, shortly after the regional work requirement was scrapped. The visa stream for British backpackers is also uncapped, meaning there is no upward limit to how many young UK nationals can come to Australia when their job market is weaker at home. Changes to the UK scheme will seek to offset some of the worker losses that regional employers face under the government’s overall plans to drive down backpacker numbers, by making more British backpackers fill those jobs.

World.title: Robert Pattinson cast as next James Bond
World.content:
Breaking CultureMoviesJames Bond Robert Pattinson cast as next James Bond Jake Coyle November 17, 2026 — 2:39am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. British actor Robert Pattinson has been unveiled as the next James Bond, becoming the seventh actor to play the iconic British spy and the first since Amazon MGM took over the beloved film franchise. The naming of Pattinson comes during the longest hiatus in 007 history and ends years of rampant speculation about who would inherit the role from Daniel Craig. Robert Pattinson in a promotional image shared on the official 007 Instagram to announce his casting as the next James Bond. Instagram It comes five years after 2021’s “No Time to Die,” the first film in Bond’s 64-year history on the silver screen to conclude with the character’s death. But 007 will be reborn, yet again, in the 26th Bond film, directed by Denis Villeneuve. “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime,” Pattinson said in a statement. “... To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”



Pattinson only entered the Bond rumour mill recently after the revelation that he screen-tested for the role. Others reportedly in the mix included Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor, Jack Lowden and Nicholas Hoult. Callum Turner, Jack Lowden and Josh O’Connor were considered the top contenders for the role for months, until Pattinson emerged as a late-favourite. While producers were expected to go with a young, less-proven star, they instead opted for one of the best-known actors of his generation. Pattinson, 40, is also relatively old to begin as 007. The actor is currently in production on another iconic role in The Batman Part II. Pattinson comes in already associated with three mega-franchises in The Batman, Twilight and Harry Potter. But since his breakthrough in Twilight, Pattinson has worked largely in more independent, auteur-driven films such as Good Time with the Safdie brothers, Robert Eggers’ The Lighthouse and Bong Joon Ho’s Mickey 17. Earlier this year, he drew rave reviews for his villainous performance in Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey. Villeneuve said it was a tough choice, but the right one.



“We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007. I am overjoyed to welcome Robert Pattinson as our new James Bond. He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new. I cannot wait to begin,” the director said in a statement. The casting comes at a pivotal juncture for the franchise. In 2022, Bond’s longtime studio, MGM, was bought by Amazon for US$8.5 billion ($12.6 billion). After haggling over next steps for 007, producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson relinquished creative control of Bond in 2025. The still-untitled Bond 26 is the first Bond movie since 1962’s inaugural Dr. No in which a Broccoli didn’t handpick the super spy. Casting a new Bond fell instead to producers Amy Pascal — the former Sony Pictures chief and Spider-Man producer — and David Heyman, shepherd of Harry Potter and Paddington. Steven Knight, known for his work on Peaky Blinders and Locke was brought in to write the script. Before Craig even departed the role, rumours and odds-making persisted nearly round-the-clock on who would follow in the footsteps of Sean Connery, George Lazenby, Roger Moore, Timothy Dalton, Pierce Brosnan and Craig. Idris Elba, for one, has spent half his career deflecting 007 conjecture.



Related Article James Bond The 007 finalists are all tall, white Brits. Is this really the Bond we need now? The Bond machine has historically never slowed down. But the 26th instalment will follow the longest absence ever for Bond. Given that No Time to Die completed principal photography in 2019 (its release was delayed due to the coronavirus pandemic), the lull is even longer. Some fans are sceptical about the new Amazon-controlled chapter for Bond. Mike Hopkins, head of Prime Video and Amazon MGM Studios, has vowed to uphold the franchise’s legacy and usher in “the next phase in the legendary 007 for audiences around the world”. At stake is one of the most lucrative film series in Hollywood, based on Ian Fleming’s series of novels. The Bond movies have grossed billions in worldwide ticket sales. Although some Bond actors came to view the role as a yoke around their necks, it turned Craig into a household name. The British actor wasn’t widely known before his casting and, at the time, was derided as the first “blond Bond”. Find out the next TV, streaming series and movies to add to your must-sees. World.content:
CultureMusicGrammys Raye, Rosalía lead women-dominated Grammy nominations Maria Sherman November 17, 2026 — 2:17am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Call her a Raye of sunshine. The English singer-songwriter leads the 2027 Grammy Award nominations, the Recording Academy announced on Monday. Raye is up for 11 awards at February’s ceremony: record, song and album of the year — the first time she’s been nominated in those big categories — as well as songwriter of the year non-classical, a variety of pop categories and music video. Raye arrives at the MTV Video Music Awards in September. AP Photo/Jordan Strauss Her 11 nods also mean she has tied Beyoncé’s record at the 2025 Grammys for the most nominations in a single year by a female artist. Speaking of Bey: She continues her reign as the most-nominated artist in Grammy history, scoring her 100th nod for Morning Dew (Donk) in the R&B solo performance category.



Raye, who is riding the success of her critically acclaimed album This Music May Contain Hope, has 15 Grammy nominations across her career. She’s never won one. The cover for Rosalía’s critically acclaimed album, Lux. Spanish singer Rosalía, fresh off her album of the year win at the 27th annual Latin Grammy Awards on Thursday for her avant-garde Lux, follows Raye with nine nominations. She’s a first-time nominee in all the categories she’s up for: record, song and album of the year as well as pop solo performance, alternative music performance, alternative music album, Latin song, global music performance and music video. Following her are Miranda Lambert, Olivia Rodrigo, Phoebe Bridgers and first-time nominee Ella Langley, who are tied with seven nods each. Bruno Mars, Leon Thomas and 2026’s best new artist winner Olivia Dean have six nominations each.



In addition to Raye’s This Music May Contain Hope and Rosalía’s Lux, the album of the year category is rounded out by Bridgers’ Lost Weekend, Dean’s The Art of Loving, Langley’s Dandelion, Mars’ The Romantic, Rodrigo’s You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love and Taylor Swift’s The Life of a Showgirl. Swift’s nomination is her fifth consecutive studio album to be nominated for album of the year, something only one other artist has ever done: Kendrick Lamar. Taylor Swift has previously won 14 Grammy Awards, and is nominated in five categories in 2027. Invision Only recordings commercially released in the US between August 31, 2025, and August 28, 2026, were eligible for nominations. The final round of Grammy voting, which determines the winners, will take place between December 10 and January 7. The record of the year category is made up of Dean’s Man I Need, Langley’s Choosin’ Texas, Mars’ I Just Might, Raye’s Where Is My Husband!, Rodrigo’s The Cure, Rosalía’s Berghain featuring Björk and Yves Tumor, Swift’s The Fate of Ophelia and Tame Impala and Jennie’s Dracula.



Jennie, perhaps best known as one-fourth of the juggernaut girl group Blackpink, is also a first-time nominee at the 2027 Grammys. Last year her bandmate Rosé became the first K-pop artist to ever receive a nomination in the record of the year field for APT her megahit with Mars. Jennie’s Dracula nomination makes her the second. Tame Impala, the project of Australian musician Kevin Parker, added four nominations to his previous two Grammy wins. Alongside the record of the year nod, the viral hit Dracula is also nominated for Best Pop Duo/Group Performance. Tame Impala’s album Deadbeat is nominated for Best Dance/Electronic Album, and the track My Old Ways is nominated for Best Dance/Electronic Recording. Related Article Good Weekend The revolutionary music machine invented by an ‘audio mad scientist’ and Tame Impala frontman Tame Impala has won two consecutive Grammys in the latter category in the last two years. Song of the year — an award for a track’s songwriters, which sometimes includes the performer but not always — is made up of an almost identical list to record of the year, featuring the same song selections from Dean, Langley, Raye, Rodrigo and Rosalía. But it also includes Ariana Grande’s Hate That I Made You Love Me, Swift’s Toy Story 5 song I Knew It, I Knew You and Mars’ Risk It All.



Filmmaker and fellow Australian Baz Luhrmann is nominated for best music film for EPiC: Elvis Presley in Concert. In the best new artist category, Langley, Angine de Poitrine, Geese, Slayyyter, Sienna Spiro, Don Toliver, Remi Wolf and The Womack Sisters will go head-to-head. Country music legend Dolly Parton, who died in August, received three posthumous nominations. The 2027 Grammy Awards will be held at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles on February 7. Grammy Nominations - Key Categories



Album of the year: Lost Weekend (Phoebe Bridgers), The Art of Loving (Olivia Dean), Dandelion (Ella Langley), The Romantic (Bruno Mars), This Music May Contain Hope (Raye), You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love (Olivia Rodrigo), LUX (Rosalía), The Life of a Showgirl (Taylor Swift). Record of the year: Man I Need (Olivia Dean), Choosin’ Texas (Ella Langley), I Just Might (Bruno Mars), Where Is My Husband! (Raye), the cure (Olivia Rodrigo), Berghain (Rosalía, Björk and Yves Tumor), The Fate of Ophelia (Taylor Swift), Dracula (Tame Impala with Jennie). Song of the year (songwriter’s award): Berghain (Björk Guðmundsdóttir, Noah Goldstein, Jake Miller, Rosalía Vila Tobella and Dylan Wiggins), Choosin’ Texas (Luke Dick, Miranda Lambert, Ella Langley and Joybeth Taylor), the cure (Daniel Nigro and Olivia Rodrigo), hate that i made you love me (Ariana Grande, Max Martin and Ilya Salmanzadeh), I Knew It, I Knew You (Jack Antonoff and Taylor Swift), Man I Need (Olivia Dean, Tobias Jesso Jr. and Zach Nahome), Risk It All (Dernst Emile II, James Fauntleroy, Philip Lawrence and Bruno Mars), Where Is My Husband! Songwriter of the year: Amy Allen, Edgar Barrera, Raye, Joybeth Taylor, Theron Thomas.

World.title: Brisbane wins over visitors, but locals cool on quality of life
World.content:
NationalQueenslandCity life Brisbane wins over visitors, but locals cool on quality of life Cameron Atfield November 17, 2026 — 1:00am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month.
