Brisbane’s reputation as a destination for dining, culture and major events has enhanced, according to new research, with Queenslanders increasingly visiting the inner-city for experiences other than work. But while out-of-towners are embracing the city, Brisbane residents appear less enthusiastic than a year ago. On Tuesday, the Committee for Brisbane will release two reports – its annual economic Inner City Vitality Report and Brisbane in 2026: How Queenslanders Experience the Inner City, which explores how Queenslanders perceive and use the city. More than 70 per cent of Queenslanders have visited Brisbane’s inner-city in the past year. Rhett Hamilton The latter report, based on an Ipsos survey of 600 Queenslanders conducted in September, found concerns about housing affordability, safety and ease of navigation have tempered residents’ optimism in the lead-up to the 2032 Olympic Games.



While the city’s overall rating remained at seven out of 10, the proportion of Brisbane residents awarding the city top marks fell from 21 per cent to 13 per cent over the year. Committee for Brisbane chief executive Jen Williams. Overall satisfaction with quality of life dropped from 78 per cent to 72 per cent. The decline was most pronounced among men and people aged between 30 and 49. “As a growing and changing city, challenges are inevitable,” Committee for Brisbane chief executive Jen Williams said. “The opportunity now is to address these concerns while protecting the experiences, places and qualities that people value most, and continuing to build on what makes Brisbane distinctive and authentic.



“The story of Brisbane’s inner city is no longer simply about office towers, business activity or a destination people visit from nine to five. It is increasingly a place people choose to visit, choose to spend time in and choose to return to. Related Article Food Brisbane’s best food and drink openings of 2026 (so far) “A city that locals love will be a city the world loves.” The Brisbane in 2026 perceptions survey found 72 per cent of Queenslanders living outside Greater Brisbane had visited the inner city during the past year, with dining overtaking shopping and entertainment as the city’s biggest drawcard. Thirty-six per cent of regional Queensland respondents nominated dining as the city’s main attraction, up from 25 per cent a year earlier.



Dining was also ranked Brisbane’s strongest overall attribute, scoring 7.5 out of 10 among both Brisbane and regional respondents. Culture, atmosphere and the city’s natural environment also ranked highly. While South Bank remained the highest-rated inner-city precinct (7.2 out of 10), ratings dropped for both Kangaroo Point (down from 7.1 to 6.7) and the Victoria Park precinct (down from 7.0 to 6.4), perhaps unsurprising given it is now a construction site for the new Brisbane Stadium. Nighttime pedestrian movements along Brunswick Street have declined since 2022. Paul Harris The Inner City Vitality Report found nighttime pedestrian movements along Fortitude Valley’s Brunswick Street have declined since 2022. “This downward trend suggests a weakening of Fortitude Valley’s nighttime vitality and its role as a vibrant, active destination beyond standard business hours,” the report finds.



“Reversing this decline will be important to supporting local businesses, improving perceptions of safety and reinforcing the Valley as a diverse, genuinely 24-hour precinct.” Related Article Brisbane 2032 Olympics Floating hotels and student digs: Solving Brisbane’s 2032 bed crunch Queen Street Mall, meanwhile, experienced a record 10.2 million pedestrian movements in the first half of 2026. Williams said one of the strongest messages from the 2026 research was Brisbane’s inner city served all of Queensland. “When we invest in major cultural venues, public spaces, transport infrastructure and city-shaping projects, the benefits flow well beyond Brisbane’s boundaries,” she said.



“Regardless of where Queenslanders live, Brisbane’s inner city is increasingly where the state comes together for major events, business, culture, recreation, and access to Queensland’s leading health and tertiary education institutions.” Related Article Exclusive

Planning How closing streets to cars might be good for Brisbane businesses Housing affordability emerged as the city’s biggest weakness, with 38 per cent of respondents identifying it as the area most in need of improvement. Safety ranked second at 33 per cent, followed by ease of navigation. Affordable accommodation was Brisbane’s lowest-rated attribute, scoring just 4.9 out of 10 among residents and 5.1 among regional Queenslanders. But respondents remained broadly positive about Brisbane’s future.



Thirty-nine per cent of Brisbane residents said they expected the city would improve over the next 12 months, compared with 16 per cent who expected it to worsen. Related Article Exclusive

Brisbane 2032 Olympics The LNP is adamant Brisbane 2032 will be delivered within budget. Here’s what voters think There was broad support for hosting the 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games, with 54 per cent of Brisbane residents and 48 per cent of regional Queenslanders backing the event. Twenty-seven per cent of Brisbanites opposed the hosting of the Games, compared to 28 per cent in the rest of Queensland. “Brisbane is increasingly a city of experiences,” Williams said of the reports’ findings.



“More people are choosing to spend time in the city for what it offers, whether that’s discovering new restaurants, attending major events, enjoying our cultural institutions or simply connecting with the energy and vibrancy of city life. “What’s emerging is a city that is distinctly Brisbane. A city that embraces our subtropical lifestyle, our river, our culture and our relaxed approach to city living.” Start the day with a summary of the day’s most important and interesting stories, analysis and insights.

World.title: I had to wait 30 years for my aunty to drop this game-changing cooking hack
World.content:
Tips & adviceKnow how I had to wait 30 years for my aunty to drop this game-changing cooking hack From non-stick frying to perfect pavlovas, Sarina Kamini shares four kitchen tips that will make life easier, and tastier, in the kitchen. Sarina Kamini November 17, 2026 Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

I’d been cooking for close to three decades when my aunt casually dropped THE tip that permanently levelled up my frying prowess. Like she’d been keeping that secret tucked up in her sari, just waiting for the right moment to blow my mind. As far as my experience indicates, you can Cordon Bleu and MasterChef masterclass it all you like. But after years documenting home cooking techniques in the kitchens of India – my family’s included – the universal truth is that the smallest details at the stovetop or the kitchen bench make the biggest impact. So in the spirit of not making anyone else wait 30 years to get the gold, here are four hacks that finesses my kitchen. Turmeric mixed with salt will stop food from sticking to the pan. Alamy The secret to non-stick frying



Forget non-stick or Teflon pots and pans, and reach for the salt and turmeric powder instead. The secret to non-stick frying is as simple as a pinch of salt and turmeric powder together, added to your hot oil, before adding anything else to your pan. It’s a tip that works for any produce, used in any oil, either shallow or deep fried. (Side note: the turmeric powder will turn everything a little yellow.) Test it with your morning fried eggs. Use it as a hack when frying potatoes or frozen chips. I do it when frying paneer. You could try it with tofu. The best recipes from Australia's leading chefs straight to your inbox. Sign up The wonder here is twofold. One, the heat tension created in stainless steel or cast iron cooking pans translates to the kind of nuanced taste and — when required — bite of char that non-stick pans can’t provide. So now you can have the non-stick and still use your standard cookware. And, two, the touch of salt and turmeric is an infinitesimal savoury flavour boost to any dish without messing with its classic profile. Sarina prepares her meringue. Lauren Trickett The perfect whipping technique for your pav



This one was given to my by my maternal grandmother a long way back, in the passing over of the tradition of the making of the Christmas pav. Thank you Grandma Beryl! Other than uneven oven heat, the fastest way to kill your pavlova is to not be properly prepped for the beating of the eggs. To ensure ultimate gloss, stickiness, and external crunch to interior pillowy meringue ratio, whip your egg whites and sugar in a completely dry stainless steel bowl. Fold and turn out with only stainless steel utensils. And, as a last hack, folding through just a quarter teaspoon of green cardamom powder as the last step before baking will tone down the sugar-sweet and turn up the dial on its gooey richness. It’s seen me through every Christmas for almost 30 years without a single fail. Yes, you can char steak without grilling it. Getty Images How to char without a barbecue



This tip came courtesy of a Sicilian chef. Replacing oil with salt in your frying pan or griddle will mimic a barbecue char on your favourite cut of meat. This is a game changer for those times when you don’t want the hassle of a barbecue, if you don’t have a barbecue, or if you can never seem to cook a steak without stewing it. Replacing oil with salt serves to dry, brown and crust the protein, bringing with it that delicious char. It works beautifully with cuts of beef and with chicken thighs, ready to slice and toss into a fresh summer salad. Try it with marinated lamb tenderloin to create a pseudo souvlaki. You don’t need any special pan, and the salt will withstand high heat cooking. Prawn tarts: a delicious use of baking powder. Lauren Trickett How to fluff up your tarts My favourite go-to summer dinner of quiche and salad has received a makeover thanks to a Mumbai home cook who knows how to handle his savoury tarts. Adding a touch of baking powder to your quiche, tart or even omelette is the sure fire way to ensure a lighter, fluffier result.



In the same way that baking powder makes baked goods rise, it also makes eggs fluffy. A half teaspoon is enough to work its magic in any tart or quiche made for six to eight people. If it’s a single-serve omelette you’re making, just go for a pinch. That Mumbai cook I mentioned? Soumitra. He uses it in a traditional savoury bake. Try blitzing mixing 100 grams short-grained rice and soak for one hour. Then mix it up with 10 fresh shelled prawns, two ripe plantains, 1 very finely sliced onion, 5 teaspoons of coconut milk powder and a handful of chopped coriander. In this recipe, the banana stands in for the egg. Add the half teaspoon of baking powder, salt to taste and a few finely chopped fresh green chillies. Mix well with your hands, adding a few tablespoons of ghee to gloss and bind. Turn out into a shallow tart or quiche tin and bake at 180 degrees until a knife pushed into the centre comes out clean. Serve as a savoury afternoon tea snack. It’s the most delicious use of baking powder I’ve ever come across. World.title: Irwin and Gout headline Queensland’s Australian of the Year picks
World.content:
NationalQueenslandAustralia Day Irwin and Gout headline Queensland’s Australian of the Year picks Cameron Atfield November 16, 2026 — 9:45pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Wildlife conservationist Robert Irwin and teenage sprint sensation Gout Gout have headlined Queensland’s Australian of the Year Awards, with the son of the late Steve Irwin recognised for his conservation work and the Ipswich speedster honoured after a record-breaking rise that has made him one of the world’s most exciting young athletes. While Irwin and Gout have built international profiles, Queensland’s Senior Australian of the Year Carmel Crouch and Noel Brown, who was recognised as the state’s Local Hero, were honoured for changing lives closer to home. Robert Irwin is Queensland’s nominee for 2027 Australian of the Year, with Gout Gout in the running to be Young Australian of the Year. Composite National Australia Day Council chief executive Carrie Leeson said the achievements of the Queensland recipients were “nothing short of inspirational”. “Robert is continuing his family’s legacy and sharing their passion for conservation with a new generation, while Gout is a teenage sprint sensation breaking world records,” Leeson said.



“Carmel is helping people gain independence and dignity, while Noel provides understanding and support when it’s needed most.” Related Article Good Weekend ‘I feel like I am at my limit’: Robert Irwin on fame, DWTS and the one role that still eludes him Irwin, 22, was named 2027 Australian of the Year for Queensland in recognition of his wildlife conservation work and efforts to inspire younger generations to protect the environment. Irwin was unable to attend the awards ceremony. His mother, Terri Irwin, accepted the honour on his behalf. He has become one of Australia’s most recognisable environmental advocates, combining work at Australia Zoo with wildlife photography, television projects and international conservation efforts.



Irwin serves on the board of Wildlife Warriors, the family’s conservation charity. His photography has earned recognition from Australian Geographic and the Wildlife Photographer of the Year Awards, while his television appearances – most recently on The Graham Norton Show alongside Prince William – have helped take his conservation message to a global audience. Sprint prodigy Gout Gout was named Queensland’s Young Australian of the Year and is now in the running for the national title. The 18-year-old has emerged as one of the world’s most exciting teenage athletes. At the 2024 Australian All Schools Athletics Championships, he ran 20.04 seconds in the 200 metres, eclipsing Usain Bolt’s time at the same age. He backed that up with a breakthrough 2026 season, lowering his Australian record and setting a world junior record of 19.67 seconds after a successful European debut. Born in Ipswich to South Sudanese migrant parents, Gout first focused on football before being identified by his coach as a running prospect at age 14. He now has his sights set on the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics and Brisbane 2032.



Queensland’s Senior Australian of the Year, Carmel Crouch, has spent more than four decades helping people with disability gain skills, secure employment and live independently. Queensland’s Senior Australian of the Year for 2027, Carmel Crouch. STEPS Pathways College The 80-year-old was founding board member of STEPS Group Australia in 1989 and helped transform a small community organisation into a national provider of training, employment, disability and mental health services. Among her most notable initiatives is STEPS Pathways College, described as Australia’s only independence college of its kind, supporting students with disability and autism to build life skills and confidence. Her work has also extended to migrants, refugees and First Nations communities through a range of social enterprises and community programs.



Rounding out the Queensland nominees was Noel Brown, a specialist First Nations greeter at Cairns Hospital whose work has been credited with improving healthcare experiences for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander patients. Noel Brown is Queensland’s nomination for Local Hero. Australian of the Year awards. Brown, 65, provides cultural support and a welcoming presence for First Nations people arriving at the hospital, helping reduce anxiety and build trust in the healthcare system. Award organisers said his work demonstrated that cultural safety was as important as clinical treatment, and had set a benchmark for culturally grounded care that hospitals around the country could seek to emulate. The four Queensland nominees will now join counterparts from every state and territory for the national Australian of the Year Awards, which will be held in Canberra on January 25, 2027. World.title: Australia and UK close on deal to send record wave of British backpackers out bush
World.content:
PoliticsFederalImmigration Australia and UK close on deal to send record wave of British backpackers out bush Paul Sakkal and Natassia Chrysanthos November 17, 2026 — 3:56am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

Regional employers crying out for backpackers to fill pubs and cafes are set to win a reprieve on Tuesday, when Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke is expected to wind back a proposed crackdown on working holidaymakers. The number of backpackers, notably young Brits, has soared in recent years. They were the main target of Burke’s migration overhaul announced in September, which followed policy releases from the Coalition and One Nation aimed at tapping into public anxiety about migration. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese with his British counterpart, Andy Burnham, in September. The pair have discussed changes to working holiday visas. Dominic Lorrimer The government has been examining delaying until next year the rollout of a ballot system for backpackers seeking to extend their stay, lifting the 5000-person cap on third-year working holiday visas and imposing longer regional work requirements on visa holders. Two sources familiar with Burke’s announcement said Labor was close to an agreement with the UK to ensure the British backpackers arriving in Australia in record numbers helped fill skills shortages in the regions rather than spending all their time in the cities.



Related Article Exclusive

Immigration Labor quietly pauses working holidaymaker visas as stoush over backpackers brews Pubs, clubs and agriculture groups have campaigned against Labor’s backpacker proposals. The backlash highlights the tough trade-offs in the migration debate, where cutting historically high arrivals risks harming key sectors such as universities, health and construction depending on the visa class. Conservatives argue that Labor’s plan focuses too heavily on backpackers, urging a tougher crackdown instead on international students – a sector Labor is already squeezing. Last week, Burke said Australia must find a way to reduce the number of UK backpackers arriving and staying in the country under a free-trade deal signed by the governments of Scott Morrison and Boris Johnson in 2021. It allows British citizens to live in Australia for up to three years without specific work requirements. “We can find a way to bring that back to something more sensible and in the national interest, without jeopardising the other parts of the free-trade agreement,” Burke said.



Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has had two meetings with UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham in as many weeks. Last Thursday, the pair discussed changes to working holidaymaker visas on the sidelines of the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey. This followed a discussion with Burnham at the Commonwealth summit in the Caribbean earlier this month, which Albanese described as “very constructive”. Under the free-trade deal, Australian and British backpackers gained rights to live in each other’s countries for three years, and the visa age limit was lifted from 30 to 35. For British backpackers, there was an extra sweetener: from 2024, they no longer needed to work 88 days in Australia’s regions to stay on, a condition for all other nationalities. The move was criticised by the Nationals at the time, who warned that farmers would lose up to 10,000 workers a year.



Numbers have since surged. There were 217,827 working holidaymakers in Australia at the end of September this year, according to the latest data, which represents a record for that quarter. Of them, 51,248 were British – a figure that has doubled since two years ago, shortly after the regional work requirement was scrapped. The visa stream for British backpackers is also uncapped, meaning there is no upward limit to how many young UK nationals can come to Australia when their job market is weaker at home. Changes to the UK scheme will seek to offset some of the worker losses that regional employers face under the government’s overall plans to drive down backpacker numbers, by making more British backpackers fill those jobs.

World.title: Robert Pattinson cast as next James Bond
World.content:
Breaking CultureMoviesJames Bond Robert Pattinson cast as next James Bond Jake Coyle November 17, 2026 — 2:39am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. British actor Robert Pattinson has been unveiled as the next James Bond, becoming the seventh actor to play the iconic British spy and the first since Amazon MGM took over the beloved film franchise. The naming of Pattinson comes during the longest hiatus in 007 history and ends years of rampant speculation about who would inherit the role from Daniel Craig. Robert Pattinson in a promotional image shared on the official 007 Instagram to announce his casting as the next James Bond. Instagram It comes five years after 2021’s “No Time to Die,” the first film in Bond’s 64-year history on the silver screen to conclude with the character’s death. But 007 will be reborn, yet again, in the 26th Bond film, directed by Denis Villeneuve. “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime,” Pattinson said in a statement. “... To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”



Pattinson only entered the Bond rumour mill recently after the revelation that he screen-tested for the role. Others reportedly in the mix included Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor, Jack Lowden and Nicholas Hoult. Callum Turner, Jack Lowden and Josh O’Connor were considered the top contenders for the role for months, until Pattinson emerged as a late-favourite. While producers were expected to go with a young, less-proven star, they instead opted for one of the best-known actors of his generation. Pattinson, 40, is also relatively old to begin as 007. The actor is currently in production on another iconic role in The Batman Part II. Pattinson comes in already associated with three mega-franchises in The Batman, Twilight and Harry Potter. But since his breakthrough in Twilight, Pattinson has worked largely in more independent, auteur-driven films such as Good Time with the Safdie brothers, Robert Eggers’ The Lighthouse and Bong Joon Ho’s Mickey 17. Earlier this year, he drew rave reviews for his villainous performance in Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey. Villeneuve said it was a tough choice, but the right one.



“We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007. I am overjoyed to welcome Robert Pattinson as our new James Bond. He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new. I cannot wait to begin,” the director said in a statement. The casting comes at a pivotal juncture for the franchise. In 2022, Bond’s longtime studio, MGM, was bought by Amazon for US$8.5 billion ($12.6 billion). After haggling over next steps for 007, producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson relinquished creative control of Bond in 2025. The still-untitled Bond 26 is the first Bond movie since 1962’s inaugural Dr. No in which a Broccoli didn’t handpick the super spy. Casting a new Bond fell instead to producers Amy Pascal — the former Sony Pictures chief and Spider-Man producer — and David Heyman, shepherd of Harry Potter and Paddington. Steven Knight, known for his work on Peaky Blinders and Locke was brought in to write the script. Before Craig even departed the role, rumours and odds-making persisted nearly round-the-clock on who would follow in the footsteps of Sean Connery, George Lazenby, Roger Moore, Timothy Dalton, Pierce Brosnan and Craig. Idris Elba, for one, has spent half his career deflecting 007 conjecture.



Related Article James Bond The 007 finalists are all tall, white Brits. Is this really the Bond we need now? The Bond machine has historically never slowed down. But the 26th instalment will follow the longest absence ever for Bond. Given that No Time to Die completed principal photography in 2019 (its release was delayed due to the coronavirus pandemic), the lull is even longer. Some fans are sceptical about the new Amazon-controlled chapter for Bond. Mike Hopkins, head of Prime Video and Amazon MGM Studios, has vowed to uphold the franchise’s legacy and usher in “the next phase in the legendary 007 for audiences around the world”. At stake is one of the most lucrative film series in Hollywood, based on Ian Fleming’s series of novels. The Bond movies have grossed billions in worldwide ticket sales. Although some Bond actors came to view the role as a yoke around their necks, it turned Craig into a household name. The British actor wasn’t widely known before his casting and, at the time, was derided as the first “blond Bond”. Find out the next TV, streaming series and movies to add to your must-sees. World.content:
CultureMusicGrammys Raye, Rosalía lead women-dominated Grammy nominations Maria Sherman November 17, 2026 — 2:17am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Call her a Raye of sunshine. The English singer-songwriter leads the 2027 Grammy Award nominations, the Recording Academy announced on Monday. Raye is up for 11 awards at February’s ceremony: record, song and album of the year — the first time she’s been nominated in those big categories — as well as songwriter of the year non-classical, a variety of pop categories and music video. Raye arrives at the MTV Video Music Awards in September. AP Photo/Jordan Strauss Her 11 nods also mean she has tied Beyoncé’s record at the 2025 Grammys for the most nominations in a single year by a female artist. Speaking of Bey: She continues her reign as the most-nominated artist in Grammy history, scoring her 100th nod for Morning Dew (Donk) in the R&B solo performance category.



Raye, who is riding the success of her critically acclaimed album This Music May Contain Hope, has 15 Grammy nominations across her career. She’s never won one. The cover for Rosalía’s critically acclaimed album, Lux. Spanish singer Rosalía, fresh off her album of the year win at the 27th annual Latin Grammy Awards on Thursday for her avant-garde Lux, follows Raye with nine nominations. She’s a first-time nominee in all the categories she’s up for: record, song and album of the year as well as pop solo performance, alternative music performance, alternative music album, Latin song, global music performance and music video. Following her are Miranda Lambert, Olivia Rodrigo, Phoebe Bridgers and first-time nominee Ella Langley, who are tied with seven nods each. Bruno Mars, Leon Thomas and 2026’s best new artist winner Olivia Dean have six nominations each.



In addition to Raye’s This Music May Contain Hope and Rosalía’s Lux, the album of the year category is rounded out by Bridgers’ Lost Weekend, Dean’s The Art of Loving, Langley’s Dandelion, Mars’ The Romantic, Rodrigo’s You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love and Taylor Swift’s The Life of a Showgirl. Swift’s nomination is her fifth consecutive studio album to be nominated for album of the year, something only one other artist has ever done: Kendrick Lamar. Taylor Swift has previously won 14 Grammy Awards, and is nominated in five categories in 2027. Invision Only recordings commercially released in the US between August 31, 2025, and August 28, 2026, were eligible for nominations. The final round of Grammy voting, which determines the winners, will take place between December 10 and January 7. The record of the year category is made up of Dean’s Man I Need, Langley’s Choosin’ Texas, Mars’ I Just Might, Raye’s Where Is My Husband!, Rodrigo’s The Cure, Rosalía’s Berghain featuring Björk and Yves Tumor, Swift’s The Fate of Ophelia and Tame Impala and Jennie’s Dracula.



Jennie, perhaps best known as one-fourth of the juggernaut girl group Blackpink, is also a first-time nominee at the 2027 Grammys. Last year her bandmate Rosé became the first K-pop artist to ever receive a nomination in the record of the year field for APT her megahit with Mars. Jennie’s Dracula nomination makes her the second. Tame Impala, the project of Australian musician Kevin Parker, added four nominations to his previous two Grammy wins. Alongside the record of the year nod, the viral hit Dracula is also nominated for Best Pop Duo/Group Performance. Tame Impala’s album Deadbeat is nominated for Best Dance/Electronic Album, and the track My Old Ways is nominated for Best Dance/Electronic Recording. Related Article Good Weekend The revolutionary music machine invented by an ‘audio mad scientist’ and Tame Impala frontman Tame Impala has won two consecutive Grammys in the latter category in the last two years. Song of the year — an award for a track’s songwriters, which sometimes includes the performer but not always — is made up of an almost identical list to record of the year, featuring the same song selections from Dean, Langley, Raye, Rodrigo and Rosalía. But it also includes Ariana Grande’s Hate That I Made You Love Me, Swift’s Toy Story 5 song I Knew It, I Knew You and Mars’ Risk It All.



Filmmaker and fellow Australian Baz Luhrmann is nominated for best music film for EPiC: Elvis Presley in Concert. In the best new artist category, Langley, Angine de Poitrine, Geese, Slayyyter, Sienna Spiro, Don Toliver, Remi Wolf and The Womack Sisters will go head-to-head. Country music legend Dolly Parton, who died in August, received three posthumous nominations. The 2027 Grammy Awards will be held at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles on February 7. Grammy Nominations - Key Categories



Album of the year: Lost Weekend (Phoebe Bridgers), The Art of Loving (Olivia Dean), Dandelion (Ella Langley), The Romantic (Bruno Mars), This Music May Contain Hope (Raye), You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love (Olivia Rodrigo), LUX (Rosalía), The Life of a Showgirl (Taylor Swift). Record of the year: Man I Need (Olivia Dean), Choosin’ Texas (Ella Langley), I Just Might (Bruno Mars), Where Is My Husband! (Raye), the cure (Olivia Rodrigo), Berghain (Rosalía, Björk and Yves Tumor), The Fate of Ophelia (Taylor Swift), Dracula (Tame Impala with Jennie). Song of the year (songwriter’s award): Berghain (Björk Guðmundsdóttir, Noah Goldstein, Jake Miller, Rosalía Vila Tobella and Dylan Wiggins), Choosin’ Texas (Luke Dick, Miranda Lambert, Ella Langley and Joybeth Taylor), the cure (Daniel Nigro and Olivia Rodrigo), hate that i made you love me (Ariana Grande, Max Martin and Ilya Salmanzadeh), I Knew It, I Knew You (Jack Antonoff and Taylor Swift), Man I Need (Olivia Dean, Tobias Jesso Jr. and Zach Nahome), Risk It All (Dernst Emile II, James Fauntleroy, Philip Lawrence and Bruno Mars), Where Is My Husband! (Rachel Keen and Mike Sabath). Best new artist: Angine de Poitrine, Geese, Ella Langley, Slayyyter, Sienna Spiro, Don Toliver, Remi Wolf, The Womack Sisters. Songwriter of the year: Amy Allen, Edgar Barrera, Raye, Joybeth Taylor, Theron Thomas.



Best pop solo performance: Man I Need (Olivia Dean), Risk It All (Bruno Mars), Where Is My Husband! (Raye), the cure (Olivia Rodrigo), Sauvignon Blanc (Rosalía). Best pop duo/group performance: Runway (Lady Gaga and Doechii), Bring Your Love (Madonna and Sabrina Carpenter), Click Clack Symphony (Raye featuring Hans Zimmer), The Life of a Showgirl (Taylor Swift and Sabrina Carpenter), Dracula (Tame Impala with Jennie). Best rap performance: Good Flirts (Baby Keem featuring Kendrick Lamar and Momo Boyd), Errtime (Cardi B), Run It Back!! (De La Soul featuring Nas), Let ’Em Know (T.I.), Body (Don Toliver). Best pop vocal album: The Art of Loving (Olivia Dean), petal (Ariana Grande), The Romantic, (Bruno Mars), This Music May Contain Hope (Raye), you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love (Olivia Rodrigo). Best rap album: Dillagence II (Busta Rhymes and J Dilla), Am I the Drama? (Cardi B), God Gotta Afro & Gold Hoops (Rapsody), Octane (Don Toliver), Everything Is a Lot. (Wale), Bully - Deluxe (Ye).



Best contemporary country album: Mount Pleasant (Kelsea Ballerini), Cherry Valley (Carter Faith), Dandelion (Ella Langley), Cloud 9 (Megan Moroney), Middle of Nowhere (Kacey Musgraves). World.content:
NationalQueenslandCity life Brisbane wins over visitors, but locals cool on quality of life Cameron Atfield November 17, 2026 — 1:00am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Brisbane’s reputation as a destination for dining, culture and major events has enhanced, according to new research, with Queenslanders increasingly visiting the inner-city for experiences other than work. But while out-of-towners are embracing the city, Brisbane residents appear less enthusiastic than a year ago. On Tuesday, the Committee for Brisbane will release two reports – its annual economic Inner City Vitality Report and Brisbane in 2026: How Queenslanders Experience the Inner City, which explores how Queenslanders perceive and use the city. More than 70 per cent of Queenslanders have visited Brisbane’s inner-city in the past year. Rhett Hamilton The latter report, based on an Ipsos survey of 600 Queenslanders conducted in September, found concerns about housing affordability, safety and ease of navigation have tempered residents’ optimism in the lead-up to the 2032 Olympic Games.



While the city’s overall rating remained at seven out of 10, the proportion of Brisbane residents awarding the city top marks fell from 21 per cent to 13 per cent over the year. Committee for Brisbane chief executive Jen Williams. Overall satisfaction with quality of life dropped from 78 per cent to 72 per cent. The decline was most pronounced among men and people aged between 30 and 49. “As a growing and changing city, challenges are inevitable,” Committee for Brisbane chief executive Jen Williams said. “The opportunity now is to address these concerns while protecting the experiences, places and qualities that people value most, and continuing to build on what makes Brisbane distinctive and authentic.



“The story of Brisbane’s inner city is no longer simply about office towers, business activity or a destination people visit from nine to five. It is increasingly a place people choose to visit, choose to spend time in and choose to return to. Related Article Food Brisbane’s best food and drink openings of 2026 (so far) “A city that locals love will be a city the world loves.” The Brisbane in 2026 perceptions survey found 72 per cent of Queenslanders living outside Greater Brisbane had visited the inner city during the past year, with dining overtaking shopping and entertainment as the city’s biggest drawcard. Thirty-six per cent of regional Queensland respondents nominated dining as the city’s main attraction, up from 25 per cent a year earlier.



Dining was also ranked Brisbane’s strongest overall attribute, scoring 7.5 out of 10 among both Brisbane and regional respondents. Culture, atmosphere and the city’s natural environment also ranked highly. While South Bank remained the highest-rated inner-city precinct (7.2 out of 10), ratings dropped for both Kangaroo Point (down from 7.1 to 6.7) and the Victoria Park precinct (down from 7.0 to 6.4), perhaps unsurprising given it is now a construction site for the new Brisbane Stadium. Nighttime pedestrian movements along Brunswick Street have declined since 2022. Paul Harris The Inner City Vitality Report found nighttime pedestrian movements along Fortitude Valley’s Brunswick Street have declined since 2022. “This downward trend suggests a weakening of Fortitude Valley’s nighttime vitality and its role as a vibrant, active destination beyond standard business hours,” the report finds.



“Reversing this decline will be important to supporting local businesses, improving perceptions of safety and reinforcing the Valley as a diverse, genuinely 24-hour precinct.” Related Article Brisbane 2032 Olympics Floating hotels and student digs: Solving Brisbane’s 2032 bed crunch Queen Street Mall, meanwhile, experienced a record 10.2 million pedestrian movements in the first half of 2026. Williams said one of the strongest messages from the 2026 research was Brisbane’s inner city served all of Queensland. “When we invest in major cultural venues, public spaces, transport infrastructure and city-shaping projects, the benefits flow well beyond Brisbane’s boundaries,” she said.



“Regardless of where Queenslanders live, Brisbane’s inner city is increasingly where the state comes together for major events, business, culture, recreation, and access to Queensland’s leading health and tertiary education institutions.” Related Article Exclusive

Planning How closing streets to cars might be good for Brisbane businesses Housing affordability emerged as the city’s biggest weakness, with 38 per cent of respondents identifying it as the area most in need of improvement. Safety ranked second at 33 per cent, followed by ease of navigation. Affordable accommodation was Brisbane’s lowest-rated attribute, scoring just 4.9 out of 10 among residents and 5.1 among regional Queenslanders. But respondents remained broadly positive about Brisbane’s future.



Thirty-nine per cent of Brisbane residents said they expected the city would improve over the next 12 months, compared with 16 per cent who expected it to worsen. Related Article Exclusive

Brisbane 2032 Olympics The LNP is adamant Brisbane 2032 will be delivered within budget. Here’s what voters think There was broad support for hosting the 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games, with 54 per cent of Brisbane residents and 48 per cent of regional Queenslanders backing the event. Twenty-seven per cent of Brisbanites opposed the hosting of the Games, compared to 28 per cent in the rest of Queensland. “Brisbane is increasingly a city of experiences,” Williams said of the reports’ findings.



“More people are choosing to spend time in the city for what it offers, whether that’s discovering new restaurants, attending major events, enjoying our cultural institutions or simply connecting with the energy and vibrancy of city life. “What’s emerging is a city that is distinctly Brisbane. A city that embraces our subtropical lifestyle, our river, our culture and our relaxed approach to city living.” Start the day with a summary of the day’s most important and interesting stories, analysis and insights.

World.title: I had to wait 30 years for my aunty to drop this game-changing cooking hack
World.content:
Tips & adviceKnow how I had to wait 30 years for my aunty to drop this game-changing cooking hack From non-stick frying to perfect pavlovas, Sarina Kamini shares four kitchen tips that will make life easier, and tastier, in the kitchen. Sarina Kamini November 17, 2026 Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

I’d been cooking for close to three decades when my aunt casually dropped THE tip that permanently levelled up my frying prowess. Like she’d been keeping that secret tucked up in her sari, just waiting for the right moment to blow my mind. As far as my experience indicates, you can Cordon Bleu and MasterChef masterclass it all you like. But after years documenting home cooking techniques in the kitchens of India – my family’s included – the universal truth is that the smallest details at the stovetop or the kitchen bench make the biggest impact. So in the spirit of not making anyone else wait 30 years to get the gold, here are four hacks that finesses my kitchen. Turmeric mixed with salt will stop food from sticking to the pan. Alamy The secret to non-stick frying



Forget non-stick or Teflon pots and pans, and reach for the salt and turmeric powder instead. The secret to non-stick frying is as simple as a pinch of salt and turmeric powder together, added to your hot oil, before adding anything else to your pan. It’s a tip that works for any produce, used in any oil, either shallow or deep fried. (Side note: the turmeric powder will turn everything a little yellow.) Test it with your morning fried eggs. Use it as a hack when frying potatoes or frozen chips. I do it when frying paneer. You could try it with tofu. The best recipes from Australia's leading chefs straight to your inbox. Sign up The wonder here is twofold. One, the heat tension created in stainless steel or cast iron cooking pans translates to the kind of nuanced taste and — when required — bite of char that non-stick pans can’t provide. So now you can have the non-stick and still use your standard cookware. And, two, the touch of salt and turmeric is an infinitesimal savoury flavour boost to any dish without messing with its classic profile. Sarina prepares her meringue. Lauren Trickett The perfect whipping technique for your pav



This one was given to my by my maternal grandmother a long way back, in the passing over of the tradition of the making of the Christmas pav. Thank you Grandma Beryl! Other than uneven oven heat, the fastest way to kill your pavlova is to not be properly prepped for the beating of the eggs. To ensure ultimate gloss, stickiness, and external crunch to interior pillowy meringue ratio, whip your egg whites and sugar in a completely dry stainless steel bowl. Fold and turn out with only stainless steel utensils. And, as a last hack, folding through just a quarter teaspoon of green cardamom powder as the last step before baking will tone down the sugar-sweet and turn up the dial on its gooey richness. It’s seen me through every Christmas for almost 30 years without a single fail. Yes, you can char steak without grilling it. Getty Images How to char without a barbecue



This tip came courtesy of a Sicilian chef. Replacing oil with salt in your frying pan or griddle will mimic a barbecue char on your favourite cut of meat. This is a game changer for those times when you don’t want the hassle of a barbecue, if you don’t have a barbecue, or if you can never seem to cook a steak without stewing it. Replacing oil with salt serves to dry, brown and crust the protein, bringing with it that delicious char. It works beautifully with cuts of beef and with chicken thighs, ready to slice and toss into a fresh summer salad. Try it with marinated lamb tenderloin to create a pseudo souvlaki. You don’t need any special pan, and the salt will withstand high heat cooking. Prawn tarts: a delicious use of baking powder. Lauren Trickett How to fluff up your tarts My favourite go-to summer dinner of quiche and salad has received a makeover thanks to a Mumbai home cook who knows how to handle his savoury tarts. Adding a touch of baking powder to your quiche, tart or even omelette is the sure fire way to ensure a lighter, fluffier result.



In the same way that baking powder makes baked goods rise, it also makes eggs fluffy. A half teaspoon is enough to work its magic in any tart or quiche made for six to eight people. If it’s a single-serve omelette you’re making, just go for a pinch. That Mumbai cook I mentioned? Soumitra. He uses it in a traditional savoury bake. Try blitzing mixing 100 grams short-grained rice and soak for one hour. Then mix it up with 10 fresh shelled prawns, two ripe plantains, 1 very finely sliced onion, 5 teaspoons of coconut milk powder and a handful of chopped coriander. In this recipe, the banana stands in for the egg. Add the half teaspoon of baking powder, salt to taste and a few finely chopped fresh green chillies. Mix well with your hands, adding a few tablespoons of ghee to gloss and bind. Turn out into a shallow tart or quiche tin and bake at 180 degrees until a knife pushed into the centre comes out clean. Serve as a savoury afternoon tea snack. It’s the most delicious use of baking powder I’ve ever come across. Related Article Six common curry mistakes that home cooks make – and how to fix them Related Article Four quick pickles chutneys and sauces to perk up any sanga, steak or veg

World.title: Irwin and Gout headline Queensland’s Australian of the Year picks
World.content:
NationalQueenslandAustralia Day Irwin and Gout headline Queensland’s Australian of the Year picks Cameron Atfield November 16, 2026 — 9:45pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Wildlife conservationist Robert Irwin and teenage sprint sensation Gout Gout have headlined Queensland’s Australian of the Year Awards, with the son of the late Steve Irwin recognised for his conservation work and the Ipswich speedster honoured after a record-breaking rise that has made him one of the world’s most exciting young athletes. While Irwin and Gout have built international profiles, Queensland’s Senior Australian of the Year Carmel Crouch and Noel Brown, who was recognised as the state’s Local Hero, were honoured for changing lives closer to home. Robert Irwin is Queensland’s nominee for 2027 Australian of the Year, with Gout Gout in the running to be Young Australian of the Year. Composite National Australia Day Council chief executive Carrie Leeson said the achievements of the Queensland recipients were “nothing short of inspirational”. “Robert is continuing his family’s legacy and sharing their passion for conservation with a new generation, while Gout is a teenage sprint sensation breaking world records,” Leeson said.



“Carmel is helping people gain independence and dignity, while Noel provides understanding and support when it’s needed most.” Related Article Good Weekend ‘I feel like I am at my limit’: Robert Irwin on fame, DWTS and the one role that still eludes him Irwin, 22, was named 2027 Australian of the Year for Queensland in recognition of his wildlife conservation work and efforts to inspire younger generations to protect the environment. Irwin was unable to attend the awards ceremony. His mother, Terri Irwin, accepted the honour on his behalf. He has become one of Australia’s most recognisable environmental advocates, combining work at Australia Zoo with wildlife photography, television projects and international conservation efforts.



Irwin serves on the board of Wildlife Warriors, the family’s conservation charity. His photography has earned recognition from Australian Geographic and the Wildlife Photographer of the Year Awards, while his television appearances – most recently on The Graham Norton Show alongside Prince William – have helped take his conservation message to a global audience. Sprint prodigy Gout Gout was named Queensland’s Young Australian of the Year and is now in the running for the national title. The 18-year-old has emerged as one of the world’s most exciting teenage athletes. At the 2024 Australian All Schools Athletics Championships, he ran 20.04 seconds in the 200 metres, eclipsing Usain Bolt’s time at the same age. He backed that up with a breakthrough 2026 season, lowering his Australian record and setting a world junior record of 19.67 seconds after a successful European debut. Born in Ipswich to South Sudanese migrant parents, Gout first focused on football before being identified by his coach as a running prospect at age 14. He now has his sights set on the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics and Brisbane 2032.



Queensland’s Senior Australian of the Year, Carmel Crouch, has spent more than four decades helping people with disability gain skills, secure employment and live independently. Queensland’s Senior Australian of the Year for 2027, Carmel Crouch. STEPS Pathways College The 80-year-old was founding board member of STEPS Group Australia in 1989 and helped transform a small community organisation into a national provider of training, employment, disability and mental health services. Among her most notable initiatives is STEPS Pathways College, described as Australia’s only independence college of its kind, supporting students with disability and autism to build life skills and confidence. Her work has also extended to migrants, refugees and First Nations communities through a range of social enterprises and community programs.



Rounding out the Queensland nominees was Noel Brown, a specialist First Nations greeter at Cairns Hospital whose work has been credited with improving healthcare experiences for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander patients. Noel Brown is Queensland’s nomination for Local Hero. Australian of the Year awards. Brown, 65, provides cultural support and a welcoming presence for First Nations people arriving at the hospital, helping reduce anxiety and build trust in the healthcare system. Award organisers said his work demonstrated that cultural safety was as important as clinical treatment, and had set a benchmark for culturally grounded care that hospitals around the country could seek to emulate. The four Queensland nominees will now join counterparts from every state and territory for the national Australian of the Year Awards, which will be held in Canberra on January 25, 2027. World.title: 'Not credible' for RNZ board to have missed financial blunders, Shane Jones says
World.content:
Associate Finance Minister Shane Jones says RNZ is in decay and it's not credible that the board was not aware of its financial blunders.

The public broadcaster last week revealed a shock $12 million budget blowout, which is more than 25 times the $470,000 it had expected to lose over the year to June.

RNZ chief financial officer Hilary Parker resigned unexpectedly in early October, and chief executive Paul Thompson - who was due to leave on 31 December - has departed six weeks early.

The organisation has commissioned an independent review of what went wrong and has indicated 58 jobs would have to go, which is double the number it had signalled in August as a response to funding cuts.

Board chair Brent Impey said the board and senior managers only learnt the full scale of the loss in mid-October.

Jones stressed the caretaker government was not across all the details.

"But know this from me ... when you see an enterprise where the cash has gone from $23 million down to $8 million in about two years, the costs have not been trimmed to meet the reduction in revenue, then you have an organisation in decay," he said.

"It is just not credible for people of governance merit to have missed such a rapid reduction in cash, and possibly believing that they would make up for the shortfall by selling assets when they know that those assets and the returns are expected by Treasury to come back to the [government]."

The broadcaster ended June with $8.5 million in cash, down from $18.8 million a year earlier and $23.5m the year before that.

RNZ chief executive Paul Thompson (R) is questioned about the budget blowout by Checkpoint host Lisa Owen. RNZ / Nick Monro

Jones said board members were pointing the finger and using "hysterical" language in the media, such as saying the situation is incomprehensible.

"Incomprehensible to who? That's why you have a board, that's why you have an audit committee," he said.

"You put people with experience that you can trust, and I just feel that someone in that organisation has flipped the bird to the taxpayer, and I'm very worried that the right people are held accountable."

The independent review was too little, too late, Jones said.

"This is a major financial blow to a flagship organisation in New Zealand, and I'm sorry, I'm just not going to tolerate all this theatrical performative nonsense that no one knew what was happening. It's just not credible."

Jones said the next government would make decisions on the future of the board once it had all the necessary information from the independent review RNZ had commissioned.

"A future government has to deal with that issue on the basis of facts and on the basis of whether or not the current stewardship is sustainable."

RNZ did not respond specifically to Jones' criticisms.

In a statement, a spokesperson said: "RNZ accepts responsibility as an organisation for this result."

World.title: Hundreds of parcels containing suspected illegal peptides seized at border
World.content:
Ministry of Health data shows the number of parcels containing suspected illegal peptides intercepted at the border has soared.

Figures for the first six months of this year have already exceeded the number for the whole of 2025.

Ministry of Health figures show 398 parcels containing peptide products, suspected peptides or selective androgen receptor modulators (SARMs) were intercepted in the six months to June.

That's compared with 370 during all of 2025, about 100 in 2024, about 18 in 2023, and about 15 in 2022.

A spokesperson for Medsafe, part of the Ministry of Health, explained it was unlawful to sell any peptides for a therapeutic purpose in New Zealand, unless by a person licensed or otherwise authorised under the Medicines Act.

Peptide products identified at the border were held and investigated. If they were imported without a prescription or not clearly labelled - including products identified only by codes - they were destroyed.

What are peptides, anyway?

Health NZ spokesperson Bronwyn Petrie told Morning Report: "Peptides are small substances made naturally in the body that act as signals, helping to regulate things like growth, healing, hormones and our metabolism."

Unregulated peptides seized by Medsafe. Supplied / Medsafe

Not all peptides were illegal or unsafe, and some approved medicines were peptide-based - such as Wegovy. Authorities were concerned about unapproved products sold online without the quality controls applied to approved medicines.

"I don't think we know the size and scale of the unapproved peptides in New Zealand, but what we do know is that internationally and here in New Zealand, there has been a huge spike in people injecting peptides," she said in October.

Unapproved peptides were being promoted "widely" on social media, she said, with claims they could slow ageing and help with muscle-building and losing weight.

A Medsafe spokesperson cautioned against using unapproved peptides as there was no assurance the products were safe, effective or free from contamination.

It was particularly risky to inject peptides, they said.

Health NZ had begun supplying peptide-injecting kits as part of its needle exchange programme to promote safe use, with 2300 peptide injection kits distributed to 190 pharmacies in the programme's first six weeks.

Since it published a safety alert in May, Medsafe had received seven reports of adverse reactions potentially linked to peptides.

Five of the seven reports potentially involved products patients believed contained retatrutide, an experimental weight-loss drug.

Australia's Therapeutic Goods Administration recently published a statement after identifying serious adverse effects linked to the use of unapproved peptides in its hospitalisation data, including liver damage and severe allergic reactions requiring hospitalisation.

World.title: Will political uncertainty affect next OCR call?
World.content:
Audio player for " What's the biggest risk to our economy right now? " removed for printing Visit page to play audio: https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9._v0.KrRTFtoPsaA8nSDloPZ4KejQJr59ANQpD9ULgGwzaM0/business/2633255%2Fwill-political-uncertainty-affect-next-ocr-call

Will New Zealand not yet having a new government affect the Reserve Bank's next official cash rate (OCR) decision?

The Reserve Bank is due to review the OCR at the start of next month, in the last update for the year.

But economists say whether or not there is a new government in place by then is unlikely to make much difference.

Westpac chief economist Kelly Eckhold said even if it were possible to announce this week what the next coalition would be, it would not be until the first Budget was released that anyone could quantify what impact that would have on the economy.

Kelly Eckhold. Supplied / Westpac

He said a Labour-led government was likely to change the Reserve Bank's mandate so that it had to give consideration to the unemployment rate when setting the OCR. "That is probably something a bit more concrete, if the Reserve Bank knew that was coming then perhaps at least some MPC [Monetary Policy Committee] members might be having a bit more of a debate about trading off the time it takes for inflation to get to 2 percent versus where they think the unemployment rate is going to track.

"But I'm doubtful that even if that discussion was occurring in the December meeting whether you'd really see it because the mandate itself wouldn't have changed at this stage."

He said in general the lack of a political decision was likely to have limited impact on economic activity. "The tendency is for this not to matter that much because businesses and consumers just get on with doing what they're doing … I'm not really feeling that the economy is sitting there doing nothing because of the outcome of the election. My sense of a lot of business clients is they've tended to take the preliminary results at face value and think that will stand once we get through the process."

Brad Olsen. RNZ / Samuel Rillstone

Infometrics principal economist Brad Olsen agreed the political machinations were unlikely to have an impact on the Reserve Bank's decision-making. International markets, fuel prices and the labour market were more important factors, he said.

"Once they put out a mini budget or some sort of financial thing and appoint a finance minister … it would still take quite a bit of time for whatever changes came through from a government point of view to influences finances. Policies take time to emerge. Legislation takes time to be put through the house.

"What the Reserve Bank does do is when the Budget comes out in May, they always incorporate that information into their expectations."

Simplicity chief economist Shamubeel Eaqub said the Reserve Bank was expecting economic growth to come from a recovery in private sector investments rather than household or government in 2027.

Miles Workman. Supplied / ANZ

ANZ senior economist Miles Workman agreed the outcome would not make a significant difference even when it was known.

"Despite the major parties having different policy priorities, both National and Labour campaigned on similar fiscal strategies, committing to the same operating and capital allowances for upcoming Budgets. So, assuming one of the major parties ends up leading the next government (and the next government sticks to these allowances), the high-level fiscal outlook is unlikely to change materially, even if the mix of tax and spending does."

World.title: Punch-up between staff member and young person at youth justice facility
World.content:
A punch-up between a staff member and a young person took place in a youth justice facility in September, RNZ can reveal.

It comes a year after a "reset plan" was undertaken at the facility - Korowai Manaaki - to lift standards.

Official documents seen by RNZ show a staff member antagonised a rangatahi (young person) during a table tennis game, making a hand gesture indicating they were breaking something across their knee.

This was taken to mean his head, and he then challenged the staff member to a fight.

They unlocked the door to the courtyard where the pair were then seen "adjusting their stance and raising their fists in what appeared to be preparation for a physical altercation".

They then exchanged blows before another staff member intervened and stopped the altercation.

When the pair stopped fighting they were then seen shaking hands and hugging each other. The staff member sustained a bloody nose, which was possibly broken.

The staff member was escorted offsite, access was removed and official documents stated they would not return.

The young person later said he was surprised the staff member had followed through and did not expect it.

Police attended the incident at the time, and had photographed the injuries.

Acting Detective Inspector Martin Bienvenu, Counties Manukau CIB told RNZ enquiries were underway following the report of an alleged assault "to understand the full circumstances surrounding the incident".

Labour's spokesperson for children Willow-Jean Prime said it was "yet another harmful incident" at the same facility.

Labour's spokesperson for children Willow-Jean Prime. VNP / Phil Smith

The incident occured the same month RNZ revealed staff were present during the assault of a young person by his peers in a ritual attack known as 'walking the line' at Korowai Manaaki earlier this year.

"We need clear answers about how staff are being trained to de-escalate situations and why incidents involving staff continue to occur," Prime told RNZ .

Minister for Children Karen Chhour wouldn't comment on the employment issue, given it was operational.

Korowai Manaaki is seen as a "challenging residence" partly due to the cohort of young people it has, according to Oranga Tamariki (OT)'s head of youth justice and residential care Dean Winter.

Official documents also showed - like other residences - it was seeing increasing complex needs and behaviours, more serious offending behaviours, and a higher proportion being sentenced to longer periods on remand by the youth courts.

Chhour has consistently pointed to training undergone to make improvements across youth justice, part of that was a specific reset for Korowai Manaaki.

RNZ asked Chhour whether the training and developing of Youth Justice (YJ) residence staff was working as she hoped.

Chhour said the improved training programme was an important step towards better practice, "but I acknowledge that it will take time to embed".

"This training is just one part of Oranga Tamariki's efforts to fix long-standing issues stemming from a previous lack of standard operating procedures and adequate training at these facilities.

"I am confident that once these efforts are fully implemented, they will significantly improve the safety of young people and staff."

Minister for Children Karen Chhour. RNZ / Nate McKinnon

12 week reset plan

Korowai Manaaki is the largest YJ facililty in New Zealand, providing care for up to 42 young people aged 14-19.

OT said it had "unique challenges" as a residence, and external reviews and observations by leaders had identified consistent themes which needed to be addressed, "namely leadership visibility, culture and practice, and improved security and safety provisions".

Poor standards in secure care had also been noted - these were units where young people were placed for short periods if they were likely to cause harm to themselves or others.

In Budget 2025, $40 million was allocated over four years to the professionalisation of the workforce, with the money held in contingency. RNZ has requested the amount spent so far on training.

In March, Chhour told Prime in a written parliamentary question she had been advised by Oranga Tamariki performance at Korowai Manaki was being monitored on an ongoing basis following the reset plan. She said positive changes included improved staff engagement, strengthened processes and improvement to infrastructure.

RNZ requested information about the reset plan itself, which took place in late 2025.

The "intensive intervention" was designed to "stabilise operations, strengthen capability, and lay the foundation for lasting cultural change".

Official documents from Oranga Tamariki showed the main risk of the plan was that "change will not embed".

Police attended the incident and photographed the injuries (file photo). RNZ/Peter de Graaf

Over 750 training sessions and assessments were completed, across modules including professional standards and workplace integrity, standard operating procedures, secure care essentials and leadership training.

At the completion of the reset, OT acknowledged some harm was still occuring on site, but practice in managing complex dynamics and reducing risk of violence had improved.

A post reset report from December noted staff had raised frustrations with management and policy consistency, staffing gaps, low morale and a desire for more recognition through pay and rewards, safety and voice.

In June this year, Chhour was asked by Prime whether she was satisfied with the management of Korowai Manaaki, to which she said "absolutely".

Chhour added there'd been a decrease in incidents occuring under her watch.

"I'm absolutely proud of the work they've done.

World.title: Tropical Cyclone Xavier to bring damaging winds to Northern Cook Islands
World.content:
A storm warning is in place for parts of Northern Cook Islands due to Tropical Cyclone Xavier.

The storm intensified into a category 1 cyclone on Sunday evening, before it was upgraded to a category 2 on Monday night.

The Cook Islands Meteorological Service has issued a tropical cyclone alert for Pukapuka and Nassau.

It says a storm warning remains in place for Manihiki and Rakahanga, which could see damaging gale-force winds up to 85km/h with wind gusts of up to 120km/h.

These were set to increase to 95km/h with gusts up to 130km/h on Monday night.

Heavy rain and thunderstorms are also forecast.

The metservice is advising people to secure lose items around their homes and properties and for fishermen to avoid going out to the sea if conditions are unsafe.

Tropical Cyclone Xavier is gradually moving westward within the Northern Cook Islands.

World.title: Staggered age of consent becomes 'difficult' with smaller age gaps - chief victims advisor
World.content:
It is worth having a conversation about a staggered age of consent for sex, says the chief victims advisor, but she also warns that there could be serious challenges in enforcing it.

The UK government is investigating a law change that could make sex between a much older adult and a teenager between 16 and 18 illegal - after recent cases where young women who legally were able to consent were allegedly groomed by much older men.

Media personality Russell Brand has been jailed for more than 10 years for serious sexual offences. A woman who alleges she was raped by Brand when she was 16 and he was 30, is now campaigning for a staggered age of consent.

British comedian and author David Walliams is also facing allegations he groomed teenagers as young as 15, but did not have sex with them until they were older.

Audio player for " Does NZ need to consider a staggered age of consent? " removed for printing Visit page to play audio: https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9._v0.KrRTFtoPsaA8nSDloPZ4KejQJr59ANQpD9ULgGwzaM0/crime-and-justice/2631607%2Fstaggered-age-of-consent-becomes-difficult-with-smaller-age-gaps-chief-victims-advisor

Does NZ need to consider a staggered age of consent? Checkpoint Download MP3 7m

In New Zealand, the National Party has promised it would review consent laws and chief victims advisor Ruth Money told Checkpoint that staggered age issues should be part of the conversation.

"It's a good conversation to have and it's certainly good timing when we do have a government to put it as part of that consent review that is going to happen."

But she said overseas experiences have shown there would be some operational challenges.

"If we look at Canada, for example, there is a five year difference, so they have criminalised sexual activity if your partner is five years or more older. I think it's difficult - is it five years, is it seven years? Obviously at the extremes, if I'm 13 and the person is 60, we could ask some questions about grooming and influence. But at the smaller margins it becomes quite difficult for the courts to operationalise, in terms of how can can you prove intent, was the age gap big enough, was there coercion, it becomes difficult."

She said it was such a complex issue and the important thing was to educate the public.

"So what does grooming and coercion look like, what does manipulation look like?"

Money said there were also major issues with NDAs being used to mask sexual misconduct, and there needed to be a wholesale review of consent laws in New Zealand.

"Yes, I will be working with the incoming government to do such a thing."
